items.label: Strong Wolfe counterexample with sharp Hölder regularity
items.statement:
thm:main and eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: in every dimension at least
two, the same strong-Wolfe counterexample has a globally one-half Hölder
Hessian and admits no larger exponent even on its initial sublevel.
items.title: Strong Wolfe counterexample with sharp Hölder regularity

items.label: Identity initialization with Hölder regularity
items.statement:
cor:identity-initialization: identity-initialized classical DFP fails to
converge in every dimension at least two even with a global one-half Hölder
Hessian and positive ordered uniform Hessian bounds.
items.title: Identity initialization with Hölder regularity

items.label: Planar convergence: weak Wolfe
items.statement:
Paper-facing form of thm:planar-convergence: arbitrary initial
positive-definite planar DFP data converge under the full fixed weak-Wolfe
range when the globally strongly convex C2 objective has locally Lipschitz
Hessian near its initial sublevel. Stationary termination is included through
constant continuation of the point sequence.
items.title: Planar convergence: weak Wolfe

items.label: Planar convergence: strong Wolfe
items.statement:
Paper-facing strong-Wolfe consequence of thm:planar-convergence:
strong curvature implies weak curvature after the descent property is
derived from Armijo and strong convexity.
items.title: Planar convergence: strong Wolfe

items.label: General secant degeneration
items.statement:
lem:planar-degeneration: positive-definite secant search matrices under
weak Wolfe degenerate along every nonconvergent planar strongly convex orbit.
The free coefficient is positive and bounded by adjacent step products, the
matrix sequence is bounded, and its smallest eigenvalue tends to zero.
items.title: General secant degeneration

items.label: Failure of global weak-Wolfe convergence
items.statement:
TASK-11 Main theorem: for every pair in the paper's Wolfe range, the
global weak-Wolfe convergence predicate is false.
items.title: Failure of global weak-Wolfe convergence

items.label: Failure of level-set global weak-Wolfe convergence
items.statement:
TASK-15: The same paper-range counterexample refutes the level-set version
of the fixed-coefficient global-convergence predicate.  The explicit
containment field is supplied by the Armijo/DFP descent bridge.
items.title: Failure of level-set global weak-Wolfe convergence

items.label: Strong Wolfe counterexample in every dimension
items.statement:
TASK-11: The paper-range strong-Wolfe counterexample is available in every
finite dimension `n` with `2 ≤ n`, while retaining the exact Hessian bounds
`(1 / 2, 3 / 2)`.
items.title: Strong Wolfe counterexample in every dimension

items.label: Identity-initialized strong Wolfe counterexample
items.statement:
TASK-15: For every pair in the paper's coefficient range and every
dimension `n ≥ 2`, the identity-initialization corollary has a genuine
matrix `InverseIteration` presentation.  The positive ordered Hessian bounds
and the `liminf` conclusion are generated automatically from the initial
positive-definite matrix.
items.title: Identity-initialized strong Wolfe counterexample

items.label: ofParabolicRecurrence
items.statement:
A positive real sequence tending to zero and satisfying
`ε (j + 1) = ε j - a * ε j ^ (p + 1) + O(ε j ^ (p + 2))` is asymptotic to
`(a * (p : ℝ) * (j : ℝ)) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))` when `a > 0` and
`p` is a positive natural number.
items.title: ofParabolicRecurrence

items.label: ofQuadraticRecurrence
items.statement:
A positive sequence tending to zero whose quadratic-recurrence residual
`ε (j + 1) - ε j + a * ε j ^ 2` is `O(ε j ^ 3)` is asymptotic to
the explicit reciprocal scale `(a * (j : ℝ))⁻¹`.
items.title: ofQuadraticRecurrence

items.label: ofQuarticRecurrence
items.statement:
A positive sequence tending to zero whose quartic-recurrence residual
`ε (j + 1) - ε j + a * ε j ^ 4` is `O(ε j ^ 5)` is asymptotic to
the parabolic scale `(3 * a * (j : ℝ)) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 3)`.
items.title: ofQuarticRecurrence

items.label: summable_rpow_iff
items.statement:
If `ε j` is asymptotic to `C * j ^ (-1 / p)` for positive `C` and `p`,
then the sequence `ε j ^ q` is summable exactly when `p < q`.
items.title: summable_rpow_iff

items.label: tail_rpow_isBigO
items.statement:
Under the same power-scale asymptotic hypotheses, the shifted `q`-power tail is
`O(j ^ (1 - q / p))` whenever `p < q`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isBigO

items.label: tail_rpow_isBigO_self
items.statement:
Under the same power-scale asymptotic hypotheses, the shifted `q`-power tail is
`O(ε j ^ (q - p))` whenever `p < q`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isBigO_self

items.label: tail_rpow_isEquivalent
items.statement:
If `ε j` is asymptotic to `C * j ^ (-1 / p)` for positive `C` and `p`, then
for `p < q` its shifted `q`-power tail has sharp asymptotic coefficient
`C ^ q * (p / (q - p))`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isEquivalent

items.label: tail_rpow_isEquivalent_self
items.statement:
If `ε j` is asymptotic to `C * j ^ (-1 / p)` for positive `C` and `p`, then
for `p < q` its shifted `q`-power tail is asymptotic to
`C ^ p * (p / (q - p)) * ε j ^ (q - p)`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isEquivalent_self

items.label: tsum_nat_add
items.statement:

items.title: tsum_nat_add

items.label: frame_col_one
items.statement: The second column of the frame is the positively oriented perpendicular direction.

items.label: ofSpectral_amplitude

The amplitude projection of a spectrally recovered state is its low oriented gradient
coordinate.

items.label: ofSpectral_gradient
items.statement:
A spectrally recovered state has the prescribed positive oriented gradient coordinates in
its frame.
items.title: ofSpectral_gradient

items.label: ofSpectral_h
items.statement: The high-metric projection of a spectrally recovered state is its high spectral value.
items.title: ofSpectral_h

items.label: ofSpectral_metric

items.title: ofSpectral_metric

items.title: ofSpectral_p

items.label: ofSpectral_r

items.title: ofSpectral_r

items.label: ofSpectral_spec
items.statement:
Spectral recovery produces positive canonical parameters with the prescribed projections,
metric spectrum, and oriented gradient coordinates.
items.title: ofSpectral_spec

items.label: perp_eq
items.statement: The perpendicular direction has the prescribed coordinate formula.
items.title: perp_eq

items.label: recoveryHigh_mul_shape_mul_radius_sq
items.statement:
The high spectral value times the recovered shape and squared radius is the low spectral
value.
items.title: recoveryHigh_mul_shape_mul_radius_sq

items.label: recoveryRadius_pos
items.statement:
The recovered radius is positive for positive ordered spectral values and positive oriented
gradient coordinates.

The product of the recovered shape and radius is the ratio of the oriented gradient
coordinates.

The recovered shape is positive for positive ordered spectral values and positive oriented
gradient coordinates.

items.label: recovery_iff
items.statement:
Positive canonical parameters satisfy the spectral and oriented-gradient coordinate
equations exactly when they are given by the recovery formulas.

items.label: spec

items.title: spec

items.label: dfpDenominators_ne_zero
items.statement:
Both scalar denominators in the inverse-form DFP update of an abstract secant step
are nonzero.
items.title: dfpDenominators_ne_zero

items.label: displacement_def

items.title: displacement_def

items.label: displacement_ne_zero

items.title: displacement_ne_zero

items.label: gradientChangeEnergy_pos
items.statement:

matrix.
items.title: gradientChangeEnergy_pos

items.statement: The gradient change is the abstract secant matrix applied to the displacement.
items.title: gradientChange_def

items.label: gradientChange_ne_zero
items.statement: The gradient change produced by an abstract secant step is nonzero.
items.title: gradientChange_ne_zero

items.label: gradientEnergy_pos
items.statement: The gradient has strictly positive energy with respect to the inverse-Hessian matrix.
items.title: gradientEnergy_pos

items.label: lineRatio
items.statement: The constructed secant curvature has the prescribed ratio to predicted decrease.
items.title: lineRatio

items.label: nextGradient_def
items.statement: The next gradient is the current gradient plus the secant change.
items.title: nextGradient_def

items.label: nextGradient_eigenframe
items.statement:
In a two-dimensional diagonal eigenframe, the next gradient is obtained
from the coordinate formulas for the preconditioned gradient and its secant image.
items.title: nextGradient_eigenframe

items.label: nextGradient_formula
items.statement:
Writing `v = H *ᵥ g`, `δ = g ⬝ᵥ v`, `w = A *ᵥ v`, and `β = v ⬝ᵥ w`,
the next gradient is `g - (τ * δ / β) • w`.
items.title: nextGradient_formula

items.label: nextGradient_pairing_eq
items.statement:
The next-gradient pairing of an abstract secant step is
`-(1 - τ)` times its predicted decrease.
items.title: nextGradient_pairing_eq

items.label: nextGradient_pairing_eq_add_secantCurvature
items.statement:
The next-gradient pairing equals the initial-gradient pairing plus the
secant curvature.
items.title: nextGradient_pairing_eq_add_secantCurvature

items.label: nextInverseHessian_def
items.statement: The next inverse-Hessian approximation is the inverse-form DFP update.
items.title: nextInverseHessian_def

items.label: nextInverseHessian_eigenframe
items.statement:
In a two-dimensional diagonal eigenframe, the next inverse-Hessian has the
displayed symmetric entrywise formula.
items.title: nextInverseHessian_eigenframe

items.label: nextInverseHessian_formula
items.statement:
Writing `v = Hg`, `w = Av`, `β = vᵀw`, and `γ = wᵀHw`, the next
inverse-Hessian matrix has the exact rank-two DFP formula.
items.title: nextInverseHessian_formula

items.label: nextInverseHessian_posDef
items.statement: The inverse-form DFP update of an abstract secant step remains positive definite.
items.title: nextInverseHessian_posDef

items.label: nextInverseHessian_tau_independent
items.statement:
Abstract secant steps with the same inverse Hessian, gradient, and secant
matrix have the same next inverse-Hessian matrix, independently of their positive scales.
items.title: nextInverseHessian_tau_independent

items.label: nextSlope_def
items.statement: The next slope is the next-gradient-displacement pairing.
items.title: nextSlope_def

items.label: nextSlope_eq
items.statement: The next slope is `(1 - τ)` times the initial slope.
items.title: nextSlope_eq

items.label: nextSlope_eq_add_secantCurvature
items.statement: The next slope is the initial slope plus the secant curvature.
items.title: nextSlope_eq_add_secantCurvature

items.label: phaseStepRatio_deviation_le
items.statement:
For a phase-controlled abstract step, the squared-step-to-decrease ratio
differs from the prescribed phase ratio by the phase quadratic-form defect.
items.title: phaseStepRatio_deviation_le

items.label: preconditionedEnergy_pos
items.statement:
The preconditioned gradient has strictly positive energy with respect to the secant
matrix.
items.title: preconditionedEnergy_pos

items.label: preconditionedGradient_def
items.statement: The preconditioned gradient is obtained by multiplying the gradient by `H`.
items.title: preconditionedGradient_def

items.label: preconditionedGradient_ne_zero
items.statement: The preconditioned gradient of an abstract secant step is nonzero.
items.title: preconditionedGradient_ne_zero

items.label: predictedDecrease_def
items.statement: The predicted decrease is the negative gradient-displacement pairing.
items.title: predictedDecrease_def

items.label: predictedDecrease_eq_stepLength_mul_gradientEnergy
items.statement:
The predicted decrease is the step length times the inverse-Hessian energy of the
gradient.
items.title: predictedDecrease_eq_stepLength_mul_gradientEnergy

items.label: predictedDecrease_mem_Icc_of_phase
items.statement:
An abstract secant step whose matrix and line ratio are one of the two
prescribed phase controls has predicted decrease uniformly comparable to the
squared Euclidean displacement norm.
items.title: predictedDecrease_mem_Icc_of_phase

items.label: predictedDecrease_pos
items.statement: The abstract secant step has positive predicted decrease.
items.title: predictedDecrease_pos

items.label: recurrences_of_orthogonalTransport
items.statement:
Coordinate identifications with one orthogonally transported abstract
secant step imply the physical point and inverse-Hessian DFP recurrences.
items.title: recurrences_of_orthogonalTransport

items.label: secantCurvature_def
items.statement: The secant curvature is the displacement-gradient-change pairing.
items.title: secantCurvature_def

items.label: secantCurvature_eq_stepLength_sq_mul_preconditionedEnergy
items.statement:
The secant curvature is the squared step length times the secant-matrix energy of
the preconditioned gradient.
items.title: secantCurvature_eq_stepLength_sq_mul_preconditionedEnergy

items.label: secantCurvature_eq_tau_mul_predictedDecrease
items.statement: The secant curvature is `tau` times the predicted decrease.
items.title: secantCurvature_eq_tau_mul_predictedDecrease

items.label: secantCurvature_pos
items.statement: The abstract secant pair has positive curvature.
items.title: secantCurvature_pos

items.label: secantImageEnergy_pos
items.statement:
The secant image of the preconditioned gradient has strictly positive energy with
respect to the inverse-Hessian matrix.
items.title: secantImageEnergy_pos

items.label: slope_def
items.statement: The initial slope is the gradient-displacement pairing.
items.title: slope_def

items.label: slope_eq_neg_predictedDecrease
items.statement: The initial slope is the negative predicted decrease.
items.title: slope_eq_neg_predictedDecrease

items.label: stepLengthDenominator_ne_zero
items.statement:
The preconditioned-gradient energy occurring in the step-length denominator is
nonzero.
items.title: stepLengthDenominator_ne_zero

items.label: stepLength_def

items.title: stepLength_def

items.label: stepLength_pos

items.title: stepLength_pos

items.label: strongCurvature

items.title: strongCurvature

items.label: strongCurvature_of_tau_values
items.statement:
A secant step whose line ratio is `1 / 3` or `2 / 3` satisfies strong curvature for every
coefficient at least `2 / 3`.
items.title: strongCurvature_of_tau_values

items.label: transportedDisplacement_eq_step
items.statement:
Transporting an abstract displacement by an orthogonal frame gives the
physical inverse-Hessian search step for the conjugated metric and transported
gradient.
items.title: transportedDisplacement_eq_step

items.label: transportedGradientChange
items.statement:
Transporting the difference of the next and current gradients gives the
transport of the abstract gradient change.
items.title: transportedGradientChange

items.label: weakCurvature
items.statement: A lower bound on `τ` gives the weak-Wolfe scalar curvature condition.
items.title: weakCurvature

items.label: weakCurvature_of_tau_lower_bound
items.statement:
A lower bound `1 - c₂ ≤ τ` gives the weak-curvature inequality for an
abstract secant step.
items.title: weakCurvature_of_tau_lower_bound

items.label: canonicalFactorization
items.statement:
Locally at `(0, 2, 1)` away from `ε = 0`, canonical recovery yields radius
`ε ^ 2 * ℛ₁` and shape `p₁`.
items.title: canonicalFactorization

items.label: coordinates_analyticAt
items.statement:
The complete pair of first-leg gradient coordinates in the canonical frame is real analytic
at the common base point.
items.title: coordinates_analyticAt

items.label: coordinates_contDiffAt
items.statement: The first-leg coordinate pair is `C^k` at the common base point for every order `k`.
items.title: coordinates_contDiffAt

items.label: coordinates_continuousAt
items.statement:
The complete pair of first-leg gradient coordinates in the canonical frame
is continuous at the common zero-scale base point.
items.title: coordinates_continuousAt

items.label: eigenvalues_eq_lowHigh
items.statement:
The first-leg eigenvalue pair is the explicit low/high spectrum of the
physical output metric.
items.title: eigenvalues_eq_lowHigh

items.label: factorsAnalytic
items.statement: All six removable first-leg factors are jointly real analytic at `(0, 2, 1)`.
items.title: factorsAnalytic

items.label: factorsBase
items.statement:
The first-leg spectral, gradient, radius, and shape factors have base values
`(2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1 / 2)`.
items.title: factorsBase

items.label: factors_apply
items.statement:
The combined first-leg factor package exposes its spectral, gradient, and
canonical components.
items.title: factors_apply

items.label: frameDiagonalization
items.statement:
Locally at `(0, 2, 1)`, the first-leg eigenframe diagonalizes the updated metric
with diagonal entries `ε ^ 4 * L₁` and `ℋ₁`.
items.title: frameDiagonalization

items.label: frameDiagonalization_of_ne
items.statement:
Under the two nonvanishing factor hypotheses, the fixed first-leg frame
diagonalizes the updated metric pointwise.
items.title: frameDiagonalization_of_ne

items.label: frameEntry_analyticAt
items.statement:
Every entry of the canonical first-leg eigenframe is real analytic at the common base
point.
items.title: frameEntry_analyticAt

items.label: frameEntry_continuousAt
items.statement:
Every entry of the canonical first-leg eigenframe is continuous at the
common zero-scale base point.
items.title: frameEntry_continuousAt

items.label: frameOriented
items.statement:
Near the base point, the fixed analytic low eigenvector is already oriented toward
the first updated gradient.
items.title: frameOriented

items.label: frame_eq_lowEigenframe
items.statement:
The first-leg frame is the canonical low-eigenvector frame of the physical
output metric.
items.title: frame_eq_lowEigenframe

items.label: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup
items.statement:
If the low gradient coordinate is nonzero, the fixed first-leg eigenframe
is a positively oriented orthogonal frame.
items.title: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.label: frame_transpose_mulVec_outputGradient
items.statement:
In the oriented first-leg eigenframe, the updated gradient has the exact
factored coordinates `G • ![𝒢₁, ε ^ 2 * U₁]` for every parameter triple
and amplitude.
items.title: frame_transpose_mulVec_outputGradient

items.label: gradientFactorization
items.statement:
Locally at `(0, 2, 1)`, the oriented first updated gradient coordinates factor as
`G • ![𝒢₁, ε ^ 2 * U₁]` for every amplitude `G`.
items.title: gradientFactorization

items.label: gradientFactors_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the removable oriented-gradient factors of the first leg.
items.title: gradientFactors_apply

items.label: lowDenom_ne_zero_of_gradientFactor_ne_zero
items.statement:
A nonzero low gradient factor forces the normalization denominator of the
fixed first-leg low eigenvector to be nonzero.
items.title: lowDenom_ne_zero_of_gradientFactor_ne_zero

items.label: metricReconstruction_of_ne
items.statement:
Under the same hypotheses, conjugating the removable spectral diagonal
back by the fixed frame reconstructs the physical first-leg metric.
items.title: metricReconstruction_of_ne

items.label: outputEqStep
items.statement:
The canceled outputs agree with the established abstract DFP step on the canonical
input with radius `ε ^ 2`, first control, and amplitude `G`.
items.title: outputEqStep

items.label: outputGradientEntry_analyticAt
items.statement:
Every coordinate of the canceled first-leg output gradient is real analytic at the common
base point.
items.title: outputGradientEntry_analyticAt

items.label: outputGradientEntry_continuousAt
items.statement:
Every coordinate of the canceled first-leg output gradient is continuous at
the common zero-scale base point.
items.title: outputGradientEntry_continuousAt

items.label: outputGradient_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the normalized gradient after the first DFP leg.
items.title: outputGradient_apply

items.label: outputMetricEntry_analyticAt
items.statement:
Every entry of the canceled first-leg output metric is real analytic at the common base
point.
items.title: outputMetricEntry_analyticAt

items.label: outputMetricEntry_continuousAt
items.statement:
Every entry of the canceled first-leg output metric is continuous at the
common zero-scale base point.
items.title: outputMetricEntry_continuousAt

items.label: outputMetric_eq_symmetricMatrix
items.statement:
The canceled first-leg metric is the symmetric matrix determined by its
three independent entries.
items.title: outputMetric_eq_symmetricMatrix

items.label: spectralFactors_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the removable spectral factors of the first leg.
items.title: spectralFactors_apply

items.label: spectrumFactorization
items.statement:
Locally at `(0, 2, 1)`, the first updated low and high eigenvalues factor as
`ε ^ 4 * L₁` and `ℋ₁`.
items.title: spectrumFactorization

items.label: spectrumFactorization_of_high_ne_zero
items.statement:
A nonzero high spectral factor exposes the pointwise removable
factorization of the first-leg eigenvalues.
items.title: spectrumFactorization_of_high_ne_zero

items.label: toObjectiveSublevel
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: a global Hessian bound restricts to every objective
sublevel set.
items.title: toObjectiveSublevel

items.label: analytic_spec
items.statement: Differentiability and positive definiteness at one index of a DFP trajectory.

items.label: denominators_spec
items.statement: Both scalar denominators in the inverse-form DFP update are nonzero.
items.title: denominators_spec

items.label: gradientInnerDisplacementNeg
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: a positive DFP step length and a positive-definite
inverse Hessian make the actual displacement a strict descent step.
items.title: gradientInnerDisplacementNeg

items.label: gradientNeZeroOfSecantDenominator
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: the nonzero secant denominator of an inverse-form DFP
iteration rules out a zero gradient at every index.
items.title: gradientNeZeroOfSecantDenominator

items.label: isOrbit
items.statement:
An inverse-form DFP iteration with positive step lengths gives the corresponding
certified orbit with its canonical gradient sequence.
items.title: isOrbit

items.label: objectiveSuccLeOfWeakWolfe
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: Armijo along a positive inverse-form DFP step makes the
objective value nonincreasing at that step.
items.title: objectiveSuccLeOfWeakWolfe

items.label: objectiveValuesAntitoneOfWeakWolfe
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: positive inverse-form DFP weak-Wolfe steps make the
objective values along the whole trajectory antitone.
items.title: objectiveValuesAntitoneOfWeakWolfe

items.label: ofSequences_inverseHessian
items.statement: The inverse-Hessian sequence of an iteration constructed by `ofSequences`.
items.title: ofSequences_inverseHessian

items.label: ofSequences_objective
items.statement: The objective of an iteration constructed by `ofSequences`.
items.title: ofSequences_objective

items.label: ofSequences_point
items.statement: The point sequence of an iteration constructed by `ofSequences`.
items.title: ofSequences_point

items.label: ofSequences_stepLength
items.statement: The step-length sequence of an iteration constructed by `ofSequences`.
items.title: ofSequences_stepLength

items.label: orthogonalSum_gradients

The canonical gradient sequence of the orthogonal-sum iteration is the embedded
canonical gradient sequence of the original iteration.
items.title: orthogonalSum_gradients

items.label: orthogonalSum_inverseHessian
items.statement:
The inverse Hessians of the orthogonal-sum iteration are the identity-block
extensions of the original inverse Hessians.
items.title: orthogonalSum_inverseHessian

items.label: orthogonalSum_objective
items.statement:
The objective of the orthogonal-sum iteration is the original objective plus the
identity quadratic block.

items.label: orthogonalSum_point
