items.label: bumpCorrection_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the global bump correction as a pointwise finsum.
items.title: bumpCorrection_apply

items.label: bumpCorrection_endpoint
items.statement:
The disjoint endpoint-bump correction vanishes at every endpoint when the interpolation
radii are positive and the interpolation balls are pairwise disjoint.
items.title: bumpCorrection_endpoint

items.label: bumpCorrection_eq_finsum_scaledLinearBump
items.statement:
The global bump correction is the pointwise finsum of the corresponding
generic scaled linear bumps.
items.title: bumpCorrection_eq_finsum_scaledLinearBump

items.label: bumpCorrection_eq_tsum
items.statement: The finsum-defined endpoint correction equals the pointwise endpoint-bump tsum.
items.title: bumpCorrection_eq_tsum

items.label: bumpCorrection_gradient_endpoint
items.statement:
The canonical gradient of the endpoint-bump correction at an endpoint is its prescribed
endpoint correction vector.
items.title: bumpCorrection_gradient_endpoint

items.label: bumpCorrection_hasGradientAt_endpoint
items.statement: The endpoint-bump correction has the prescribed endpoint correction as its Fréchet gradient.
items.title: bumpCorrection_hasGradientAt_endpoint

items.statement:
Helper for eq:endpoint-data: disjoint interpolation bumps have zero Hessian
at every interpolation center, since their cutoff is locally constant there.
items.title: bumpCorrection_hessian_endpoint

items.label: closedSetCandidate_eq
items.statement:
The endpoint closed-set candidate is the union of its limiting circle and
the range of the flattened endpoint sequence.
items.title: closedSetCandidate_eq

items.label: contDiff_endpointBump
items.statement:
Every endpoint bump is infinitely continuously differentiable, independently
of the endpoint data and interpolation radius.
items.title: contDiff_endpointBump

items.label: cycleCountBound_of_twoPhaseGap
items.statement:
An antitone two-phase angle lift with quadratic phase-gap bounds controls the
angular displacement across a positive number of cycles.  The factor `10` accounts
for the two phase gaps in a cycle and the two possible endpoint phases.
items.title: cycleCountBound_of_twoPhaseGap

items.label: endpointBump_activeIndices_subsingleton
items.statement: At each point, at most one endpoint bump has a nonzero value.
items.title: endpointBump_activeIndices_subsingleton

items.statement: Evaluation of the cutoff bump attached to an endpoint.
items.title: endpointBump_apply

items.label: endpointBump_eq_scaledLinearBump
items.statement: The endpoint bump is the generic scaled linear bump specialized to the endpoint data.
items.title: endpointBump_eq_scaledLinearBump

items.label: endpointBump_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement: Pairwise-disjoint interpolation balls give pairwise-disjoint endpoint-bump supports.
items.title: endpointBump_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: endpointBump_summable
items.statement: At each point, the endpoint-bump family is summable.
items.title: endpointBump_summable

items.statement: If endpoint bump `k` is nonzero at a point, the pointwise tsum is that bump.
items.title: endpointBump_tsum_eq_of_ne_zero

items.label: endpointBump_tsupport_subset_interpolationClosedBall
items.statement: The topological support of an endpoint bump lies in its interpolation closed ball.
items.title: endpointBump_tsupport_subset_interpolationClosedBall

items.label: endpointCenter_def

items.title: endpointCenter_odd

The endpoint correction is the prescribed gradient minus the translated
endpoint.
items.title: endpointCorrection_def

items.statement: The endpoint correction is the limiting center minus the endpoint center.
items.title: endpointCorrection_eq_center

items.statement: At an even endpoint, the correction is the limiting center minus the boundary center.
items.title: endpointCorrection_even

items.statement: At an odd endpoint, the correction is the limiting center minus the intermediate center.
items.title: endpointCorrection_odd

items.label: endpointCurvatureCertificates
items.statement:
Every flattened physical endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit
satisfies weak curvature with `c₂ = 3 / 4` and has positive secant curvature.
items.title: endpointCurvatureCertificates

items.label: endpointCurvatureCertificates_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the endpoint strong/weak curvature certificates are
available together for every `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointCurvatureCertificates_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_coe
items.statement: Coercing an endpoint-gradient lift recovers its quotient-valued direction angle.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_coe

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ
items.statement: The endpoint-gradient lift advances by the canonical representative of the next angle gap.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ_sub
items.statement:
Consecutive endpoint-gradient lifts differ by the canonical representative of their
quotient-angle gap.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ_sub

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_zero
items.statement: The endpoint-gradient lift starts at the canonical representative of the zeroth angle.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_zero

items.statement: The endpoint-gradient angle is measured from the first standard basis vector.
items.title: endpointGradientAngle_def

items.label: endpointGradientAngle_nextEven_sub_odd
items.statement:
Within an exact cycle, the gradient angle from its odd endpoint to the next even
endpoint is the second normalized endpoint-angle observable.
items.title: endpointGradientAngle_nextEven_sub_odd

items.label: endpointGradientAngle_odd_sub_even
items.statement:
Within an exact cycle, the gradient angle from the even endpoint to the following
odd endpoint is the first normalized endpoint-angle observable.
items.title: endpointGradientAngle_odd_sub_even

items.label: endpointGradientNorm_mem_Icc_of_amplitude_and_normalized

Amplitude and normalized-observable intervals give a uniform endpoint-gradient interval,
with the even and odd endpoint branches transported separately.
items.title: endpointGradientNorm_mem_Icc_of_amplitude_and_normalized

items.label: endpointGradient_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
Exact-cycle data transports the flattened endpoint gradient directly from
the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointGradient_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointGradient_eq_phaseGradient
items.statement: The flattened endpoint gradient is the physical gradient of the selected phase.
items.title: endpointGradient_eq_phaseGradient

items.label: endpointGradient_even
items.statement:
At an even endpoint, `endpointGradient` is the corresponding cycle-boundary
gradient.

items.label: endpointGradient_odd
items.statement:
At an odd endpoint, `endpointGradient` is the corresponding intermediate
first-leg gradient.
items.title: endpointGradient_odd

items.label: endpointGradient_succ_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
The flattened endpoint gradient after an exact phase is the next abstract
gradient transported by that phase's frame.
items.title: endpointGradient_succ_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointMetric_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
Exact-cycle data transports the flattened metric directly from the
selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointMetric_eq_exactStepTransport

items.statement:
The flattened endpoint metric at a structured phase index is the physical
metric selected for that phase.
items.title: endpointMetric_eq_phaseMetric

items.label: endpointMetric_even
items.statement: At an even endpoint, `endpointMetric` is the corresponding cycle-boundary metric.
items.title: endpointMetric_even

items.label: endpointMetric_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, `endpointMetric` is the corresponding intermediate metric.
items.title: endpointMetric_odd

items.label: endpointMetric_posDef
items.statement:
Every inverse-Hessian matrix in the flattened sequence of an exact
two-phase orbit is positive definite.
items.title: endpointMetric_posDef

items.label: endpointMetric_succ_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
The flattened metric after an exact phase is the transported next inverse
Hessian of the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointMetric_succ_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointPhaseSlope_transport
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the two physical endpoint pairings of a
phase are the slope and next-slope of its abstract secant step.

items.label: endpointPhaseStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.title: endpointPhaseStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointPhaseWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: every exact phase has weak-Wolfe curvature for any
`c₂` in the paper's range, again using the exact phase ratios.
items.title: endpointPhaseWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointPolarAngleLift_coe

items.label: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ_sub
items.statement:
Consecutive lifted values differ by the canonical real representative of the
quotient-angle gap.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ_sub

items.statement:
In the local signed-angle interval, the recursive increment is the unique representative
of the corresponding quotient-valued endpoint-angle gap.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ_sub_unique

items.statement: The endpoint polar-angle lift starts at the canonical representative of the zeroth angle.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_zero

items.label: endpointPolarAngle_def

items.title: endpointPolarAngle_def

items.statement: The polar angle at an even index is the angle of the corresponding boundary endpoint.
items.title: endpointPolarAngle_even

items.title: endpointPolarAngle_spec

items.statement:
The quotient-valued endpoint polar angle minus the gradient angle is the physical
oriented angle from the endpoint gradient to the radial displacement.
items.title: endpointPolarAngle_sub_gradientAngle

items.label: endpointPredictedDecrease_eq_exactStep
items.statement:
The physical predicted decrease between adjacent flattened endpoints is the
predicted decrease of the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointPredictedDecrease_eq_exactStep

items.label: endpointRadius_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, the radius is the square of the corresponding cycle scale.
items.title: endpointRadius_odd

items.label: endpointSecantCurvature_pos

Every flattened endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit has positive
gradient-displacement secant curvature.

items.statement:
The flattened exact step length at a structured phase index is the step
length of the selected abstract secant step.

The adjacent flattened-endpoint distance has the norm of the selected

items.statement:
Exact-cycle data transports the flattened adjacent-endpoint displacement

items.statement:
The flattened adjacent-endpoint displacement is the physical displacement

items.label: endpointStrongCurvature

TASK-03: Every flattened endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit has
strong curvature for any `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.

items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the flattened strong-curvature theorem in
the absolute-inequality form consumed by gradient-facing strong-Wolfe APIs.

items.label: endpointStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: every flattened exact-cycle endpoint has strong-Wolfe
curvature for all coefficients `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

construct the strong-Wolfe predicate for every flattened endpoint step.

items.statement:
Every flattened endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit satisfies the
weak-Wolfe curvature condition with `c₂ = 3 / 4`.

items.label: endpointWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: every flattened exact-cycle endpoint has weak-Wolfe
curvature for all coefficients `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: an endpoint Armijo inequality together with the
parameterized exact-cycle curvature certificate constructs the gradient-facing
weak-Wolfe predicate used by downstream iteration consumers.

items.label: endpoint_even

items.label: frameAngleIncrement_eq_observable

Each recursive frame-angle difference is the frame-angle field of the complete
observable map at the current normalized state.
items.title: frameAngleIncrement_eq_observable

items.statement:
If an orbit starts in the identity frame and all relative updates remain in the

current physical low vector.

disjoint from the limiting circle, provided the endpoint is not on that
circle.

distance.

The endpoint interpolation radius is the generic metric isolation radius in

limiting circle.

for an objective at the flattened endpoints, makes the flattened data a
classical inverse-form DFP orbit.

items.statement: A positive-scale limiting circle is nonempty.
items.title: limitCircle_nonempty

items.label: mapClusterPt_eq_of_tendsto
items.statement:
A cluster point of a sequence agrees with the sequence limit whenever the latter exists.

This is the basic `EndpointClusterSet/Basic` transport used to identify scalar limits
obtained from radial or angular error estimates.
items.title: mapClusterPt_eq_of_tendsto

items.label: mapClusterPt_mem_of_tendsto_infDist
items.statement:
A closed nonempty target contains every cluster point whose sequence distance to that
target tends to zero.

This is the metric `EndpointClusterSet/Basic` adapter for converting a radial remainder
estimate into a genuine cluster-set inclusion.
items.title: mapClusterPt_mem_of_tendsto_infDist

items.label: mapClusterSet_subset_limitCircle_of_tendsto_infDist
items.statement:
Every cluster point of an endpoint sequence belongs to a positive-scale limiting circle
when the endpoint distance to that circle tends to zero.

This is the one-sided `EndpointClusterSet/Basic` bridge; equality with the whole circle still
requires a separate angular recurrence or density hypothesis.
items.title: mapClusterSet_subset_limitCircle_of_tendsto_infDist

items.label: mem_closedSetCandidate
items.statement: Membership in the endpoint closed-set candidate.
items.title: mem_closedSetCandidate

items.label: mem_limitCircle
items.statement: Membership in the limiting circle in its affine unit-vector form.
items.title: mem_limitCircle

items.label: middleGradientNorm_eq_amplitude_mul_intermediateObservable
items.statement:
A valid intermediate gradient factors into its positive amplitude and
intermediate observable norm.
items.title: middleGradientNorm_eq_amplitude_mul_intermediateObservable

items.label: ofSlowCurveExact
items.statement:
For every sufficiently small positive initial scale, every physical cycle has valid
oriented phase data and agrees exactly with both abstract inverse-form DFP steps.
items.title: ofSlowCurveExact

items.label: ofSlowCurve_coordinates
items.statement:
The coordinates of the physical slow-curve orbit are the iterates of the signed
two-leg state map.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_coordinates

items.label: ofSlowCurve_phaseValidity
items.statement: Every sufficiently small slow-curve orbit has valid phase data at every cycle.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_phaseValidity

items.label: ofSlowCurve_succ
items.statement: Every slow-curve orbit applies the complete physical transition at the successor index.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_succ

items.label: ofSlowCurve_zero
items.statement: The slow-curve orbit starts at the explicit canonical physical state.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_zero

items.label: ofState_succ
items.statement: Every iterated orbit applies the complete physical transition at the successor index.
items.title: ofState_succ

items.label: ofState_zero
items.statement: An iterated orbit starts at its prescribed physical state.
items.title: ofState_zero

items.label: pairwiseDisjoint_interpolationClosedBall
items.statement:
Injectivity of the endpoint sequence makes its closed interpolation balls
pairwise disjoint.
items.title: pairwiseDisjoint_interpolationClosedBall

items.label: polarGradientLiftDifference_coe
items.statement:
Coercing the difference of the endpoint polar and gradient lifts gives the physical
polar-to-gradient correction angle.
items.title: polarGradientLiftDifference_coe

items.label: polarGradientLiftDifference_eq_correction_of_small
items.statement:
Small consecutive polar and gradient increments select a single real branch on
which the difference of their lifts equals the physical correction angle at every
endpoint.
items.title: polarGradientLiftDifference_eq_correction_of_small

items.label: polarGradientLiftDifference_zero_of_small
items.statement:
If the initial endpoint polar and gradient representatives are both in a common
quarter-turn chart, their lifted difference is the principal representative of the
physical correction angle.
items.title: polarGradientLiftDifference_zero_of_small

items.label: realizedObjective_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the realized objective at a point.
items.title: realizedObjective_apply

items.label: realizedObjective_decreaseRatio
items.statement:
The normalized decrease of the realized objective along an endpoint step is
the translated quadratic contribution plus the endpoint-correction contribution.
items.title: realizedObjective_decreaseRatio

items.label: realizedObjective_endpoint
items.statement:
The realized objective agrees with its translated quadratic part at every
interpolation endpoint.
items.title: realizedObjective_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_gradientChanges
items.statement:
The successive realized gradients along the endpoints have the same changes as
the prescribed abstract endpoint gradients.
items.title: realizedObjective_gradientChanges

items.label: realizedObjective_gradient_endpoint
items.statement:
At every interpolation endpoint, the realized objective has the prescribed
abstract endpoint gradient.
items.title: realizedObjective_gradient_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_gradient_formula_endpoint
items.statement:
At every interpolation endpoint, the gradient of the realized objective is the
translated quadratic gradient plus the endpoint correction.
items.title: realizedObjective_gradient_formula_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_hasEndpointGradientAt
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the endpoint gradient certificate of the
realized objective can be expressed with the orbit's prescribed gradient.
items.title: realizedObjective_hasEndpointGradientAt

items.label: realizedObjective_hasGradientAt_endpoint
items.statement:
The realized objective has the translated quadratic gradient plus the prescribed
endpoint correction at every interpolation endpoint.
items.title: realizedObjective_hasGradientAt_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_hessian_endpoint
items.statement:
Helper for eq:endpoint-data: the Hessian of the realized objective at an
interpolation endpoint is exactly the identity operator.
items.title: realizedObjective_hessian_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_isOrbit
items.statement:
The realized objective, prescribed endpoint step lengths, endpoints,
gradients, and inverse Hessians of an exact two-phase orbit satisfy the
classical inverse-form DFP recurrence.
items.title: realizedObjective_isOrbit

items.label: realizedObjective_not_hessianHolderOn
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: the concrete realized objective
cannot have a Hölder Hessian of exponent greater than one half on a convex
set containing its endpoints, whenever the physical steps are bounded by
a constant times the squares of the vanishing orbit scales.
items.title: realizedObjective_not_hessianHolderOn

items.label: slowCurveAdjacentEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Consecutive slow-curve endpoints have a uniform separation proportional to the
square of the scale of the cycle containing the earlier endpoint.
items.title: slowCurveAdjacentEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeAsymptotics
items.statement:
Every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit has a positive limiting
amplitude whose excess has first-order coefficient `13 / 3` in the scale.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeAsymptotics

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeDriftModulus
items.statement:
The canonical tail-supremum modulus uniformly controls the fourth-order
physical amplitude drift along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeDriftModulus

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeExistsPositiveLimit
items.statement:
For every sufficiently small positive initial scale, the amplitude of the canonical
slow-curve orbit converges to a strictly positive limit.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeExistsPositiveLimit

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeTailEquivalent
items.statement:
The amplitude excess of a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit is
asymptotic to `(13 / 3) * Glim * ε` at every positive limiting amplitude `Glim`.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeTailEquivalent

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeTailUniform
items.statement:
A common right-hand modulus controls the first-order amplitude-tail error on every
sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeTailUniform

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeUniformBounds
items.statement:
A common positive interval contains every amplitude and its limit on each sufficiently
small invariant slow-curve orbit with the prescribed jets.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurveAngularGapEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Comparable slow-curve endpoints with a definite principal angular gap have a
uniform separation proportional to the square of the earlier endpoint scale.
items.title: slowCurveAngularGapEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveArmijo
items.statement: The Armijo estimate for every endpoint step of an unbundled slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveArmijo

items.label: slowCurveCenterIncrementNormSummable
items.statement:
The norms of the full-cycle center increments are summable on a sufficiently
small positive invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveCenterIncrementNormSummable

items.label: slowCurveCenterTailUniformBound
items.statement:
A single positive constant uniformly controls the boundary and intermediate
center tails of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveCenterTailUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveCenterTendsto
items.statement:
The cycle-boundary centers of a sufficiently small positive invariant
slow-curve orbit converge in the Euclidean plane.
items.title: slowCurveCenterTendsto

items.label: slowCurveComparableScaleAmplitudeLoss
items.statement:
A comparable-scale interval of a positive slow-curve orbit has a uniform
positive fourth-order loss in physical amplitude at each intervening cycle.
items.title: slowCurveComparableScaleAmplitudeLoss

items.label: slowCurveDifferentScaleEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Chronologically ordered endpoints on sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits
with a fixed scale gap are separated in endpoint distance at squared-scale order.
items.title: slowCurveDifferentScaleEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveDifferentScaleRadialGap
items.statement:
Chronologically ordered endpoints on sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits
with a fixed scale gap have a uniform first-order radial separation.
items.title: slowCurveDifferentScaleRadialGap

items.label: slowCurveEndpointAngleRemainderModulus
items.statement:
The canonical tail-supremum modulus uniformly controls both real endpoint-gradient
angle remainders along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointAngleRemainderModulus

items.label: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionRadiusUniformBound
items.statement: A single positive constant uniformly controls endpoint corrections by scale times endpoint radius.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionRadiusUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionUniformBound
items.statement: A single positive constant uniformly controls endpoint corrections by the cube of their cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormTendsto
items.statement:
For every sufficiently small canonical slow-curve orbit, the norms of the
gradients along the full endpoint sequence converge to a strictly positive limit.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormTendsto

items.label: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormUniformBounds
items.statement:
One common positive interval contains every endpoint-gradient norm on all
sufficiently small canonical slow-curve orbits.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleDistanceEquivalent
items.statement:
The distance of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve endpoint to
its limiting circle is asymptotic to the first-order amplitude excess.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleDistanceEquivalent

items.label: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleInfDistUniformLower
items.statement:
Every endpoint of a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit stays at
least a uniform positive multiple of its squared cycle scale from the limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleInfDistUniformLower

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapExplicitBounds
items.statement:
Explicit-constant endpoint-angle gap bound: the two consecutive endpoint-angle
gaps lie between one half and five halves of the squared cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapExplicitBounds

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapLowerBound
items.statement:
Every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit has a consecutive lifted
endpoint-angle gap at least half the square of its cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapLowerBound

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapUniformBounds
items.statement:
For a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the lifted physical endpoint
angles are strictly decreasing and each consecutive gap is uniformly comparable to
the square of the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurveEndpointRadiusIsLittleODistance
items.statement:
The squared cycle scale is little-o of the endpoint distance to the
limiting circle for every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointRadiusIsLittleODistance

items.label: slowCurveEndpoint_injective
items.statement:
The flattened endpoint sequence of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve
orbit is injective once its center and amplitude have the stated limits.
items.title: slowCurveEndpoint_injective

items.label: slowCurveFirstStepNormRemainder
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the first
physical displacement divided by the amplitude differs from `2 * ε_j ^ 2` by
`o(ε_j ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveFirstStepNormRemainder

items.label: slowCurveFrameAngleIncrementUnique
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small exact invariant slow-curve orbit, every recursive
frame-angle difference is the unique small angle representing the relative frame.
items.title: slowCurveFrameAngleIncrementUnique

items.label: slowCurveFrameAngleRepresentsLowVector
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small exact invariant slow-curve orbit, the accumulated frame
angle rotates the initial physical low vector to every cycle-boundary low vector.
items.title: slowCurveFrameAngleRepresentsLowVector

items.label: slowCurveFullCenterDrift
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, one physical cycle
changes the center by `-(116 / 5) * G * ε ^ 6` times the physical low vector,
up to a vector remainder bounded by a constant multiple of `G * ε ^ 7`.
items.title: slowCurveFullCenterDrift

items.label: slowCurveFullCenterDriftBound
items.statement:
Any prescribed positive threshold below `1 / 4` admits a smaller threshold
with the same uniform full-cycle center-drift estimate.
items.title: slowCurveFullCenterDriftBound

items.label: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacement
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the physical
first-half center displacement is bounded asymptotically by the amplitude times
the cube of the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacement

items.label: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacementBound
items.statement:
Along all sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits, one positive
constant uniformly bounds every physical first-half center displacement by the
amplitude times the cube of the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacementBound

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnAmplitudeGap
items.statement:
Comparable-scale cycle endpoints whose lifted angles differ by a positive
number of windings have an amplitude gap bounded below by that winding count
times the squared incoming scale.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnAmplitudeGap

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnCycleCountBound
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow curve, a positive near-return winding
across `N` cycles satisfies the uniform cycle-count inequality.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnCycleCountBound

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Comparable-scale positive-winding near returns on a sufficiently small invariant
slow curve have endpoint separation proportional to the earlier squared scale.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnWindingNumber_pos
items.statement:
A near-return decomposition of two lifted endpoint angles has positive winding
number when the later endpoint is chronologically and radially separated.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnWindingNumber_pos

items.label: slowCurvePhaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound`.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound

items.label: slowCurvePhaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound
items.statement: The uniform decrease-ratio estimate for an unbundled slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound

items.label: slowCurvePhasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds`.
items.title: slowCurvePhasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsBigO
items.statement:
Both endpoint phases have radial error bounded by a cubic power of the
cycle scale along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsBigO

items.label: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsLittleO
items.statement:
Both endpoint phases have radial error little-o of the square of the
cycle scale along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsLittleO

items.label: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorUniform
items.statement:
A monotone right-hand modulus uniformly bounds both phase-radius errors by
the square of the cycle scale over all sufficiently small initial scales.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorUniform

items.label: slowCurvePhaseStepNormUniformBounds
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phaseStepNormUniformBounds`.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseStepNormUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurvePhaseStepRatioUniformBound
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phaseStepRatioUniformBound`.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseStepRatioUniformBound

items.label: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsBigO
items.statement:
The lifted polar-to-gradient angle error is big-O of the cubic orbit scale
along every endpoint phase of a small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsBigO

items.label: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsLittleO
items.statement:
The lifted polar-to-gradient angle error is little-O of the quadratic orbit
scale along every endpoint phase of a small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsLittleO

items.label: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorUniform
items.statement:
A uniform cubic bound controls the lifted polar-to-gradient angle error on a
small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorUniform

items.label: slowCurveSecondStepNormRemainder
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the second
physical displacement divided by the amplitude differs from `ε_j ^ 2` by
`o(ε_j ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveSecondStepNormRemainder

items.label: slowCurveTotalStepLengthNotSummable
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the series of
the two physical displacement norms in each cycle is not summable.
items.title: slowCurveTotalStepLengthNotSummable

items.label: slowCurveUniformEndpointPairSeparation
items.statement:
All distinct endpoints of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit
are uniformly separated at the squared scale of the first endpoint.
items.title: slowCurveUniformEndpointPairSeparation

items.label: slowCurveUniformEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Every endpoint of a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit is uniformly
isolated from all other endpoints and from the limiting circle at its squared scale.
items.title: slowCurveUniformEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowGradientNorms_eventually_mem_Icc
items.statement: Both normalized endpoint norms enter a fixed positive interval along a slow graph.
items.title: slowGradientNorms_eventually_mem_Icc

items.label: slowGraphPath_tendsto
items.statement:
The fifth-order slow-graph remainders force the parameter path to converge
to the canceled base state `(0, 2, 1)`. This is the unbundled compatibility
wrapper for `DFP.TwoLeg.SlowGraph.path_tendsto`.
items.title: slowGraphPath_tendsto

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: an identity-initialized operator certificate has a positive gradient
`liminf` once its recorded eventual lower bound is supplemented by an
eventual finite upper bound.  The extra hypothesis is explicit because a
conditionally complete real `liminf` is not determined by a lower bound alone.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: an identity-initialized operator certificate whose transformed gradient norm
is known to converge has the paper-facing positive `liminf` conclusion.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto

items.label: initialInverseHessian_is_identity
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: the identity-initialized operator certificate exposes its exact initial
inverse-Hessian identity as a direct semantic projection.
items.title: initialInverseHessian_is_identity

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: a strong identity-initialized operator certificate has the same semantic
`liminf` projection, under the explicit eventual upper bound required by the
real-valued liminf construction.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: the strong identity-initialized operator certificate has the same `liminf`
projection when its transformed gradient norm is supplied with a positive
limit.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto

items.label: initialInverseHessian_is_identity
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: the strong identity-initialized certificate preserves the exact initial
inverse-Hessian identity from its underlying operator certificate.
items.title: initialInverseHessian_is_identity

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos
items.statement: Helper for TASK-16: the matrix certificate exposes its paper-facing positive gradient liminf.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos

items.label: hessianBounds_pos_le
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-16: the matrix certificate exposes the ordered positive Hessian bounds required
by the identity corollary.
items.title: hessianBounds_pos_le

items.label: ofOperator
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-16: assemble the matrix-facing certificate from an identity-initialized
operator certificate.  The matrix positive-definiteness, secant denominator,
and gradient-liminf obligations are explicit hypotheses of this bridge.
items.title: ofOperator

items.label: ofOperatorWithObjective
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: the operator-to-matrix bridge
retains the objective exactly, preserving its analytic regularity.
items.title: ofOperatorWithObjective

items.label: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-16: assemble the matrix-facing liminf certificate from identity initialization
and strict positive secant curvature.  The existing matrix bridge derives
positive definiteness and all nonzero DFP denominators; no gradient-norm
convergence hypothesis is used.
items.title: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature

items.label: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-16: a convenience bridge deriving the matrix denominator hypothesis from
strict positive secant curvature of the operator orbit.
items.title: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature

items.label: gradientNormLiminf_pos
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: the eventual positive gradient tail of a matrix certificate implies the
corresponding strict positivity of its filter liminf.
items.title: gradientNormLiminf_pos

items.label: ofOperator
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: assemble a matrix-facing identity certificate from an operator certificate
when the canonical matrix sequence has the required positive definiteness and
nonzero DFP secant denominators.
items.title: ofOperator

items.label: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: assemble the matrix-facing certificate using only the operator orbit's
strict secant curvature.  The preceding identity-orbit lemmas derive both the
matrix positive-definiteness and the DFP denominator conditions.
items.title: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature

items.label: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: assemble a matrix-facing identity certificate from positive secant
curvature; the curvature lemma supplies the denominator side condition needed
by `InverseIteration`.
items.title: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_apply
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: evaluation of the canonical matrix representation at
an iteration index.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_apply

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_denominator_ne_of_operatorOrbit
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: a strictly positive secant pairing along an operator orbit supplies the
nonzero denominator for its canonical matrix orbit.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_denominator_ne_of_operatorOrbit

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_eq_explicit
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: identify the canonical matrix sequence with its
explicit `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.symm` pointwise representation.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_eq_explicit

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_posDef_of_identityOrbit
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: the identity-initialized operator orbit has positive-definite canonical
matrices at every step when its secant curvature is strictly positive.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_posDef_of_identityOrbit

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_zero_eq_one
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: identity of an operator is identity of its canonical
matrix representation.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_zero_eq_one

items.label: canonicalMatrix_posDef_of_operatorStrictPositive
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: convert strict positivity of a self-adjoint operator into positive
definiteness of its canonical real matrix.
items.title: canonicalMatrix_posDef_of_operatorStrictPositive

items.label: canonicalMatrix_posDef_of_pushforward_one
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-13: an arbitrary invertible coordinate factor sends the identity operator to a
strictly positive canonical matrix.
items.title: canonicalMatrix_posDef_of_pushforward_one

items.label: exists_identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_initialPosDef
items.statement:
TASK-14: Every parameterized strong-Wolfe counterexample with a
positive-definite initial inverse Hessian admits an automatically normalized
identity-initialized strong-Wolfe operator certificate.  The existential
output displays the factor and the positive distortion constants
`a = q` and `b = ‖A‖ + 1` together with every map inequality consumed by
`identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_factorized`.
items.title: exists_identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_initialPosDef

items.label: exists_matrixIdentityLiminfStrongWolfe_of_initialPosDef
items.statement:
TASK-16: every paper-range strong-Wolfe counterexample with positive-definite
initial inverse Hessian admits a matrix identity-initialized certificate with
some positive, ordered Hessian bounds and a strictly positive gradient liminf.
The bounds are generated from the positive square-root factor of the initial
matrix.
items.title: exists_matrixIdentityLiminfStrongWolfe_of_initialPosDef

items.label: factorAndBounds_of_initialPosDef
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-14: a positive-definite initial inverse Hessian determines
an invertible self-adjoint factor and explicit lower and upper Loewner bounds
for its pullback and pushforward identity operators.
items.title: factorAndBounds_of_initialPosDef

items.label: factorInitialInverseHessian_and_pullback
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: The matrix orbit of a certified inverse iteration has
an operator orbit whose initial factor can be normalized by a continuous linear
equivalence.
items.title: factorInitialInverseHessian_and_pullback

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: a weak-Wolfe counterexample's positive gradient limit is the paper-facing
strictly positive `liminf` statement.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos

items.label: gradient_ne_zero
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: the nonzero secant denominator in a classical inverse iteration rules out a
zero gradient at every iteration index.
items.title: gradient_ne_zero

items.label: hessianBounds_pos_le
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: positive Hessian bounds and the nontrivial Euclidean state space give the
paper's ordered parameter statement `0 < m ≤ M`.
items.title: hessianBounds_pos_le

items.label: identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_dimension_ge_two
items.statement:
TASK-10: A dimension-indexed strong certificate in the paper's Wolfe range
can be normalized once its concrete witness and factorization are supplied.
The witness is an explicit argument so that the factor equation refers to the
same trajectory used by the conclusion.
items.title: identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_dimension_ge_two

items.label: identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_factorized
items.statement:
TASK-10: A strong-Wolfe counterexample with an explicitly factorized
initial inverse Hessian can be affinely normalized to identity initialization.
The parameters `a`, `b`, and `q` are explicit lower/upper Loewner bounds for
the Hessian pullback and gradient pushforward, respectively.
items.title: identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_factorized

items.label: identityInitialized_fixedWeakWolfe_of_factorized
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: Fixed-constant weak-Wolfe specialization of
`identityInitialized_of_factorized`.  The output bounds remain the explicitly
transported `(a / 2, 3 * b / 2)` bounds rather than the original constants.
items.title: identityInitialized_fixedWeakWolfe_of_factorized

items.label: identityInitialized_of_factorized
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: Pulling back a fixed weak-Wolfe certificate through a
factorized initial inverse Hessian yields an identity-initialized operator
certificate.  The parameters `a` and `b` are the explicit lower and upper
Loewner distortion constants for the Hessian bounds.
items.title: identityInitialized_of_factorized

items.label: initialInverseHessianPosDef
items.statement:
The initial inverse-Hessian approximation of a certified counterexample is
positive definite.
items.title: initialInverseHessianPosDef

items.label: levelSetWeakWolfeAdmissible
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: A certified global weak-Wolfe counterexample supplies the
level-set admissibility data used by the paper-facing predicate.
items.title: levelSetWeakWolfeAdmissible

items.label: matrixIdentityLiminfStrongWolfeWithObjective
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: square-root normalization and
matrix reconstruction retain the exact pullback objective.
items.title: matrixIdentityLiminfStrongWolfeWithObjective

items.label: matrixIdentityLiminfStrongWolfe_of_factorized
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-16: an explicit factorized strong-Wolfe trajectory yields a classical matrix
identity-initialized certificate with the paper-facing positive gradient liminf.
items.title: matrixIdentityLiminfStrongWolfe_of_factorized

items.label: orthogonalSum
items.statement:
A weak-Wolfe DFP counterexample remains one after adjoining an identity
quadratic block on an orthogonal finite-dimensional summand, provided the
identity Hessian lies between the original bounds.
items.title: orthogonalSum

items.label: pullback_linearIsometryEquiv
items.statement:
Pulling a weak-Wolfe DFP counterexample back through a linear isometry
equivalence preserves its Hessian bounds, Wolfe conditions, and positive
limiting gradient norm.
items.title: pullback_linearIsometryEquiv

items.label: scalar_le_of_identity_loewner_bounds
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-16: scalar lower and upper Loewner bounds on the identity operator are ordered
on every Euclidean space whose coordinate index has at least two elements.
items.title: scalar_le_of_identity_loewner_bounds

items.label: weakWolfeAdmissible
items.statement:
A certified weak-Wolfe counterexample supplies the admissibility data used by
the global convergence predicate.
items.title: weakWolfeAdmissible

items.label: decreaseRatio_eq_one_sub_normSq_add_correction
items.statement:
If an objective agrees with a translated half squared norm at two points
and its reference gradient splits into the quadratic displacement plus a
correction, then its exact decrease ratio has the corresponding quadratic and
correction terms.
items.title: decreaseRatio_eq_one_sub_normSq_add_correction

items.label: directions_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the search-direction sequence at an iteration index.
items.title: directions_apply

items.label: existsHessianHolderPullback
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: a continuous linear change of
coordinates preserves existence of a positive global one-half Hölder constant.
items.title: existsHessianHolderPullback

items.label: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexample
items.statement:
TASK-08: Parameterized planar strong-Wolfe assembly. The invariant
slow-curve construction supplies a planar certificate for every admissible
pair of symbolic Wolfe coefficients.
items.title: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexample

items.label: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexampleHolder
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: the planar strong-Wolfe construction has a globally
one-half Hölder Hessian, with all properties attached to the same objective.
items.title: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexampleHolder

items.label: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexampleHolderSharp
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: the planar strong-Wolfe counterexample has exact
Hölder exponent one half, already on its initial objective sublevel.
items.title: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexampleHolderSharp

items.label: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexampleWithProperty
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: any objective and point-sequence property that holds
uniformly for sufficiently small realizations of every invariant slow curve can
be imposed on the same parameterized strong-Wolfe counterexample.
items.title: existsPlanarStrongWolfeCounterexampleWithProperty

items.label: existsPlanarWeakWolfeCounterexample
items.statement:
Theorem 2.3 (Uniformly convex weak-Wolfe DFP counterexample in dimension two):
there exists a globally `C²` planar objective with Hessian between `(1 / 2)I` and
`(3 / 2)I`, a well-defined positive-step inverse-form DFP trajectory satisfying weak
Wolfe with `(1 / 4, 3 / 4)`, and gradient norms tending to a positive limit.
items.title: existsPlanarWeakWolfeCounterexample

items.label: existsStrongWolfeCounterexampleHolder_of_dimension_ge_two
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: in every dimension at least two, one classical strong-Wolfe
counterexample has the exact Hessian bounds and a globally one-half Hölder Hessian.
items.title: existsStrongWolfeCounterexampleHolder_of_dimension_ge_two

items.label: existsStrongWolfeCounterexample_of_dimension_ge_two
items.statement:
TASK-09: A parameterized planar strong-Wolfe counterexample extends to every
finite dimension `n ≥ 2` with the same Hessian bounds and Wolfe coefficients.
items.title: existsStrongWolfeCounterexample_of_dimension_ge_two

items.label: existsWeakWolfeCounterexample
items.statement:
Theorem 2.4 (Counterexample in every dimension $n\ge2$): for every `n` with
`2 ≤ n`, there is a globally `C²` objective on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` with
Hessian between `(1 / 2)I` and `(3 / 2)I`, and a positive-step inverse-form DFP
trajectory satisfying weak Wolfe with `(1 / 4, 3 / 4)` whose gradient norms tend to
a positive limit.
items.title: existsWeakWolfeCounterexample

items.label: existsWeakWolfeCounterexample_fixedParameters
items.statement:
TASK-06 helper: the fixed-parameter weak-Wolfe certificate is available in
every finite dimension `n` with `2 ≤ n`.
items.title: existsWeakWolfeCounterexample_fixedParameters

items.label: gradientChanges_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the gradient-change sequence at an iteration index.
items.title: gradientChanges_apply

items.label: gradients_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the gradient sequence at an iteration index.
items.title: gradients_apply

items.label: hessianBounds_lower_le_upper
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: uniform lower and upper Loewner bounds on a Hessian force the lower scalar
bound to be no larger than the upper scalar bound on a nontrivial space.
items.title: hessianBounds_lower_le_upper

items.label: hessianHolderOn_sublevel_of_comp
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: a Hölder Hessian bound on an
initial sublevel pulls back through an invertible linear coordinate change.
items.title: hessianHolderOn_sublevel_of_comp

items.label: identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_parameterRange
items.statement:
TASK-11: The identity-initialized strong-Wolfe corollary is exposed with
the explicit witness, factorization, and Loewner/gradient bounds required by
the operator-level normalization theorem.
items.title: identityInitializedStrongWolfe_of_parameterRange

items.label: main_not_globalWeakWolfeConvergence_fixedParameters
items.statement:
TASK-06 Main theorem: at the fixed weak-Wolfe coefficients `(1 / 4, 3 / 4)`,
the global convergence predicate is false.
items.title: main_not_globalWeakWolfeConvergence_fixedParameters

items.label: main_not_globalWeakWolfeConvergence_forall_parameterRange
items.statement:
TASK-11: The preceding negative convergence theorem is uniform over all
coefficient pairs satisfying `0 < c₁ < 2 / 3` and `2 / 3 ≤ c₂ < 1`.
items.title: main_not_globalWeakWolfeConvergence_forall_parameterRange

items.label: main_not_levelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_forall_parameterRange
items.statement:
TASK-15: The level-set global-convergence predicate is false for every
coefficient pair in the paper's stated range.
items.title: main_not_levelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_forall_parameterRange

items.label: mem_objectiveSublevel_iff
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: membership in the initial objective sublevel set is
exactly the corresponding objective-value inequality.
items.title: mem_objectiveSublevel_iff

items.label: not_PaperRangeGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence
items.statement:
TASK-15: A direct negation of the positive convergence predicate
quantified over the paper's coefficient range.
items.title: not_PaperRangeGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence

items.label: not_PaperRangeLevelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence
items.statement: TASK-15: The level-set paper-range convergence predicate is false.
items.title: not_PaperRangeLevelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence

items.label: not_globalWeakWolfeConvergenceAt_of_counterexample
items.statement:
Any weak-Wolfe counterexample disproves the fixed-coefficient global
convergence claim at its own coefficients.
items.title: not_globalWeakWolfeConvergenceAt_of_counterexample

items.label: not_levelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergenceAt_of_counterexample
items.statement:
TASK-15: Any weak-Wolfe counterexample disproves the level-set global
convergence claim at its own coefficients.
items.title: not_levelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergenceAt_of_counterexample

items.label: not_tendsto_zero_of_pos_limit
items.statement: A real sequence with a strictly positive limit cannot converge to zero.
items.title: not_tendsto_zero_of_pos_limit

items.label: not_universalGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_fixedParameters
items.statement:
TASK-06 corollary: one fixed weak-Wolfe counterexample refutes the universal
global convergence claim over all admissible coefficient pairs.
items.title: not_universalGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_fixedParameters

items.label: not_universalGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_of_counterexample
items.statement:
A single admissible weak-Wolfe counterexample refutes the universal global
convergence claim over all Wolfe coefficients.
items.title: not_universalGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_of_counterexample

items.label: not_universalLevelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_of_counterexample
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: A single admissible counterexample refutes the universal
level-set global convergence claim over all Wolfe coefficients.
items.title: not_universalLevelSetGlobalWeakWolfeConvergence_of_counterexample

items.label: positive_liminf_of_eventually_lower_upper
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: a sequence with an eventual positive lower bound and an
eventual finite upper bound has strictly positive real `liminf`.
items.title: positive_liminf_of_eventually_lower_upper

items.label: positive_liminf_of_tendsto
items.statement:
Helper for TASK-15: convergence of a real sequence to a positive value identifies its
`liminf` with that value and hence makes the `liminf` positive.
items.title: positive_liminf_of_tendsto

items.label: steps_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the scaled-step sequence at an iteration index.
items.title: steps_apply

items.label: twoStepSequence_even
items.statement: The even terms of a flattened two-step sequence are its boundary data.
items.title: twoStepSequence_even

items.label: twoStepSequence_odd
items.statement: The odd terms of a flattened two-step sequence are its intermediate data.
items.title: twoStepSequence_odd

items.label: map_apply
items.statement: The bundled endomorphism `map` acts by matrix-vector multiplication.
items.title: map_apply

items.label: matrix_mulVec
items.statement: Multiplication by `matrix` in coordinates.
items.title: matrix_mulVec

items.label: weightedSum_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the explicit weighted coordinate-sum seminorm.
items.title: weightedSum_apply

items.label: weightedSum_comp_le
items.statement: The explicit contraction bound as an inequality of seminorms.
items.title: weightedSum_comp_le

items.label: weightedSum_contracts
items.statement: The stable endomorphism contracts `weightedSum` at the rational rate `1 / 3 < 1`.
items.title: weightedSum_contracts

items.label: weightedSum_isContracting
items.statement: The explicit weighted coordinate-sum seminorm makes `map` contracting below one.
items.title: weightedSum_isContracting

items.label: weightedSum_isEquivalent
items.statement: The weighted coordinate-sum seminorm is equivalent to the standard norm seminorm.
items.title: weightedSum_isEquivalent

items.label: activeIndices_subsingleton_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement:
A point belongs to the topological support of at most one member of a
pairwise-disjoint family of topological supports.
items.title: activeIndices_subsingleton_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: fderiv_eq_at_center
items.statement:
At an active center outside the cluster set, the ordinary Fréchet derivative of a
pointwise disjoint finsum is the derivative of the unique active summand.
items.title: fderiv_eq_at_center

items.label: fderiv_eq_at_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
The first Frechet derivative of a pointwise disjoint finsum at a designated center
equals that of the centered summand without an active-support assumption.
items.title: fderiv_eq_at_center_of_disjoint

items.label: finsum_eq_eventuallyEq_at_center_of_pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall
items.statement:
Near the center of a positive-radius pairwise-disjoint closed ball, a supported finsum is
eventually equal to its centered summand.
items.title: finsum_eq_eventuallyEq_at_center_of_pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall

items.label: finsum_eq_single_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement:
A point in one member of a pairwise-disjoint support family sees only that summand in the
pointwise finsum.
items.title: finsum_eq_single_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: gradient_at_center
items.statement:
The gradient of a pointwise disjoint finsum at an active center is the certified gradient
of its active summand.
items.title: gradient_at_center

items.label: gradient_at_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
The gradient of a pointwise disjoint finsum at a designated center is the certified
gradient of the centered summand, without requiring active support at the center.
items.title: gradient_at_center_of_disjoint

items.label: gradient_finsum_of_pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall
items.statement:
The gradient of a pairwise-disjoint positive-radius closed-ball finsum at a center is the
gradient of its centered summand.
items.title: gradient_finsum_of_pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall

items.label: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_finsum_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
The gradient of a translated quadratic plus a pointwise disjoint finsum at a center is
the displacement from the quadratic center plus the centered-summand gradient.
items.title: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_finsum_center_of_disjoint

items.label: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_indicator_compl_finsum_center
items.statement:
The gradient of a translated quadratic plus a zero-extended disjoint finsum at a center
is the displacement from the quadratic center plus the centered-summand gradient.
items.title: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_indicator_compl_finsum_center

items.label: halfNormSq_sub_add_finsum_apply_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
If the centered summand vanishes at its center, adding the pointwise disjoint finsum
does not change the translated quadratic value there.
items.title: halfNormSq_sub_add_finsum_apply_center_of_disjoint

items.label: halfNormSq_sub_add_indicator_compl_finsum_apply_center
items.statement:
If the centered summand vanishes at its center, adding the zero-extended disjoint finsum
does not change the translated quadratic value there.
items.title: halfNormSq_sub_add_indicator_compl_finsum_apply_center

items.label: hasGradientAt_at_center
items.statement:
A gradient certificate for an active summand transfers to the pointwise disjoint finsum
at the same center.
items.title: hasGradientAt_at_center

items.label: hasGradientAt_at_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
A gradient certificate for the centered summand transfers to the pointwise disjoint
finsum even when the center is outside every topological support.
items.title: hasGradientAt_at_center_of_disjoint

items.label: hasGradientAt_finsum_of_pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall
items.statement:
A gradient certificate for a centered summand transfers across a pairwise-disjoint
positive-radius closed-ball finsum.
items.title: hasGradientAt_finsum_of_pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall

items.label: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_finsum_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
A centered-summand gradient certificate gives the corresponding gradient certificate
for a translated quadratic plus the pointwise disjoint finsum.
items.title: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_finsum_center_of_disjoint

items.label: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_indicator_compl_finsum_center
items.statement:
A centered-summand gradient certificate gives the corresponding gradient certificate
for a translated quadratic plus the zero-extended disjoint finsum.
items.title: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_indicator_compl_finsum_center

items.label: hasGradientAt_indicator_compl_finsum_at_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
A gradient certificate for a centered summand transfers to the zero extension of the
pointwise disjoint finsum at that center.
items.title: hasGradientAt_indicator_compl_finsum_at_center_of_disjoint

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_centered
items.statement:
At a designated center outside the cluster set, every available iterated derivative
of a pointwise disjoint finsum equals that of the corresponding summand. No assumption
that the center belongs to the summand's topological support is needed.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_centered

items.label: summable_apply_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement:
Pointwise evaluation of a family with pairwise-disjoint topological
supports is summable.
items.title: summable_apply_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: summable_of_support_subsingleton
items.statement: A family with at most one nonzero term is summable.
items.title: summable_of_support_subsingleton

items.label: support_apply_subsingleton_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement:
At each point, the values of a family with pairwise-disjoint topological
supports have subsingleton function support.
items.title: support_apply_subsingleton_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: tsum_apply_eq_single_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement:
At a point in one topological support, the pointwise infinite sum of a
pairwise-disjoint support family is the corresponding summand.
items.title: tsum_apply_eq_single_of_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: tsum_apply_eq_zero_of_forall_not_mem_tsupport
items.statement:
If a point lies in none of the topological supports, the corresponding
pointwise infinite sum is zero.
items.title: tsum_apply_eq_zero_of_forall_not_mem_tsupport

items.label: tsum_eq_single_of_support_subsingleton
items.statement:
If a family has at most one nonzero term and its value at `k` is nonzero,
then its infinite sum is that value.
items.title: tsum_eq_single_of_support_subsingleton

items.label: tsum_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero
items.statement: If every term of a family is zero, then its infinite sum is zero.
items.title: tsum_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero

items.label: value_eq_at_center
items.statement:
The value of a pointwise disjoint finsum at an active center is the value of its unique
active summand.
items.title: value_eq_at_center

items.label: value_eq_at_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
The value of a pointwise disjoint finsum at a designated center equals the value of
the centered summand, including when both sides vanish near that center.
items.title: value_eq_at_center_of_disjoint

items.label: value_indicator_compl_finsum_eq_at_center_of_disjoint
items.statement:
At a designated center outside the cluster set, the zero extension of a pointwise
disjoint finsum has the value of the centered summand.
items.title: value_indicator_compl_finsum_eq_at_center_of_disjoint

items.label: analyticOnNhd_coordinate
items.statement: The signed-angle coordinate is real-analytic throughout the identity chart.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_coordinate

items.label: coordinate_mem_interval
items.statement: Every signed-angle coordinate lies in the arctangent branch interval.
items.title: coordinate_mem_interval

items.label: coordinate_one
items.statement: The signed-angle coordinate of the identity matrix is zero.
items.title: coordinate_one

items.label: coordinate_rotationMatrix
items.statement: On the local branch interval, the coordinate recovers the real rotation parameter.
items.title: coordinate_rotationMatrix

items.label: coordinate_rotationMatrix_toReal
items.statement:
On the local branch, the matrix coordinate agrees with the canonical real angle
representative.
items.title: coordinate_rotationMatrix_toReal

items.label: coordinate_unique
items.statement: The local real parameter of a special orthogonal matrix is uniquely its coordinate.
items.title: coordinate_unique

items.label: isOpen_chart
items.statement: The signed-angle chart is open in the ambient matrix space.
items.title: isOpen_chart

items.label: mem_chart
items.statement: Membership in the signed-angle chart is positivity of the upper-left entry.
items.title: mem_chart

items.label: one_mem_chart
items.statement: The identity matrix belongs to the signed-angle chart.
items.title: one_mem_chart

items.label: rotationMatrix_coordinate
items.statement: A special orthogonal matrix in the identity chart is recovered from its coordinate.
items.title: rotationMatrix_coordinate

items.label: complexIsometry_apply_mul_exp
items.statement:
Under `complexIsometry`, a complex polar vector is the standard planar rotation of the
first coordinate vector, scaled by its radius.
items.title: complexIsometry_apply_mul_exp

items.label: contDiffAt_oangle_toReal_of_pos
items.statement:
The principal real oriented angle is smooth wherever both vectors remain in the positive
first-coordinate chart.
items.title: contDiffAt_oangle_toReal_of_pos

items.label: contDiff_smoothCutoff
items.statement: The planar cutoff is infinitely differentiable.
items.title: contDiff_smoothCutoff

items.label: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_eqOn_zero_jets
items.statement:
In the Euclidean plane, the same supportwise decay certificate also gives vanishing
gradient and operator-valued Hessian on the closed cluster set.
items.title: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_eqOn_zero_jets

items.label: det_hessianMatrix
items.statement: The determinant of the Hessian matrix equals the determinant of the Hessian linear map.
items.title: det_hessianMatrix

items.label: det_rotationMatrix
items.statement: The explicit rotation matrix has determinant one.
items.title: det_rotationMatrix

items.label: eq_frame_firstColumn_of_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup
items.statement:
A real `2 × 2` special orthogonal matrix is the positively oriented frame
generated by its first column.
items.title: eq_frame_firstColumn_of_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.label: frame_eq_rotationMatrix_oangle
items.statement:
A unit frame is the rotation matrix of the oriented angle from the first
standard basis vector.
items.title: frame_eq_rotationMatrix_oangle

items.label: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff
items.statement:
The frame `(e, perp e)` is positively oriented orthonormal exactly when
`e` is a unit vector.
items.title: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff

items.label: frame_mulVec
items.statement: Frame coordinates reconstruct the corresponding linear combination of `e` and `perp e`.
items.title: frame_mulVec

items.label: gradient_comp_linearIsometry
items.statement: The gradient transforms contravariantly under an orthogonal change of frame.
items.title: gradient_comp_linearIsometry

items.label: hasCompactSupport_smoothCutoff
items.statement: The planar cutoff has compact topological support.
items.title: hasCompactSupport_smoothCutoff

items.label: hasHessianBoundsAt_iff_hessianMatrix
items.statement:
Pointwise operator-valued Hessian bounds are equivalent to the corresponding lower and
upper positive-semidefinite bounds on the Euclidean-plane Hessian matrix.
items.title: hasHessianBoundsAt_iff_hessianMatrix

items.label: hasHessianBounds_iff_hessianMatrix
items.statement:
Global operator-valued Hessian bounds are equivalent to pointwise lower and upper
positive-semidefinite bounds on every Euclidean-plane Hessian matrix.
items.title: hasHessianBounds_iff_hessianMatrix

items.label: hessianMatrix_apply
items.statement: Applying the Hessian agrees in canonical coordinates with multiplying by its Hessian matrix.
items.title: hessianMatrix_apply

items.label: hessianMatrix_isHermitian
items.statement: At a point where `f` is `C²`, its Hessian matrix is Hermitian, hence symmetric over `ℝ`.
items.title: hessianMatrix_isHermitian

items.label: hessianMatrix_sqNorm_add_bounds_of_norm_le
items.statement:
A norm bound on the perturbation Hessian bounds the Hessian matrix of half the squared
distance plus the perturbation between the corresponding scalar identity matrices.
items.title: hessianMatrix_sqNorm_add_bounds_of_norm_le

items.label: hessian_apply_inner
items.statement:
Pairing the operator-valued Hessian with a direction recovers the second iterated
Fréchet derivative.
items.title: hessian_apply_inner

items.label: hessian_comp_linearIsometry
items.statement: The Hessian transforms by orthogonal conjugation under a change of frame.
items.title: hessian_comp_linearIsometry

items.label: hessian_def
items.statement: The operator-valued Hessian unfolds to the Fréchet derivative of the gradient.
items.title: hessian_def

items.label: hessian_eq_genericHessian
items.statement:
The Euclidean-plane Hessian agrees with the generic operator-valued Hessian on the
Euclidean plane.
items.title: hessian_eq_genericHessian

items.label: hessian_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The operator-valued Hessian of a planar zero extension vanishes identically on the
closed set under the second-order value and first-derivative decay assumptions.
items.title: hessian_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: hessian_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension across a closed subset of the Euclidean plane has vanishing operator-valued
Hessian at every boundary point under the usual second-order value and first-derivative decay.
items.title: hessian_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: hessian_isSelfAdjoint
items.statement: At a point where `f` is `C²`, its operator-valued Hessian is self-adjoint.
items.title: hessian_isSelfAdjoint

items.label: hessian_sqNorm_add
items.statement:
The Hessian of half the squared distance from `C` plus `Ψ` is the identity operator plus
the Hessian of `Ψ`.
items.title: hessian_sqNorm_add

items.label: lowerBound_hessianMatrix_iff
items.statement:
A lower Loewner bound on the Hessian matrix is equivalent to the corresponding quadratic-form
bound on the Hessian operator.
items.title: lowerBound_hessianMatrix_iff

items.label: norm_fderiv_smoothCutoff_le
items.statement: The first derivative of the planar cutoff is globally bounded by its order-one bound.
items.title: norm_fderiv_smoothCutoff_le

items.label: norm_firstColumn_eq_one_of_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup
items.statement:
The first column of a real `2 × 2` special orthogonal matrix has Euclidean
norm one.
items.title: norm_firstColumn_eq_one_of_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_smoothCutoff_le
items.statement:
The `n`-th iterated derivative of the planar cutoff is globally bounded by
its supremum-defined bound.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_smoothCutoff_le

items.label: norm_secondFDeriv_smoothCutoff_le
items.statement: The second derivative of the planar cutoff is globally bounded by its order-two bound.
items.title: norm_secondFDeriv_smoothCutoff_le

items.label: norm_smoothCutoff_le
items.statement: The values of the planar cutoff are globally bounded by its order-zero bound.
items.title: norm_smoothCutoff_le

items.label: oangle_frame_mulVec
items.statement:
Applying the same positively oriented unit frame to two coordinate vectors preserves
their oriented angle.
items.title: oangle_frame_mulVec

items.label: oangle_frame_mulVec_toReal_eq_arctan_sub_of_pos
items.statement:
In a positively oriented unit frame, the principal real oriented angle is the
difference of the arctangents of the two coordinate slopes.
items.title: oangle_frame_mulVec_toReal_eq_arctan_sub_of_pos

items.label: oangle_specialOrthogonal_mulVec
items.statement:
Simultaneously applying a real `2 × 2` special orthogonal matrix preserves
the oriented angle between two coordinate vectors.
items.title: oangle_specialOrthogonal_mulVec

items.label: oangle_toReal_eq_arctan_sub_of_pos
items.statement:
For two planar vectors whose first coordinates are positive, the principal real
representative of their oriented angle is the difference of their arctangent slope coordinates.
items.title: oangle_toReal_eq_arctan_sub_of_pos

items.label: perp_apply
items.statement: The right-angle operator sends `(x₁, x₂)` to `(-x₂, x₁)`.
items.title: perp_apply

items.label: polarDistance_ge_max_principal_sub_errors
items.statement:
Two planar points close to polar vectors about a common center inherit the maximum of the
radial and principal angular separation bounds, up to their two approximation errors.
items.title: polarDistance_ge_max_principal_sub_errors

items.label: rotationMatrix_mulVec
items.statement: Matrix-vector multiplication by `rotationMatrix` agrees with the bundled rotation.
items.title: rotationMatrix_mulVec

items.label: rotation_apply
items.statement:
Rotation in the standard Euclidean plane is the cosine-sine combination of a vector and
its positively oriented perpendicular.
items.title: rotation_apply

items.label: smoothCutoffDerivBound_nonneg
items.statement: Every iterated-derivative bound of the planar cutoff is nonnegative.
items.title: smoothCutoffDerivBound_nonneg

items.label: smoothCutoff_eq_one
items.statement: The planar cutoff equals one on the closed ball of radius one third.
items.title: smoothCutoff_eq_one

items.label: toEuclideanCLM_hessianMatrix
items.statement: Converting the Hessian matrix back to a Euclidean continuous linear map recovers the Hessian.
items.title: toEuclideanCLM_hessianMatrix

items.label: toMatrix_rotation
items.statement: The matrix of the bundled rotation in the standard Euclidean basis is `rotationMatrix`.
items.title: toMatrix_rotation

items.label: tsupport_smoothCutoff_subset
items.statement: The topological support of the planar cutoff lies in the open unit ball.
items.title: tsupport_smoothCutoff_subset

items.label: upperBound_hessianMatrix_iff
items.statement:
An upper Loewner bound on the Hessian matrix is equivalent to the corresponding quadratic-form
bound on the Hessian operator.
items.title: upperBound_hessianMatrix_iff

items.label: contDiff_objective
items.statement:
Adding a half squared norm on an orthogonal summand preserves twice continuous
differentiability.
items.title: contDiff_objective

items.label: differentiableAt_objective_inl_iff
items.statement:
Differentiability of the lifted objective at an embedded point is equivalent
to differentiability of the original objective.
items.title: differentiableAt_objective_inl_iff

items.label: gradient_objective
items.statement:
The gradient of the orthogonal-sum objective at an arbitrary point consists of the
left gradient and the current right coordinate.
items.title: gradient_objective

items.label: gradient_objective_inl
items.statement:
At an embedded point, the gradient of the orthogonal-sum objective is the embedded
gradient of the original objective.
items.title: gradient_objective_inl

items.label: hasGradientAt_objective
items.statement:
A certified gradient of the left objective and the current right coordinate combine to
the gradient of the orthogonal-sum objective at an arbitrary point.
items.title: hasGradientAt_objective

items.label: hasGradientAt_objective_inl
items.statement: A certified gradient embeds as a certified gradient of the orthogonal-sum objective.
items.title: hasGradientAt_objective_inl

items.label: hasHessianBounds_objective
items.statement:
If the original Hessian lies between `m I` and `M I`, adjoining an identity quadratic
block preserves those bounds whenever `m ≤ 1 ≤ M`.
items.title: hasHessianBounds_objective

items.label: hessianHolder_objective
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: adjoining an identity quadratic block preserves a
global Hölder Hessian bound with the same exponent and constant.
items.title: hessianHolder_objective

items.label: hessian_objective_apply
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: the Hessian of an objective extended by an identity
quadratic acts separately on its two orthogonal coordinates.
items.title: hessian_objective_apply

items.label: inner_eq_left_add_right
items.statement:
The inner product on a Euclidean orthogonal sum is the sum of the inner products of
its two coordinate projections.
items.title: inner_eq_left_add_right

items.label: inner_inl_left
items.statement:
Pairing a left-embedded vector with an arbitrary direct-sum vector depends only on the
left projection.
items.title: inner_inl_left

items.label: left_inl
items.statement: Projecting a left-embedded vector onto the left coordinates recovers it.
items.title: left_inl

items.label: left_sumEquivProd_symm
items.statement:
The left projection of a vector reconstructed from orthogonal-sum coordinates is its
left coordinate.
items.title: left_sumEquivProd_symm

items.label: norm_hessian_objective_sub_le
items.statement:
Helper for thm:main: the variable part of the extended Hessian is supported
on the original coordinates, so its difference has no larger operator norm.
items.title: norm_hessian_objective_sub_le

items.label: norm_hessian_sub_le_objective
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: restriction to the original
coordinates recovers a lower bound for the extended Hessian difference norm.
items.title: norm_hessian_sub_le_objective

items.label: norm_left_le
items.statement: Helper for thm:main: an orthogonal coordinate projection does not increase norm.
items.title: norm_left_le

items.label: norm_sq_eq_left_add_right
items.statement:
The squared norm on a Euclidean orthogonal sum is the sum of the squared norms of its
two coordinate projections.
items.title: norm_sq_eq_left_add_right

items.label: objective_apply
items.statement:
Evaluation of the objective obtained by adjoining a half squared norm on the right
orthogonal summand.
items.title: objective_apply

items.label: objective_inl
items.statement: The orthogonal-sum objective restricts to the original objective on the left summand.
items.title: objective_inl

items.label: right_inl
items.statement: Projecting a left-embedded vector onto the right coordinates gives zero.
items.title: right_inl

items.label: right_sumEquivProd_symm
items.statement:
The right projection of a vector reconstructed from orthogonal-sum coordinates is its
right coordinate.
items.title: right_sumEquivProd_symm

items.label: toDual_inl
items.statement:
The Riesz dual of a left-embedded vector is the original Riesz dual composed with the
left projection.
items.title: toDual_inl

items.label: extendMatrix_apply_inl_inl
items.statement: The upper-left block of `extendMatrix H` is `H`.
items.title: extendMatrix_apply_inl_inl

items.label: extendMatrix_apply_inl_inr
items.statement: The upper-right block of `extendMatrix H` vanishes.
items.title: extendMatrix_apply_inl_inr

items.label: extendMatrix_apply_inr_inl
items.statement: The lower-left block of `extendMatrix H` vanishes.
items.title: extendMatrix_apply_inr_inl

items.label: extendMatrix_apply_inr_inr
items.statement: The lower-right block of `extendMatrix H` is the identity.
items.title: extendMatrix_apply_inr_inr

items.label: extendMatrix_mulVec_inl
items.statement:
