The identity-block extension acts on a left-embedded vector by the embedded
original matrix action.
items.title: extendMatrix_mulVec_inl

items.label: extendMatrix_posDef_iff
items.statement:
Extending a real square matrix by an identity block preserves and reflects positive
definiteness. This statement does not require either index type to be finite.
items.title: extendMatrix_posDef_iff

items.label: inl_apply_inl
items.statement: The left coordinates of the canonical left-summand embedding are unchanged.
items.title: inl_apply_inl

items.label: inl_apply_inr
items.statement: The right coordinates of the canonical left-summand embedding vanish.
items.title: inl_apply_inr

items.label: inner_inl
items.statement: The canonical left-summand embedding preserves the real inner product.
items.title: inner_inl

items.label: norm_inl
items.statement: The canonical left-summand embedding is an isometry.
items.title: norm_inl

items.label: quadraticForm_extendMatrix
items.statement:
The quadratic form of an identity-block extension splits as the original quadratic
form plus a sum of squares.
items.title: quadraticForm_extendMatrix

items.label: tendsto_norm_div_infDist_of_sq
items.statement:
Quadratic decay relative to the distance from a set implies the corresponding
first-order decay along the same distance filter.
items.title: tendsto_norm_div_infDist_of_sq

items.label: exists_pos_le
items.statement:
A finite family of positive elements in a linear order has a common positive
lower bound below any prescribed positive bound.
items.title: exists_pos_le

items.label: add
items.statement:
Uniform finite jets are closed under pointwise addition at a common input
base.
items.title: add

items.label: boundedCoeff
items.statement:
A uniform finite jet family has uniformly bounded coefficients in every
degree through `m`.
items.title: boundedCoeff

items.label: comp
items.statement:
Uniform finite jets compose when the inner family sends its common base to
the common expansion base of the outer family.
items.title: comp

items.label: congr
items.statement:
Uniformity is unchanged when both the function family and jet family agree
on the parameter set under consideration.
items.title: congr

items.label: exists_one_le_coeff_bound
items.statement:
All coefficients in a uniform finite jet family admit one common bound of
size at least one.
items.title: exists_one_le_coeff_bound

items.label: inv
items.statement:
Reciprocal postcomposition preserves a real uniform finite jet family when
all constant coefficients equal one nonzero base value.
items.title: inv

items.label: mul
items.statement:
Uniform finite jets with values in a normed real algebra are closed under
pointwise multiplication.
items.title: mul

items.label: norm
items.statement:
Norm postcomposition preserves uniform finite jets in a real inner product
space when all constant coefficients equal one nonzero vector.
items.title: norm

items.label: remainder
items.statement:
A uniform finite jet family supplies an order-`m` remainder estimate with
every prescribed positive coefficient.
items.title: remainder

items.label: scalarRemainder_isLittleO
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (Finite-smooth invariant graph under an explicit stable
contraction): a scalar member of a uniform jet family has a pointwise Peano remainder.
items.title: scalarRemainder_isLittleO

items.label: spec
items.statement:
The defining coefficient-boundedness and every-positive-coefficient
remainder characterization of a uniform finite jet family.
items.title: spec

items.label: sqrt
items.statement:
Square-root postcomposition preserves a real uniform finite jet family when
all constant coefficients equal one positive base value.
items.title: sqrt

items.label: value_eq_constantCoeff
items.statement:
At every parameter in the uniformity set, the function value at the base
equals the constant coefficient of its jet.
items.title: value_eq_constantCoeff

items.label: weightedPath
items.statement:
Restriction along `ε ↦ (ε, ε ^ 2)` turns a uniform two-variable finite jet
family at `(0, 0)` into a uniform one-variable jet family at zero.
items.title: weightedPath

items.label: along
items.statement:
Restrict a multivariable uniform jet remainder along uniformly bounded
scalar directions to obtain the scalar-path remainder predicate.
items.title: along

items.label: bound
items.statement:
A uniform jet remainder supplies an explicit common positive radius and its
associated bound.
items.title: bound

items.label: spec
items.statement: The defining common-radius characterization of a uniform jet remainder.
items.title: spec

items.label: ambientOrder_pos_of_index_pos
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: positivity of a retained coefficient implies positivity
of the ambient finite-jet order.
items.title: ambientOrder_pos_of_index_pos

items.label: analytic_mixed_cubic_quartic_isBigO
items.statement:
An analytic map has no mixed terms through degree four along a linear direction
and a cubic-quartic perturbation if its quadratic cross derivative in the linear and
cubic directions vanishes.
items.title: analytic_mixed_cubic_quartic_isBigO

items.label: coeff_add
items.statement: Coefficients of a sum jet are sums of the corresponding coefficients.
items.title: coeff_add

items.label: coeff_comp
items.statement:
A coefficient of a composed jet is the corresponding coefficient of the
normalized formal-series composition.
items.title: coeff_comp

items.label: coeff_comp_ofFunction_scalar
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (Finite-smooth invariant graph under an explicit stable
contraction): every coefficient of a scalar formal jet composition is the corresponding
coefficient of the derivative-constructed composite jet.
items.title: coeff_comp_ofFunction_scalar

items.label: coeff_ofFunction
items.statement:
The coefficients constructed by `ofFunction` are the normalized iterated
Fréchet derivatives.
items.title: coeff_ofFunction

items.label: coeff_ofFunction_apply
items.statement:
Evaluating a coefficient constructed by `ofFunction` evaluates the
corresponding factorial-normalized iterated Fréchet derivative.
items.title: coeff_ofFunction_apply

items.label: coeff_prod
items.statement: Coefficients of a paired jet are Cartesian products of coefficients.
items.title: coeff_prod

items.label: coeff_truncate
items.statement: Truncation retains every coefficient of degree at most `m`.
items.title: coeff_truncate

items.label: coeff_weightedPathJet
items.statement:
Coefficients of the weighted-path jet are its factorial-normalized iterated
Fréchet derivatives at zero.
items.title: coeff_weightedPathJet

items.label: comp_coeff_branch_split
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a finite-jet composition coefficient splits into a chosen
composition branch and the finite sum of all remaining branches.
items.title: comp_coeff_branch_split

items.label: comp_coeff_eq_of_eq_below
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a finite-jet composition coefficient is unchanged when
the outer coefficients and positive inner coefficients agree through that order.
items.title: comp_coeff_eq_of_eq_below

items.label: comp_coeff_eq_zero_of_inner_coeff_eq_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: if every positive inner coefficient through a retained
order vanishes, the corresponding coefficient of any finite-jet composition vanishes.
items.title: comp_coeff_eq_zero_of_inner_coeff_eq_zero

items.label: comp_coeff_eq_zero_of_outer_coeff_eq_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: if every outer coefficient of a finite
Taylor jet vanishes, every coefficient of its composition vanishes.
items.title: comp_coeff_eq_zero_of_outer_coeff_eq_zero

items.label: comp_coeff_eq_zero_of_outer_coeff_eq_zero_below
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: vanishing outer coefficients through a target order
forces the corresponding composition coefficient to vanish.
items.title: comp_coeff_eq_zero_of_outer_coeff_eq_zero_below

items.label: comp_coeff_outer_ones_apply
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating an all-ones outer branch at an arbitrary
retained coefficient exposes the outer coefficient at that branch length and the repeated
inner linear coefficient.
items.title: comp_coeff_outer_ones_apply

items.label: comp_coeff_outer_ones_apply_eq_coeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: an arbitrary all-ones branch evaluated on a repeated input
is exactly the outer coefficient gap applied to repeated inner linear coefficients.
items.title: comp_coeff_outer_ones_apply_eq_coeff

items.label: comp_coeff_sub_decompose_through_projections
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: simultaneous inner and outer coefficient changes split into
the inner one-block term, the projected inner residual, the outer all-ones branch, and the
projected outer residual at any positive retained order.
items.title: comp_coeff_sub_decompose_through_projections

items.label: comp_coeff_sub_eq_inner
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: at a positive retained order, agreement of two inner jets
below that order leaves only the one-block composition branch.
items.title: comp_coeff_sub_eq_inner

items.label: comp_coeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: when two inner jets have the same linear coefficient, an
arbitrary positive composition coefficient difference is exactly the sum of its non-all-ones
branches.
items.title: comp_coeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq

items.label: comp_coeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the arbitrary positive non-all-ones
composition difference on a repeated input commutes with the finite branch sum.
items.title: comp_coeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply

items.label: comp_coeff_sub_eq_outer
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: at a positive retained order, agreement of two outer jets
below that order leaves only the all-ones composition branch.
items.title: comp_coeff_sub_eq_outer

items.label: comp_coeff_sub_eq_outer_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: replacing an outer jet through an arbitrary retained
coefficient isolates its all-ones branch from the residual with the projected outer jet.
items.title: comp_coeff_sub_eq_outer_through_topProjection

items.label: comp_comp_coeff_sub_apply_eq_outer_of_lower
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a nested scalar composition evaluates the outer
coefficient gap on the inner linear coefficient after the scalar reindexing linear coefficient.
items.title: comp_comp_coeff_sub_apply_eq_outer_of_lower

items.label: comp_eval_sub_eval_eq_highDegreeSum
items.statement:
The discrepancy between nested jet evaluation and truncated composition is
the finite sum of composition terms whose total degree exceeds the cutoff.
items.title: comp_eval_sub_eval_eq_highDegreeSum

items.label: comp_ofFunction_one
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16 (Finite-order graph-jet contraction):
derivative-constructed jets commute with function composition at order one.
items.title: comp_ofFunction_one

items.label: comp_ofFunction_scalar
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16 (Finite-smooth invariant graph under an explicit stable contraction):
for a scalar source, derivative-constructed finite jets commute with composition in every
finite order.
items.title: comp_ofFunction_scalar

items.label: comp_ofFunction_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (Finite-order graph-jet contraction):
derivative-constructed jets commute with function composition at order zero.
items.title: comp_ofFunction_zero

items.label: comp_partialSum_eq_sum_filter
items.statement:
The partial sum of a formal-series composition is the portion of the
finite composition index set whose total degree is below the cutoff.
items.title: comp_partialSum_eq_sum_filter

items.label: comp_prod_comp_coeff_sub_eq_inner_of_lower
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a lower-equal product-valued inner variation passes through
an outer jet and a scalar reindexing jet at an arbitrary positive retained coefficient.
items.title: comp_prod_comp_coeff_sub_eq_inner_of_lower

items.label: comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_of_lower
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a lower-equal fiber-jet variation passes
through a product-valued inner jet and a scalar reindexing jet at the repeated-one
top coefficient.
items.title: comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_of_lower

items.label: comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_of_zeroTop
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a product inner jet with a zero-top projection
isolates the fiber top coefficient through two nested finite-jet compositions.
items.title: comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_of_zeroTop

items.label: comp_topCoeff_branch_split
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the top coefficient branch sum splits into a chosen
composition branch and the finite sum of all remaining branches.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_branch_split

items.label: comp_topCoeff_branch_sum
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the top coefficient of a finite jet composition is the
finite sum of its formal-series composition branches.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_branch_sum

items.label: comp_topCoeff_nonOnes_eq_zeroTopReplacement
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: replacing an outer jet's top coefficient by zero
isolates the non-all-ones branches of its top composition coefficient.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_nonOnes_eq_zeroTopReplacement

items.label: comp_topCoeff_outer_ones_apply
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the all-ones outer branch on a
constant direction exposes the outer coefficient at the branch length and the
repeated inner linear coefficient.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_outer_ones_apply

items.label: comp_topCoeff_outer_ones_eq_zero_of_topCoeff_eq
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the all-ones outer branch vanishes when two
outer finite jets have the same top coefficient.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_outer_ones_eq_zero_of_topCoeff_eq

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_eq_inner_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the projected top-coefficient identity on a
repeated direction preserves the outer linear term and the projected residual term.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_eq_inner_through_topProjection

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_decompose
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a top-coefficient secant of two finite
compositions splits through the mixed composition obtained by changing the
inner jet first and the outer jet second.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_decompose

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_decompose_through_projections
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a two-sided top-coefficient secant splits into
the inner linear term, the projected inner residual, the outer all-ones term,
and the projected outer residual.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_decompose_through_projections

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: if two inner jets agree below a positive top order,
the top coefficient of their common outer composition is the outer linear map
applied to the difference of their top coefficients.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_through_replacedTopCoeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the top-coefficient secant identity can
use the canonical jet obtained by replacing the source top coefficient.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_through_replacedTopCoeff

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: replacing an inner jet by a projected jet
isolates the outer linear top-order term and the remaining projected composition.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_inner_through_topProjection

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: when two inner jets have the same linear
coefficient, their top-composition difference is exactly the sum of the
non-all-ones branch differences.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the all-ones-cancelled top
coefficient difference on a repeated input commutes with the non-ones sum.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_outer
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: if two outer jets agree below the top order, the top
coefficient of their common inner composition is exactly the all-ones branch
of the outer formal-series difference.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_outer

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_outer_through_replacedTopCoeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the outer top-coefficient secant identity
uses the canonical jet obtained by replacing the outer source top coefficient.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_outer_through_replacedTopCoeff

items.label: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_outer_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: replacing only the top outer coefficient
isolates the all-ones branch from the remaining equal-top composition residual.
items.title: comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_outer_through_topProjection

items.label: compactContDiffAtTube
items.statement:
Pointwise finite-order differentiability along a compact fiber holds on
one common tube around that fiber.
items.title: compactContDiffAtTube

items.label: compactFiberEventually
items.statement:
Pointwise product-neighborhood control over a compact second factor becomes
uniform control in the first factor.
items.title: compactFiberEventually

items.label: compactFiberNormRadius
items.statement:
Product-neighborhood control over a compact parameter set holds on one
positive norm ball in the increment variable.
items.title: compactFiberNormRadius

items.label: compactIteratedFDerivOscillation
items.statement:
On a compact fiber, the top iterated derivative has one common radius on
which its variation in the second coordinate is uniformly small.
items.title: compactIteratedFDerivOscillation

items.label: compactValueOscillation
items.statement:
A function continuous along a compact fiber varies uniformly little in
the second coordinate on one common norm ball.
items.title: compactValueOscillation

items.label: constantCoeff_apply
items.statement: The constant coefficient is evaluation at the zero increment.
items.title: constantCoeff_apply

items.label: constantCoeff_comp
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: composing finite Taylor jets preserves the constant
coefficient of the outer jet.
items.title: constantCoeff_comp

items.label: constantCoeff_eq_coeff_zero
items.statement: Evaluation at zero retains exactly the degree-zero coefficient of a finite jet.
items.title: constantCoeff_eq_coeff_zero

items.label: constantCoeff_ofFunction
items.statement:
The constant coefficient of the derivative-constructed jet is the value of
the function at its expansion base.
items.title: constantCoeff_ofFunction

items.label: contDiffOne_comp_coeff
items.statement:
Coefficientwise `C¹` scalar-source finite jets remain coefficientwise
`C¹` after finite Taylor composition.
items.title: contDiffOne_comp_coeff

items.label: contDiffOne_multilinearMap_of_apply_one
items.statement:
A scalar-source multilinear-map family is `C¹` when its value on the
all-ones vector is `C¹`.
items.title: contDiffOne_multilinearMap_of_apply_one

items.label: continuous_comp_coeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: coefficientwise continuous scalar-source
jets remain coefficientwise continuous under finite Taylor composition.
items.title: continuous_comp_coeff

items.label: continuous_constantCoeff_of_coeff_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: continuity of degree-zero coefficient maps
implies continuity of the corresponding constant-coefficient family.
items.title: continuous_constantCoeff_of_coeff_zero

items.label: continuous_multilinearMap_of_apply_one
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a family of multilinear maps is continuous
when its evaluation on the all-ones vector is continuous.
items.title: continuous_multilinearMap_of_apply_one

items.label: continuous_ofFunction_coeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: coefficients of a finite jet built from a
smooth map vary continuously with the base point.
items.title: continuous_ofFunction_coeff

items.label: continuous_prod_coeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: coefficientwise continuous families of
finite jets remain coefficientwise continuous after pairing their values.
items.title: continuous_prod_coeff

items.label: continuous_scalarCoeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: scalar evaluation of a continuous
one-variable coefficient family is continuous.
items.title: continuous_scalarCoeff

items.label: deriv_comp_add_smul_of_differentiableAt
items.statement:
Differentiating a function along an affine line applies its Fréchet
derivative to the line direction.
items.title: deriv_comp_add_smul_of_differentiableAt

items.label: deriv_iteratedFDeriv_comp_add_smul
items.statement:
The derivative of a diagonal evaluation of an iterated Fréchet derivative
along a line is the next diagonal iterated derivative.
items.title: deriv_iteratedFDeriv_comp_add_smul

items.label: eq_iff_coeff_eq
items.statement: Equality of finite Taylor jets is coefficientwise equality.
items.title: eq_iff_coeff_eq

items.label: eq_of_eval_sub_isLittleO
items.statement:
Two one-variable finite jets are equal when the difference of their evaluations is
little-o of the top retained monomial.
items.title: eq_of_eval_sub_isLittleO

items.label: eq_replaceTopCoeff_of_coeff_eq
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a jet with the prescribed lower
coefficients and top coefficient is the corresponding top replacement.
items.title: eq_replaceTopCoeff_of_coeff_eq

items.label: eval_add
items.statement: Evaluation of a sum jet is the sum of the evaluations.
items.title: eval_add

items.label: eval_comp_eq_partialSum_comp
items.statement:
Evaluation of a truncated composition is the corresponding low-degree
partial sum of the untruncated formal-series composition.
items.title: eval_comp_eq_partialSum_comp

items.label: eval_eq_partialSum
items.statement: Jet evaluation agrees with the canonical partial sum of its zero extension.
items.title: eval_eq_partialSum

items.label: eval_eq_sum
items.statement: Evaluation is the finite sum of the diagonal coefficient values.
items.title: eval_eq_sum

items.label: eval_eq_sum_smul_scalarCoeff
items.statement:
For a one-variable jet, evaluation is the power sum of its scalar
coefficients.
items.title: eval_eq_sum_smul_scalarCoeff

items.label: eval_ofFunction_zero
items.statement: The order-zero derivative jet evaluates to the base value at every increment.
items.title: eval_ofFunction_zero

items.label: eval_of_hasFPowerSeriesOnBall
items.statement:
A convergent analytic power series evaluates the derivative-constructed jet
as its corresponding finite partial sum.
items.title: eval_of_hasFPowerSeriesOnBall

items.label: eval_sub_constantCoeff_eq_sum_Ico
items.statement:
Subtracting a jet's constant coefficient leaves exactly its positive-degree
formal-series partial sum.
items.title: eval_sub_constantCoeff_eq_sum_Ico

items.label: exists_compEvalTailBound
items.statement:
Uniform coefficient bounds give a uniform order-`m+1` bound for the
high-degree tail discarded by finite-jet composition on the unit ball.
items.title: exists_compEvalTailBound

items.label: ext_coeff
items.statement: A finite Taylor jet is determined coefficientwise.
items.title: ext_coeff

items.label: inv_def
items.statement: Reciprocal jets are obtained by postcomposition with inversion.
items.title: inv_def

items.label: isUniformOn_of_contDiff
items.statement:
A jointly `C^m` family on a compact parameter set produces a uniform family
of derivative-constructed order-`m` finite jets at every fixed input base.
items.title: isUniformOn_of_contDiff

items.label: isUniformOn_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
Joint finite-order differentiability at every point of a compact parameter fiber
produces a uniform family of derivative-constructed finite jets at the fixed input base.
items.title: isUniformOn_of_contDiffAt

items.label: iteratedDeriv_comp_add_smul
items.statement:
Iterated derivatives of an affine-line restriction are diagonal evaluations
of the corresponding iterated Fréchet derivatives.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_comp_add_smul

items.label: iteratedDeriv_factorialInv_pow_smul
items.statement:
The top iterated derivative of a factorial-normalized vector monomial is
the constant vector coefficient.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_factorialInv_pow_smul

items.label: iteratedDeriv_factorialInv_pow_smul_zero
items.statement:
Every derivative below the degree of a factorial-normalized vector
monomial vanishes at zero.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_factorialInv_pow_smul_zero

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_comp_eq_taylorComp
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (finite-order graph-jet contraction): the iterated derivative
of a composite is the Faa di Bruno Taylor composition of the two derivative series.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_comp_eq_taylorComp

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_slice_eq_comp_inr_at
items.statement:
The derivative of a fixed-parameter slice is the joint derivative restricted
to the canonical right inclusion, assuming only pointwise finite smoothness.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_slice_eq_comp_inr_at

items.label: mul_def
items.statement:
Multiplication of jets is postcomposition of their paired jet by algebra
multiplication.
items.title: mul_def

items.label: norm_coeff_comp_le
items.statement:
Uniform bounds for the coefficients of two jets bound each coefficient of
their truncated formal-series composition by an explicit finite sum.
items.title: norm_coeff_comp_le

items.label: norm_comp_coeff_outer_ones_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the norm of an arbitrary retained all-ones branch is bounded
by the outer coefficient gap times the corresponding power of the inner linear coefficient.
items.title: norm_comp_coeff_outer_ones_le

items.label: norm_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_decompose_through_projections
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the simultaneous projection estimate on a
repeated direction multiplies the four coefficient bounds by the corresponding direction power.
items.title: norm_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_decompose_through_projections

items.label: norm_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_outer_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the arbitrary-order outer projection estimate on a
repeated input contributes exactly the retained-degree power of the input norm.
items.title: norm_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_outer_through_topProjection

items.label: norm_comp_coeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: branchwise bounds on arbitrary retained non-all-ones
composition terms give a direct norm bound for the coefficient difference.
items.title: norm_comp_coeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply_le

items.label: norm_comp_coeff_sub_le_decompose_through_projections
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the simultaneous arbitrary-order projection decomposition has
a four-term norm estimate, with the two distinguished branches isolated explicitly.
items.title: norm_comp_coeff_sub_le_decompose_through_projections

items.label: norm_comp_coeff_sub_le_outer_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the arbitrary-order outer projection decomposition has a norm
bound given by the all-ones coefficient gap and the projected composition residual.
items.title: norm_comp_coeff_sub_le_outer_through_topProjection

items.label: norm_comp_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_outer_of_lower
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a nested scalar composition transports a lower-equal
outer top-coefficient bound to repeated inputs with explicit inner and reindexing factors.
items.title: norm_comp_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_outer_of_lower

items.label: norm_comp_prod_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_inner_of_lower
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the arbitrary-order product-composition projection has a
repeated-input norm bound separating the scalar reindexing factor, the outer linear coefficient,
and the retained inner coefficient gap.
items.title: norm_comp_prod_comp_coeff_sub_apply_le_inner_of_lower

items.label: norm_comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_of_lower
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the lower-equal product-composition
identity has a repeated-input norm bound separating the reindexing factor,
the inner linear coefficient, and the fiber top-coefficient gap.
items.title: norm_comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_of_lower

items.label: norm_comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_of_zeroTop
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the zero-top projected nested composition is bounded
by the repeated scalar coefficient, the outer linear coefficient, and the fiber top gap.
items.title: norm_comp_prod_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_of_zeroTop

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_outer_ones_apply_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: evaluating the all-ones composition branch on a repeated
input is bounded by the outer top-coefficient gap and the scaled inner linear coefficient.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_outer_ones_apply_le

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_through_replacedTopCoeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the canonical inner top-coefficient replacement gives
the projected secant estimate after evaluation on a repeated input.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_through_replacedTopCoeff

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the projected inner top-coefficient estimate remains valid
after evaluation on a repeated input, with the expected power of its norm.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_inner_through_topProjection

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_outer_through_replacedTopCoeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the canonical outer top-coefficient replacement gives
the outer secant estimate after evaluation on a repeated input.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_outer_through_replacedTopCoeff

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_outer_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the projected outer top-coefficient estimate remains valid
after evaluation on a repeated input, with the expected power of its norm.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_apply_le_outer_through_topProjection

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a branchwise norm bound for the repeated-input
top-coefficient difference after the all-ones branch has been cancelled.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_eq_nonOnes_of_inner_linear_eq_apply_le

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_decompose_through_projections
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the four projected top-coefficient branches
have a norm estimate in which the inner and outer one-block terms are
controlled by their respective coefficient gaps.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_decompose_through_projections

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_inner
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the inner top-coefficient variation is bounded by
the norm of the outer linear coefficient times the inner top-coefficient gap.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_inner

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_inner_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the projected-inner top-coefficient identity
gives a norm estimate with the outer linear coefficient and projected remainder.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_inner_through_topProjection

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_outer
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: with a fixed inner jet, the top-coefficient variation
is bounded by the outer top-coefficient gap times the `m`-th power of the
inner linear coefficient norm.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_outer

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_outer_through_replacedTopCoeff
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the canonical outer replacement gives the
outer one-block norm bound together with its projected composition residual.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_outer_through_replacedTopCoeff

items.label: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_outer_through_topProjection
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the outer projected top-coefficient identity
admits a norm bound by the outer top gap and the projected residual.
items.title: norm_comp_topCoeff_sub_le_outer_through_topProjection

items.label: norm_continuousMultilinearCurryFin1_apply_zero_pair_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a one-variable curry of a multilinear map
is bounded on a pair with zero first component by the map norm times the
second-component norm.
items.title: norm_continuousMultilinearCurryFin1_apply_zero_pair_le

items.label: norm_def
items.statement: Norm jets are obtained by postcomposition with the norm function.
items.title: norm_def

items.label: norm_eval_sub_eval_le
items.statement:
The change in a finite jet evaluation is bounded by its coefficient norms
and the distance between the two inputs.
items.title: norm_eval_sub_eval_le

items.label: norm_formalSub_onesLength
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the all-ones composition selects the top finite-jet
coefficient of a formal-series difference after taking norms.
items.title: norm_formalSub_onesLength

items.label: norm_formal_onesProduct
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the norms of the inner factors selected by an
all-ones composition multiply to the power of the inner linear coefficient.
items.title: norm_formal_onesProduct

items.label: norm_formal_onesProduct_general
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the all-ones blocks at an arbitrary retained degree select
the inner linear coefficient, so their norms multiply to the retained-degree power.
items.title: norm_formal_onesProduct_general

items.label: norm_iteratedDeriv_radial_sub_le
items.statement:
An operator-norm oscillation bound for a joint iterated derivative bounds
the corresponding scalar radial derivative difference.
items.title: norm_iteratedDeriv_radial_sub_le

items.label: norm_taylorRemainder_le_of_iteratedFDerivOscillation
items.statement:
Oscillation of the top joint derivative along a radial segment controls
the successor-order Taylor-jet remainder of the corresponding slice.
items.title: norm_taylorRemainder_le_of_iteratedFDerivOscillation

items.label: norm_toFormalMultilinearSeries_le
items.statement:
A degreewise bound on a finite jet also bounds every retained coefficient
of its zero-extended formal multilinear series.
items.title: norm_toFormalMultilinearSeries_le

items.label: ofFunction_add_congr
items.statement: Equality of two pairs of one-variable jets is preserved by pointwise addition.
items.title: ofFunction_add_congr

items.label: ofFunction_coeff_comp_eq_taylorComp
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (finite-order graph-jet contraction): a derivative-constructed
jet coefficient of a composite is the factorial-normalized Faa di Bruno coefficient.
items.title: ofFunction_coeff_comp_eq_taylorComp

items.label: ofFunction_comp_cubic_quartic
items.statement:
Along a path whose first nonconstant terms have degrees three and four, the
four-jet of an analytic map only sees its value and first derivative at the base point.
items.title: ofFunction_comp_cubic_quartic

items.label: ofFunction_comp_eq_normalizedTaylorCompJet
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (finite-order graph-jet contraction): under finite
smoothness, the derivative-constructed composite jet is the normalized Faa di Bruno jet.
items.title: ofFunction_comp_eq_normalizedTaylorCompJet

items.label: ofFunction_composite_coeff_sub_decompose
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (finite-order graph-jet contraction): a composite secant
coefficient splits into an inner-map variation followed by an outer-map variation at the
Faa di Bruno Taylor-series level.
items.title: ofFunction_composite_coeff_sub_decompose

items.label: ofFunction_composite_coeff_sub_eq_taylorComp_sub
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (finite-order graph-jet contraction): a secant of
derivative-constructed composite coefficients is the factorial-normalized secant of the
corresponding Faa di Bruno Taylor compositions.
items.title: ofFunction_composite_coeff_sub_eq_taylorComp_sub

items.label: ofFunction_eq_iff_iteratedDeriv_eq
items.statement:
Two derivative-constructed one-variable jets agree exactly when their
iterated derivatives agree through the truncation order.
items.title: ofFunction_eq_iff_iteratedDeriv_eq

items.label: ofFunction_eq_of_eventuallyEq
items.statement: Functions equal in a neighborhood of their common base have equal finite Taylor jets there.
items.title: ofFunction_eq_of_eventuallyEq

items.label: ofFunction_eq_of_sub_isBigO_succ
items.statement: A difference of order `O(h ^ (m + 1))` is invisible to the order-`m` finite jets.
items.title: ofFunction_eq_of_sub_isBigO_succ

items.label: ofFunction_eq_of_sub_isLittleO
items.statement:
If two `C^m` one-variable functions, based at possibly different points, differ by
`o(h ^ m)` after translation to zero, then their order-`m` finite jets agree.
items.title: ofFunction_eq_of_sub_isLittleO

items.label: ofFunction_eq_zeroFunction_iff
items.statement:
The finite jet of a one-variable function is the zero-function jet exactly
when all iterated derivatives through the truncation order vanish.
items.title: ofFunction_eq_zeroFunction_iff

items.label: ofFunction_prodMk
items.statement: The finite jet of a product-valued function is the product of its component jets.
items.title: ofFunction_prodMk

items.label: ofFunction_prodMk_eq_zero
items.statement: A product of two functions with zero finite jets again has zero finite jet.
items.title: ofFunction_prodMk_eq_zero

items.label: ofFunction_split_of_isBigO_succ
items.statement:
If `f = s + t - c + O(h^(m+1))` near the expansion point, then order-`m` jet
identities for the three pieces assemble into the corresponding identity for `f`.
items.title: ofFunction_split_of_isBigO_succ

items.label: ofFunction_sub_congr
items.statement: Equality of two pairs of one-variable jets is preserved by pointwise subtraction.
items.title: ofFunction_sub_congr

items.label: ofFunction_sub_eq_zero_of_eq
items.statement: Equal jets have a difference whose finite jet is the zero jet.
items.title: ofFunction_sub_eq_zero_of_eq

items.label: partialSum_five_mixed_cubic_quartic_isBigO
items.statement:
For a formal power series, the mixed part of its degree-four partial sum along
`ε • u + ε³ • v₃ + ε⁴ • v₄` is order five when the quadratic cross coefficient
in the `(u, v₃)` directions vanishes.
items.title: partialSum_five_mixed_cubic_quartic_isBigO

items.label: postcomp_def
items.statement:
Analytic postcomposition is normalized formal-series composition with the
outer derivative jet.
items.title: postcomp_def

items.label: remainder_def
items.statement: The remainder is the function value at `x + h` minus the evaluated jet.
items.title: remainder_def

items.label: remainder_ofFunction_isLittleO
items.statement:
The derivative-constructed one-variable finite jet has Peano remainder
`o(h ^ m)` at its expansion point.
items.title: remainder_ofFunction_isLittleO

items.label: replaceTopCoeff_coeff_of_lt
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the replacement jet agrees with the source
jet at every degree strictly below the top order.
items.title: replaceTopCoeff_coeff_of_lt

items.label: replaceTopCoeff_coeff_top
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the replacement jet has exactly the
requested coefficient at its top order.
items.title: replaceTopCoeff_coeff_top

items.label: scalarCoeff_apply
items.statement:
A scalar jet coefficient is its multilinear coefficient evaluated on the
all-ones vector.
items.title: scalarCoeff_apply

items.label: scalarCoeff_eq_of_eval_sub_isLittleO
items.statement:
If the diagonal evaluations of two one-variable jets differ by `o(h ^ m)`,
then all of their scalar coefficients through degree `m` agree.
items.title: scalarCoeff_eq_of_eval_sub_isLittleO

items.label: scalarCoeff_ofFunction
items.statement:
The scalar coefficients of `ofFunction` are normalized iterated
one-variable derivatives.
items.title: scalarCoeff_ofFunction

items.label: sqrt_def
items.statement: Square-root jets are obtained by postcomposition with `Real.sqrt`.
items.title: sqrt_def

items.label: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_le
items.statement:
The zero extension agrees with the jet coefficient in every degree at most
`m`.
items.title: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_le

items.label: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_lt
items.statement:
The formal multilinear series associated to a finite jet vanishes in every
degree strictly above `m`.
items.title: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_lt

items.label: uniformCoeffBounds_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
Pointwise joint `C^m` regularity on a compact parameter set gives one
uniform norm bound for every factorial-normalized Taylor coefficient.
items.title: uniformCoeffBounds_of_contDiffAt

items.label: uniformJetData_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
The compact-fiber coefficient bounds and the standard uniform remainder
estimate can be consumed together as the two clauses of a uniform jet proof.
items.title: uniformJetData_of_contDiffAt

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticAt
items.statement:
If a family is jointly analytic at every point of a compact parameter
fiber, its factorial-normalized finite Taylor jets have a uniform Peano
remainder bound there.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticAt

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticOnNhd
items.statement:
A jointly analytic family has factorial-normalized order-`m` Taylor jets
whose Peano remainders satisfy every positive order-`m` coefficient bound uniformly on
a compact parameter set.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticOnNhd

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiff
items.statement:
A jointly `C^m` family has factorial-normalized order-`m` Taylor jets whose
Peano remainders satisfy every positive order-`m` coefficient bound uniformly on a
compact parameter set.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiff

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
If a family is jointly `C^m` at every point of a compact parameter fiber,
its factorial-normalized order-`m` Taylor jets have a uniform Peano remainder
bound there.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiffAt

items.label: uniform_orderFive_bound_of_zero_fourJet
items.statement:
A jointly `C⁵` scalar-path family whose order-four jets vanish has a
uniform fifth-order norm bound on every compact parameter set.
items.title: uniform_orderFive_bound_of_zero_fourJet

items.label: div_eq_div_of_eq_pow_mul
items.statement:
Exact factorizations by a common power have equal residual and original quotients
away from zero.
items.title: div_eq_div_of_eq_pow_mul

items.label: exists_norm_fderiv_le
items.statement:
The first derivative of a compactly supported `C^1` function admits a nonnegative
global operator-norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_fderiv_le

items.label: exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_le
items.statement:
Every fixed iterated derivative of a compactly supported `C^n` function admits a
nonnegative global norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_le

items.label: exists_norm_secondFDeriv_le
items.statement:
The second derivative of a compactly supported `C^2` function admits a nonnegative
global operator-norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_secondFDeriv_le

items.label: indicator_compl_of_mem
items.statement:
At a point in the complement of a closed set, extending a function by zero across the
set preserves its certified Frechet derivative.
items.title: indicator_compl_of_mem

items.label: contDiff_update_succ_top
items.statement: The updated Taylor witness immediately gives finite smoothness of the updated function.
items.title: contDiff_update_succ_top

items.label: update_succ_top
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a (finite-smooth invariant graph): replace only the
top formal Taylor term while retaining a predecessor Taylor series.
items.title: update_succ_top

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement: A certified gradient pulls back by the adjoint of a continuous linear equivalence.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: indicator_compl_of_mem
items.statement:
At a point in the complement of a closed set, extending a scalar function by zero
across the set preserves its certified gradient.
items.title: indicator_compl_of_mem

items.label: at
items.statement: A global Hessian bound specializes at every point.
items.title: at

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement: Relative norm bounds on a coordinate map transport global Hessian bounds.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: comp_linearIsometryEquiv
items.statement: Hessian bounds are invariant under an isometric linear change of coordinates.
items.title: comp_linearIsometryEquiv

items.label: of_forall
items.statement: Pointwise Hessian bounds at every point assemble into a global Hessian bound.
items.title: of_forall

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement: Relative norm bounds on a coordinate map transport pointwise Hessian bounds.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: of_quadraticForm
items.statement:
A self-adjoint Hessian satisfying quadratic-form inequalities has the corresponding
Loewner bounds.
items.title: of_quadraticForm

items.label: quadraticForm
items.statement: Loewner Hessian bounds imply the corresponding quadratic-form inequalities.
items.title: quadraticForm

items.label: contDiffAt_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
Adding a twice continuously differentiable perturbation to half the squared distance
preserves twice continuous differentiability at the base point.
items.title: contDiffAt_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: fderiv_gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
The Hessian of a translated squared norm plus a twice continuously differentiable
perturbation is the identity operator plus the perturbation Hessian.
items.title: fderiv_gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
The gradient of a translated squared norm plus a differentiable perturbation is the
displacement vector plus the perturbation gradient.
items.title: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hasGradientAt
items.statement:
Under a perturbation gradient certificate, the canonical gradient of the translated
quadratic plus the perturbation is the displacement plus the certified gradient.
items.title: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hasGradientAt

items.label: halfNormSq_sub_add_apply_of_eq_zero
items.statement:

unchanged there.

items.label: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
A certified perturbation gradient adds to the displacement gradient of the translated
quadratic base.
items.title: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: hasHessianBoundsAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le
items.statement:
An operator-norm bound on a perturbation Hessian gives pointwise two-sided Loewner
bounds for half the squared distance plus that perturbation.

items.label: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le
items.statement:
A uniform perturbation-Hessian norm bound gives global two-sided Loewner bounds for
half the squared distance plus the perturbation.
items.title: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le

items.label: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_secondFDeriv_norm_le
items.statement:

global two-sided Hessian bounds for a quadratic base plus a perturbation.

items.statement:
The Hessian of half the squared distance plus a `C²` perturbation is the identity
operator plus the perturbation Hessian.

items.statement:
A global Hessian norm bound below one makes a quadratic base plus the perturbation

items.label: strongConvexOn_halfNormSq_add_of_secondFDeriv_norm_le
items.statement:

items.label: contDiff_two_indicator_compl
items.statement:
A twice continuously differentiable function off a closed set extends by zero to a
globally twice continuously differentiable function when its value, first derivative, and
second derivative vanish at the corresponding distance-scaled rates.
items.title: contDiff_two_indicator_compl

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl
items.statement:
If a function and its first derivative decay at the required rates toward a closed set,
then the second derivative of its extension by zero is the extension by zero of its second
derivative.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The second Fréchet derivative of a zero extension vanishes identically on the closed
set when the source value and first derivative have the required second-order decay.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension has vanishing second Fréchet derivative at every point of the closed
set when the source value and first derivative satisfy the second-order extension decay.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl
items.statement:
The derivative of the extension by zero off a closed set agrees with the extension of
the derivative when the function is differentiable off the set and decays faster than the
distance to the set.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The first derivative of a zero extension vanishes identically on the closed set when
the source function has the required first-order distance decay.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay
items.statement:
Quadratic value decay is sufficient for the first derivative of a zero extension to
vanish identically on the closed set.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension has vanishing first derivative at every point of the closed set
when the source function has the distance-scaled value decay required for extension.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The gradient of a scalar-valued zero extension vanishes identically on the closed set
when the source function has the required first-order distance decay.
items.title: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay
items.statement:
Quadratic value decay is sufficient for the gradient of a scalar-valued zero extension
to vanish identically on the closed set.
items.title: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay

items.label: gradient_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension has zero Euclidean gradient at every point of the closed set under the
same first-order value decay hypothesis.
items.title: gradient_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: union_range_of_mapClusterPt

A closed set containing every `atTop` cluster point of a sequence remains closed after
adjoining the sequence's range.
items.title: union_range_of_mapClusterPt

coefficient family of the differentiated jet is bounded.

norm inequality with a little-o additive error.

items.label: isLittleO_of_norm_le_of_isLittleO_bridge

Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: an eventual scalar envelope that is little-o of a comparison

items.label: isLittleO_shift_of_uniform_remainder

Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a uniform translated-remainder estimate gives the
corresponding little-o statement at each base point.
items.title: isLittleO_shift_of_uniform_remainder

items.label: map_apply
items.statement: The cone-valued graph transform evaluates to the inverse-center pointwise formula.
items.title: map_apply

items.label: map_spec

The cone-valued graph transform satisfies the origin, radius, and Lipschitz
constraints.
items.title: map_spec

items.label: predecessorHasDerivAt_of_rawDefectLittleO
items.statement:
A translated first-order remainder that is little-o of its scalar increment
determines the corresponding derivative at every base point.
items.title: predecessorHasDerivAt_of_rawDefectLittleO

items.label: radiusEnvelope_sublinear_of_recurrence
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a monotone radius envelope with a locally bounded affine
recurrence is sublinear at zero when the weighted transport factor is below
one.
items.title: radiusEnvelope_sublinear_of_recurrence

items.label: rate_def
items.statement:
The contraction coefficient is the sum of the direct stable term and the term caused
by variation of the inverse center parameter.
items.title: rate_def

items.label: rawDefect_isLittleO_of_inverseRecurrence
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a locally uniformly bounded raw defect satisfying a uniformly
small inverse-coordinate affine recurrence is little-o of its scalar increment at every base
point, provided both the recurrence factor and its transported factor are strict contractions.
items.title: rawDefect_isLittleO_of_inverseRecurrence

items.label: raw_apply
items.statement:
The raw graph transform evaluates to the stable coordinate at the inverse center
parameter.
items.title: raw_apply

items.label: raw_continuous
items.statement:
The inverse-center graph-transform formula is continuous under the quantitative
Lipschitz hypotheses.
items.title: raw_continuous

items.label: raw_lipschitzWith
items.statement:
The inverse-center formula obeys the prescribed graph Lipschitz constant under the
split stable estimate.
items.title: raw_lipschitzWith

items.label: raw_norm_le
items.statement:
The stable block bound, the stable remainder bound, and the radius inequality give
the pointwise radius estimate for the raw graph transform.
items.title: raw_norm_le

items.label: raw_zero
items.statement:
If the nonlinear term fixes the origin, then the raw graph transform fixes the
origin.
items.title: raw_zero

items.label: tendsto_boundedSection_of_tendsto_operator_residual
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a strict bounded-section contraction turns a
vanishing operator residual into convergence toward its canonical fixed section.
items.title: tendsto_boundedSection_of_tendsto_operator_residual

items.label: toBoundedContinuousFunction_apply
items.statement:
The bounded continuous graph transform evaluates to the raw graph-transform
formula.
items.title: toBoundedContinuousFunction_apply

items.label: toBoundedContinuousFunction_norm_le
items.statement: The bounded continuous graph transform has norm at most the cone radius.
items.title: toBoundedContinuousFunction_norm_le

items.label: topSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv_of_derivative
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure C: a top section satisfying the predecessor
derivative equation is the unnormalised next iterated derivative of the graph.
items.title: topSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv_of_derivative

items.label: uniformTranslatedFirstOrderRemainderOn
items.statement:
First-order Taylor remainders of translated `C¹` functions are uniform
when their translation centers range over a compact set.
items.title: uniformTranslatedFirstOrderRemainderOn

items.label: centerStableLinearize_apply
items.statement:
The center-stable cutoff perturbation evaluates as its block-linear part plus the
rescaled cutoff remainder.
items.title: centerStableLinearize_apply

items.label: centerStableLinearize_eq_linear
items.statement:
Outside the topological support of the rescaled cutoff, the center-stable cutoff
perturbation equals its block-linear part.
items.title: centerStableLinearize_eq_linear

items.label: centerStableLinearize_eventuallyEq
items.statement:
A cutoff equal to one near zero makes the center-stable cutoff perturbation and the
original nonlinear center-stable map have the same germ at zero.
items.title: centerStableLinearize_eventuallyEq

items.label: centerStable_apply
items.statement: The center-stable block map sends `(u, z)` to `(u, L z)`.
items.title: centerStable_apply

items.label: contDiff_linearize
items.statement:
Local `C^ν` regularity on an open neighborhood of the rescaled cutoff support
suffices for the cutoff perturbation to be globally `C^ν`.
items.title: contDiff_linearize

items.label: exists_scale_norm_fderiv_remainder_le
items.statement:
Under explicit first-order remainder and derivative bounds, shrinking a compact
`C¹` cutoff makes the derivative of the cutoff remainder uniformly small.
items.title: exists_scale_norm_fderiv_remainder_le

items.label: fderiv_linearize_zero
items.statement:
If the nonlinear map has zero value and derivative at zero, then a differentiable
rescaled cutoff perturbation has derivative `A` there.
items.title: fderiv_linearize_zero

items.label: hasCompactSupport_remainder
items.statement:
A nonzero rescaling of a compactly supported cutoff produces a compactly supported
cutoff remainder.
items.title: hasCompactSupport_remainder

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_linearize_zero
items.statement:
Every iterated Fréchet derivative at zero is preserved by a cutoff equal to one
near zero.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_linearize_zero

items.label: linearize_apply
items.statement: The cutoff perturbation evaluates as `A x + χ (ρ⁻¹ • x) • N x`.
items.title: linearize_apply

items.label: linearize_eq_add_of_mem_closedBall
items.statement:
On the scaled inner closed ball, a plateau cutoff perturbation agrees with
`x ↦ A x + N x`.
items.title: linearize_eq_add_of_mem_closedBall

items.label: linearize_eq_linear_of_outer_radius_le_norm
items.statement:
At and beyond the scaled outer radius, a cutoff perturbation agrees with its
linear part.
items.title: linearize_eq_linear_of_outer_radius_le_norm

items.label: linearize_eventuallyEq
items.statement:
A cutoff equal to one near zero makes the cutoff perturbation and the original
nonlinear map have the same germ at zero.
items.title: linearize_eventuallyEq

items.label: linearize_zero
items.statement: A cutoff perturbation fixes zero when its nonlinear remainder vanishes there.
items.title: linearize_zero

items.label: remainder_apply
items.statement: The rescaled cutoff remainder evaluates as `χ (ρ⁻¹ • x) • N x`.
items.title: remainder_apply

items.label: boundedTransform_apply

formula.
items.title: boundedTransform_apply

items.label: centerMap_zero

items.label: exists_metricFixedGraph

fixed graph.  This theorem is intentionally metric, and finite `C^ν` regularity is supplied by the
separate finite-smooth bootstrap.

items.label: exists_metricTransformParameters

A stable contraction rate admits metric graph-transform parameters satisfying all finite-order
bunching inequalities.
items.title: exists_metricTransformParameters

items.label: fixedGraph_equation

in the original center parameter, before any smoothness or tangent argument is applied.

items.label: fixedGraph_lipschitzWith_sharp

Lipschitz constant.
items.title: fixedGraph_lipschitzWith_sharp

items.label: inverseCenter_centerMap

items.title: inverseCenter_centerMap

items.label: inverseCenter_dist_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: inverse centers of two graphs satisfy the uniform
cross-graph estimate required for contraction.
items.title: inverseCenter_dist_le

items.label: inverseCenter_eq

items.title: inverseCenter_eq

items.label: inverseCenter_lipschitzWith

items.title: inverseCenter_lipschitzWith

items.label: inverseCenter_zero

items.title: inverseCenter_zero

items.statement:

radius.
items.title: norm_boundedTransform_le

items.label: norm_deriv_fixedGraph_le_sharp
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the derivative of a metric fixed graph is bounded by
the sharp Lipschitz constant at every center coordinate.
items.title: norm_deriv_fixedGraph_le_sharp

items.label: norm_rawTransform_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: every raw transform value stays inside the prescribed
uniform graph radius.
items.title: norm_rawTransform_le

items.label: one_sub_mul_pow_lower_bound

Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: Bernoulli's lower bound for powers of a number in
the unit interval.
items.title: one_sub_mul_pow_lower_bound

items.label: rawTransform_continuous
items.statement: Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the raw metric graph transform is continuous.
items.title: rawTransform_continuous

items.label: rawTransform_dist_apply_le
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: two raw metric transforms satisfy the explicit
graph-distance estimate encoded by `metricGraphTransformRate`.
items.title: rawTransform_dist_apply_le

items.label: rawTransform_eq
items.statement: The raw metric transform has its defining inverse-center formula.
items.title: rawTransform_eq

items.label: rawTransform_lipschitzWith
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the sharp raw-transform estimate and the cone inequality
show that the metric graph transform preserves the prescribed Lipschitz cone.
items.title: rawTransform_lipschitzWith

items.label: rawTransform_lipschitzWith_sharp
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the raw metric graph transform has the sharp Lipschitz
constant obtained from the stable linear rate, graph slope, remainder size, and inverse-center
bound.
items.title: rawTransform_lipschitzWith_sharp

items.label: rawTransform_zero
items.statement: Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the raw metric graph transform fixes zero.
items.title: rawTransform_zero

items.label: transform_apply
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the bundled metric transform evaluates by its raw
inverse-center formula.
items.title: transform_apply
