items.statement:
For a Hermitian base matrix, the inverse-form DFP update commutes with an
orthogonal change of coordinates.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_conjugate_of_mem_orthogonalGroup

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_def
items.statement:
The inverse-form DFP update is the sum of its base matrix and the two
rank-one correction terms.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_def

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_denominators_ne_zero_smul_iff
items.statement:
A common nonzero scale preserves exactly the two nonvanishing denominator
conditions used by the inverse-form DFP update.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_denominators_ne_zero_smul_iff

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_dotProduct_mulVec
items.statement:
The quadratic form of an inverse-form DFP update, before using symmetry of the
base matrix.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_dotProduct_mulVec

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_dotProduct_mulVec_of_isHermitian
items.statement:
For a Hermitian real base matrix, the quadratic form of the inverse-form DFP
update is the usual difference and sum of two scalar squares.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_dotProduct_mulVec_of_isHermitian

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_isHermitian
items.statement: An inverse-form DFP update of a Hermitian real matrix is Hermitian.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_isHermitian

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_metric_denominator_smul
items.statement:
Simultaneously scaling both vectors in a secant pair scales the quadratic
denominator involving the base matrix by the square of the scalar.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_metric_denominator_smul

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_mulVec_apply
items.statement: The action of the inverse-form DFP update on a vector, expanded at one coordinate.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_mulVec_apply

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_mulVec_secant
items.statement:
If both update denominators are nonzero, the inverse-form DFP update sends
the secant vector `y` to the displacement vector `s`.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_mulVec_secant

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_mulVec_smul_secant
items.statement:
Under the original nonvanishing denominator hypotheses, the update formed
from a scaled secant pair sends `c • y` to `c • s`.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_mulVec_smul_secant

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_secant_denominator_pos_smul_iff
items.statement: A common nonzero scale preserves positivity of the secant curvature.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_secant_denominator_pos_smul_iff

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_secant_denominator_smul
items.statement:
Simultaneously scaling both vectors in a secant pair scales its curvature
denominator by the square of the scalar.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_secant_denominator_smul

items.label: inverseDFPUpdate_smul_pair
items.statement:
The inverse-form DFP update is unchanged when both vectors of the secant
pair are multiplied by the same nonzero scalar.
items.title: inverseDFPUpdate_smul_pair

items.label: isPositive_toEuclideanCLM_iff
items.statement: A real matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when its Euclidean operator is positive.
items.title: isPositive_toEuclideanCLM_iff

items.label: norm_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_mem_orthogonalGroup
items.statement:
An orthogonal matrix preserves the Euclidean norm under matrix-vector
multiplication.
items.title: norm_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_mem_orthogonalGroup

items.label: norm_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup
items.statement: A special orthogonal matrix preserves the Euclidean norm.
items.title: norm_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.label: posDef_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A strict scalar Loewner lower bound makes a real finite matrix positive definite.
items.title: posDef_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: posDef_of_quadraticForm_lowerBound
items.statement:
A Hermitian real matrix with a strictly positive quadratic-form lower bound is positive
definite.
items.title: posDef_of_quadraticForm_lowerBound

items.label: toEuclideanCLM_inverseDFPUpdate
items.statement:
The Euclidean operator represented by a matrix DFP update is the coordinate-free operator
DFP update.
items.title: toEuclideanCLM_inverseDFPUpdate

items.label: affinity_unitSphere
items.statement:
The affine image of the unit sphere with center `C` and positive scale `R` is the
metric sphere of radius `R` about `C`.
items.title: affinity_unitSphere

items.label: disjoint_closedBall_of_pointwise_lower_bound
items.statement:
A pointwise distance lower bound separates every strictly smaller closed ball from the
punctured set carrying that bound.
items.title: disjoint_closedBall_of_pointwise_lower_bound

items.label: eventually_closedBall_subset_cthickening_of_tendsto
items.statement:
If both the center distance to a closed nonempty target and the radii tend
to zero, every positive closed thickening of the target eventually contains
the corresponding closed balls.
items.title: eventually_closedBall_subset_cthickening_of_tendsto

items.label: eventually_infDist_mem_Icc_of_support_radius_isLittleO
items.statement:
If center-to-target distance is asymptotic to a positive multiple of a
scale and the support radii are negligible relative to that distance, then
every point in the corresponding supports has target distance comparable to
the same scale.
items.title: eventually_infDist_mem_Icc_of_support_radius_isLittleO

items.label: half_dist_le_of_mem_isolationClosedBall
items.statement:
Points in subsets of distinct quarter-isolation closed balls are separated by at least
half the distance between the centers.
items.title: half_dist_le_of_mem_isolationClosedBall

items.label: infDist_affinity_unitSphere
items.statement:
The distance from a point to the affine image of a unit sphere with positive scale is
the absolute difference between its distance from the center and the scale.
items.title: infDist_affinity_unitSphere

items.label: infDist_pos_of_pointwise_lower_bound
items.statement:
A strictly positive pointwise separation certificate gives a strictly positive punctured
infimum distance from the distinguished point.
items.title: infDist_pos_of_pointwise_lower_bound

items.label: infDist_sphere
items.statement:
The distance from a point to a nonempty sphere in a real normed affine space is the
absolute radial deviation from that sphere.
items.title: infDist_sphere

items.label: injective_of_pos_le_dist
items.statement:
A positive pointwise lower bound on distances between distinct images makes
the indexed family injective.
items.title: injective_of_pos_le_dist

items.label: isolationClosedBall_disjoint_derivedSet
items.statement:
A quarter-isolation closed ball in a closed set is disjoint from the set's derived set
when the isolation distance is positive.
items.title: isolationClosedBall_disjoint_derivedSet

items.label: isolationDistance_eq
items.statement: The isolation distance is the infimum distance to the punctured set.
items.title: isolationDistance_eq

items.label: isolationDistance_nonneg
items.statement: Isolation distance is nonnegative.
items.title: isolationDistance_nonneg

items.label: isolationRadius_eq
items.statement: The isolation radius is one quarter of the punctured-set distance.
items.title: isolationRadius_eq

items.label: isolationRadius_lt_isolationDistance
items.statement:
When the isolation distance is positive, its quarter-radius is strictly
smaller.
items.title: isolationRadius_lt_isolationDistance

items.label: isolationRadius_nonneg
items.statement: Isolation radius is nonnegative.
items.title: isolationRadius_nonneg

items.label: le_infDist_diff_singleton_of_pointwise_lower_bound
items.statement:
A pointwise distance lower bound on a punctured set gives the same lower bound for its
infimum distance from the distinguished point.
items.title: le_infDist_diff_singleton_of_pointwise_lower_bound

items.label: le_infDist_union_range_diff_singleton
items.statement:
Pointwise lower bounds to a background set and an indexed family combine into a
lower bound for the distance to their union after removing the distinguished point.
items.title: le_infDist_union_range_diff_singleton

items.label: le_infDist_union_range_diff_singleton_of_not_mem
items.statement:
If the distinguished point is outside a nonempty background set, lower bounds to that
set and to every other indexed point bound the corresponding punctured infimum distance.
items.title: le_infDist_union_range_diff_singleton_of_not_mem

items.label: locallyFinite_closedBall_outside
items.statement:
Shrinking closed balls are locally finite at every point outside the set containing all
`atTop` cluster points of their centers.
items.title: locallyFinite_closedBall_outside

items.label: pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall_of_radius_add_lt_dist
items.statement:
Closed balls with radii whose pairwise sums are strictly below the corresponding center
distances form a pairwise-disjoint family.
items.title: pairwiseDisjoint_closedBall_of_radius_add_lt_dist

items.label: pairwiseDisjoint_isolationClosedBall
items.statement:
The quarter-isolation closed balls centered at distinct members of a set are pairwise
disjoint.
items.title: pairwiseDisjoint_isolationClosedBall

items.label: radiusGap_le_dist_add_errors
items.statement:
A lower bound for the gap between two approximate radii is bounded by the
distance between the points together with the two radius errors.
items.title: radiusGap_le_dist_add_errors

items.label: uniform_decay_of_le_scale_of_mul_scale_le_infDist
items.statement:
A quantity bounded by a fixed multiple of a scale converges uniformly to
zero along support points approaching a target, provided target distance is
bounded below by a positive multiple of the same scale.
items.title: uniform_decay_of_le_scale_of_mul_scale_le_infDist

items.label: abs_toReal_oangle_add_le
items.statement: Adding an error vector changes the real oriented angle by at most its relative size.
items.title: abs_toReal_oangle_add_le

items.label: abs_toReal_oangle_le
items.statement: A common positive lower norm bound controls the real oriented angle between two vectors.
items.title: abs_toReal_oangle_le

items.label: abs_decrementError_le_of_residual
items.statement:
A controlled higher-order recurrence residual bounds the error in its leading
decrement term.
items.title: abs_decrementError_le_of_residual

items.label: abs_sub_inv_mul_le_of_interval
items.statement:
An interval around `x / a` with positive denominators controls the absolute
error by the wider endpoint displacement.
items.title: abs_sub_inv_mul_le_of_interval

items.label: decrementBounds_of_residual
items.statement:
A controlled residual for a parabolic recurrence traps its one-step decrement
between the corresponding perturbed leading terms.
items.title: decrementBounds_of_residual

items.label: recurrence_tail_pow_error_of_residual
items.statement:
A uniform two-term parabolic recurrence residual controls the critical power
tail's absolute error from its leading value `ε i j / a`.
items.title: recurrence_tail_pow_error_of_residual

items.label: recurrence_tail_pow_error_of_two_sided_decrement
items.statement:
Two-sided decrement bounds yield an explicit error bound for the power-tail
sum around its leading coefficient `1 / a`.
items.title: recurrence_tail_pow_error_of_two_sided_decrement

items.label: sum_range_shift_sub
items.statement: A finite sum of consecutive decrements of a shifted real sequence telescopes.
items.title: sum_range_shift_sub

items.label: summable_tail_pow_and_tsum_le_of_decrement
items.statement:
A positive family whose decrement dominates `c * ε i j ^ (p + 1)` has uniformly
summable shifted `q`-power tails whenever `p + 1 ≤ q`, with the telescoping bound
`∑' k, ε i (j + k) ^ q ≤ c⁻¹ * ε i j ^ (q - p)`.
items.title: summable_tail_pow_and_tsum_le_of_decrement

items.label: summable_tail_pow_and_tsum_le_of_residual
items.statement:
A family with a uniform parabolic recurrence residual has uniformly summable
shifted higher-power tails, with the bound obtained from its leading decrement.
items.title: summable_tail_pow_and_tsum_le_of_residual

items.label: tendsto_div_natCast_of_tendsto_forwardDiff
items.statement:
If the forward differences of a real sequence tend to `c`, then the sequence divided by
the natural-number index tends to `c`. This is the telescoping form of Cesàro convergence.
items.title: tendsto_div_natCast_of_tendsto_forwardDiff

items.label: tendsto_invPow_forwardDiff_of_isBigO
items.statement:
For a positive parabolic recurrence, the forward differences of the reciprocal `p`-th
powers tend to `a * p`.
items.title: tendsto_invPow_forwardDiff_of_isBigO

items.label: tendsto_invPow_forwardDiff_of_ratio_and_scaledDecrement
items.statement:
A normalized decrement limit and a successive-ratio limit determine the forward difference
of the reciprocal `p`-th powers.
items.title: tendsto_invPow_forwardDiff_of_ratio_and_scaledDecrement

items.label: tendsto_ratio_one_of_isBigO
items.statement:
A positive sequence tending to zero and satisfying a parabolic recurrence has successive
ratio tending to one.
items.title: tendsto_ratio_one_of_isBigO

items.label: tendsto_scaledDecrement_of_isBigO
items.statement:
The parabolic recurrence residual of order `p + 2` makes the decrement, normalized by
`ε j ^ (p + 1)`, tend to its leading coefficient `a`.
items.title: tendsto_scaledDecrement_of_isBigO

items.label: tsum_tail_pow_interval_of_residual
items.statement:
A uniform two-term parabolic recurrence residual gives the sharp interval for
the critical power tail when every member of the family tends to zero.
items.title: tsum_tail_pow_interval_of_residual

items.label: tsum_tail_pow_interval_of_two_sided_decrement
items.statement:
Two-sided order-`p + 1` decrement bounds give the sharp interval for the
corresponding power tail when every sequence tends to zero.
items.title: tsum_tail_pow_interval_of_two_sided_decrement

items.label: existsLimit
items.statement:
A positive sequence whose successive ratios have a summable nonnegative first-order
perturbation converges to a positive limit.
items.title: existsLimit

items.label: subLimitIsEquivalent
items.statement:
The first-order tail expansion as an asymptotic equivalence when its coefficient
`c` is nonzero.
items.title: subLimitIsEquivalent

items.label: subLimitIsLittleO
items.statement:
If the shifted tail of `u` is asymptotic to `v`, then the error from the positive
limit has first-order term `c * aLim * v`.
items.title: subLimitIsLittleO

items.label: coe_eq_liftSequence_succ_sub_iff
items.statement:
A real number in the principal interval represents a consecutive angle increment
exactly when it equals the corresponding increment of the canonical lift.
items.title: coe_eq_liftSequence_succ_sub_iff

items.label: coe_liftSequence
items.statement: Coercing a canonical real lift back to `Real.Angle` recovers the original sequence.
items.title: coe_liftSequence

items.label: continuous_abs_toReal
items.statement:
Although the principal representative `Angle.toReal` jumps at the branch cut,
its absolute value is a globally continuous function of the angle.
items.title: continuous_abs_toReal

items.label: liftSequence_even_sub_eq_toReal_of_coe_of_mem_Ioc
items.statement:
Along the even subsequence of a canonical angle lift, a quotient-valued relation
with an arbitrary real comparison sequence determines the corresponding real
representative.  The only branch hypothesis is that the representative predicted by
two angle increments and one comparison increment lies in the principal interval.
items.title: liftSequence_even_sub_eq_toReal_of_coe_of_mem_Ioc

items.label: liftSequence_sub_eq_toReal_sub_of_mem_Ioc
items.statement:
Two canonical angle lifts stay on the branch represented by their quotient-valued
difference when the initial branches agree and every recursively predicted difference
lies in the principal interval.
items.title: liftSequence_sub_eq_toReal_sub_of_mem_Ioc

items.label: liftSequence_succ
items.statement:
A successor value of the canonical lift adds the canonical representative of the
corresponding angle increment.
items.title: liftSequence_succ

items.label: liftSequence_succ_sub
items.statement:
Consecutive values of the canonical lift differ by the canonical representative of
the corresponding quotient-angle increment.
items.title: liftSequence_succ_sub

items.label: liftSequence_zero
items.statement: The canonical lift starts at the canonical real representative of the first angle.
items.title: liftSequence_zero

items.label: windingNumber_pos_of_antitone
items.statement:
An antitone real angle lift has positive winding number whenever the
remainder in a full-turn decomposition is smaller than the first traversed
gap.  This isolates the order argument from any particular orbit or scale
estimate.
items.title: windingNumber_pos_of_antitone

items.label: analyticAt_signedSqrtBranch
items.statement:
If `q` is analytic at `0`, satisfies `q 0 = 1`, and is eventually positive near
`0`, then `ε ↦ ε * √(q ε)` is analytic at `0`.
items.title: analyticAt_signedSqrtBranch

items.label: antilipschitzWith_inv_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
A positive derivative lower bound `lower` gives the reciprocal antilipschitz
constant `lower⁻¹`.
items.title: antilipschitzWith_inv_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: arctan_comp_sub_cubic_isBigO
items.statement:
Composing the cubic arctangent remainder with an order-`n` slope germ gives an
order-`4n` remainder.
items.title: arctan_comp_sub_cubic_isBigO

items.label: arctan_sub_cubic_isBigO
items.statement: The cubic Taylor polynomial of `Real.arctan` has a fourth-order remainder at zero.
items.title: arctan_sub_cubic_isBigO

items.label: bijective_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
A differentiable real function with a uniform positive lower derivative bound is
bijective.
items.title: bijective_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: contDiff_invFun_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
At every positive finite smoothness order, `Function.invFun` inherits the forward
map's `ContDiff` regularity.
items.title: contDiff_invFun_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: diffeomorphOfPosLEDeriv_apply
items.statement: Evaluating `diffeomorphOfPosLEDeriv` applies its forward function.
items.title: diffeomorphOfPosLEDeriv_apply

items.label: diffeomorphOfPosLEDeriv_symm_apply
items.statement: Evaluating the inverse of `diffeomorphOfPosLEDeriv` applies `Function.invFun`.
items.title: diffeomorphOfPosLEDeriv_symm_apply

items.label: exists_uniform_iteratedDeriv_invFun_bound
items.statement:
A family of `C^ν` real functions with a common positive derivative lower
bound and common higher-order forward derivative bounds admits one family-independent
bound for every inverse derivative through order `ν`.
items.title: exists_uniform_iteratedDeriv_invFun_bound

items.label: hasDerivAt_signedSqrtBranch
items.statement:
If `q` is analytic at `0`, satisfies `q 0 = 1`, and is eventually positive near
`0`, then the derivative at `0` of `ε ↦ ε * √(q ε)` is `1`.
items.title: hasDerivAt_signedSqrtBranch

items.label: lipschitzWith_invFun_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
The `Function.invFun` of a function with positive derivative lower bound `lower` is
`lower⁻¹`-Lipschitz.
items.title: lipschitzWith_invFun_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: norm_iteratedDeriv_one_invFun_le
items.statement:
A uniform positive lower bound for the derivative of a `C¹` real function
gives the reciprocal uniform bound for the first derivative of its inverse.
items.title: norm_iteratedDeriv_one_invFun_le

items.label: norm_iteratedDeriv_three_invFun_le
items.statement:
If the second and third derivatives of a `C³` real function have common
bounds, then the third derivative of its inverse obeys the explicit scalar
inverse-function bound.
items.title: norm_iteratedDeriv_three_invFun_le

items.label: norm_iteratedDeriv_two_invFun_le
items.statement:
If the second derivative of a `C²` real function is bounded by
`secondBound`, then the second derivative of its inverse is bounded by
`secondBound * lower⁻¹ ^ 3`.
items.title: norm_iteratedDeriv_two_invFun_le

items.label: signedSqrtBranch_eventuallyEq_sqrt
items.statement:
On a sufficiently small right neighborhood of `0`, the signed square-root branch
`ε ↦ ε * √(q ε)` agrees with `ε ↦ √(ε ^ 2 * q ε)`.
items.title: signedSqrtBranch_eventuallyEq_sqrt

items.label: strictMono_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
A differentiable real function with a uniform positive lower derivative bound is
strictly increasing.
items.title: strictMono_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: surjective_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
A differentiable real function with a uniform positive lower derivative bound is
surjective.
items.title: surjective_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
A differentiable real function with a uniform positive lower derivative bound tends
to `atBot` at `atBot`.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: tendsto_atTop_of_pos_le_deriv
items.statement:
A differentiable real function with a uniform positive lower derivative bound tends
to `atTop` at `atTop`.
items.title: tendsto_atTop_of_pos_le_deriv

items.label: tsum_nat_add_rpow_isEquivalent
items.statement:
The tail of the real `p`-series with exponent `s > 1` is asymptotic to
`(s - 1)⁻¹ * j ^ (1 - s)`.
items.title: tsum_nat_add_rpow_isEquivalent

items.label: analyticOnNhd_frame
items.statement:
Every entry of the positively oriented frame of the fixed low eigenvector branch is analytic
throughout `lowChart`.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_frame

items.label: analyticOnNhd_gap
items.statement: The spectral gap is analytic throughout the chart `a < d`.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_gap

items.label: analyticOnNhd_high
items.statement: The upper eigenvalue is analytic throughout the chart `a < d`.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_high

items.label: analyticOnNhd_highVector
items.statement: The perpendicular high-eigenvector branch is analytic throughout the chart `a < d`.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_highVector

items.label: analyticOnNhd_low
items.statement: The lower eigenvalue is analytic throughout the chart `a < d`.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_low

items.label: analyticOnNhd_lowVector
items.statement: The normalized low-eigenvector branch is analytic throughout the chart `a < d`.
items.title: analyticOnNhd_lowVector

items.label: diag_mem_lowChart
items.statement: The coordinates of `matrix 0 0 1` belong to the low-eigenvector chart.
items.title: diag_mem_lowChart

items.label: eigenvalues_one
items.statement: The first ordered Hermitian eigenvalue is the explicit lower eigenvalue.
items.title: eigenvalues_one

items.label: eigenvalues_zero
items.statement: The zeroth ordered Hermitian eigenvalue is the explicit upper eigenvalue.
items.title: eigenvalues_zero

items.label: exists_ball_inner_lowVector_pos
items.statement:
A positive base-point pairing with an analytic vector field persists on a positive-radius
ball, using the fixed analytic low-eigenvector branch throughout.
items.title: exists_ball_inner_lowVector_pos

items.label: firstCoordinate_lowVector_pos
items.statement: On the chart `a < d`, the first coordinate fixes the sign of the low eigenvector.
items.title: firstCoordinate_lowVector_pos

items.label: frame_diag
items.statement: At `matrix 0 0 1`, the positively oriented eigenframe is the identity matrix.
items.title: frame_diag

items.label: frame_diagonalizes
items.statement: Conjugation by the positively oriented eigenframe diagonalizes the symmetric matrix.
items.title: frame_diagonalizes

items.label: frame_diagonalizes_of_lowDenom_ne_zero
items.statement:
A nonzero normalization denominator is sufficient for the fixed oriented
eigenframe to diagonalize the symmetric matrix; no separate chart inequality
is needed.
items.title: frame_diagonalizes_of_lowDenom_ne_zero

items.label: frame_diagonalizes_of_mem_orthogonalGroup
items.statement:
Once the explicit eigenframe is known to be orthogonal, conjugation by it
diagonalizes the symmetric matrix.
items.title: frame_diagonalizes_of_mem_orthogonalGroup

items.label: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup
items.statement: On `lowChart`, the frame of the fixed low eigenvector branch is special orthogonal.
items.title: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.label: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_of_lowDenom_ne_zero
items.statement:
A nonzero normalization denominator is enough for the fixed low-vector
branch to define a special orthogonal frame, without a separate chart
inequality.
items.title: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_of_lowDenom_ne_zero

items.label: frame_reconstructs_of_lowDenom_ne_zero
items.statement:
A nonzero normalization denominator also gives the reverse spectral
reconstruction of the symmetric matrix.
items.title: frame_reconstructs_of_lowDenom_ne_zero

items.label: frame_reconstructs_of_mem_orthogonalGroup
items.statement:
Once the explicit eigenframe is known to be orthogonal, conjugating its
spectral diagonal back reconstructs the symmetric matrix.
items.title: frame_reconstructs_of_mem_orthogonalGroup

items.label: gap_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the explicit spectral gap.
items.title: gap_apply

items.label: gap_sq
items.statement: Squaring the spectral gap recovers the discriminant.
items.title: gap_sq

items.label: highVector_eigen
items.statement: The explicit perpendicular vector satisfies the high-eigenvalue equation.
items.title: highVector_eigen

items.label: highVector_eq_coordinatePerp
items.statement:
The explicit high vector has the coordinate pair obtained by positively rotating the low
vector through a right angle.
items.title: highVector_eq_coordinatePerp

items.label: highVector_eq_perp_lowVector
items.statement:
The explicit high eigenvector is the positively oriented perpendicular of the fixed low
eigenvector branch.
items.title: highVector_eq_perp_lowVector

items.label: high_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the upper eigenvalue branch.
items.title: high_apply

items.label: inner_lowVector_highVector
items.statement: The explicit low and high vectors are orthogonal.
items.title: inner_lowVector_highVector

items.label: isOpen_lowChart
items.statement: The low-eigenvector coordinate chart is open.
items.title: isOpen_lowChart

items.label: lowDenom_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the normalization denominator of the low eigenvector.
items.title: lowDenom_apply

items.label: lowDenom_eq_norm_lowRaw
items.statement: The explicit normalization denominator is the norm of the raw low eigenvector.
items.title: lowDenom_eq_norm_lowRaw

items.label: lowDenom_nonneg
items.statement:
The normalization denominator of the fixed low-eigenvector branch is
nonnegative.
items.title: lowDenom_nonneg

items.label: lowVector_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the normalized low-eigenvector branch.
items.title: lowVector_apply

items.label: lowVector_diag
items.statement: At `matrix 0 0 1`, the low eigenvector is the first standard basis vector.
items.title: lowVector_diag

items.label: lowVector_eigen
items.statement: The explicit low vector satisfies the low-eigenvalue equation.
items.title: lowVector_eigen

items.label: lowVector_hasEigenvector
items.statement: On the chart `a < d`, the explicit low vector is a nonzero eigenvector.
items.title: lowVector_hasEigenvector

items.label: low_add_high
items.statement: The explicit eigenvalues add to the trace.
items.title: low_add_high

items.label: low_apply
items.statement: Evaluation formula for the lower eigenvalue branch.
items.title: low_apply

items.label: low_eq_det_div_high_of_ne
items.statement:
If the high eigenvalue is nonzero, the low eigenvalue is the determinant
divided by the high eigenvalue.
items.title: low_eq_det_div_high_of_ne

items.label: low_le_high
items.statement: The explicit lower eigenvalue is at most the explicit upper eigenvalue.
items.title: low_le_high

items.label: low_lt_high_iff_gap_pos
items.statement: The explicit eigenvalues are strictly ordered exactly when the gap is positive.
items.title: low_lt_high_iff_gap_pos

items.label: low_mul_high
items.statement: The explicit eigenvalues multiply to the determinant.
items.title: low_mul_high

items.label: low_ne_high
items.statement: A positive spectral gap makes the two explicit eigenvalues distinct.
items.title: low_ne_high

items.label: matrix_eq
items.statement: The entries of `matrix a b d` are the displayed symmetric matrix.
items.title: matrix_eq

items.label: matrix_isHermitian
items.statement: The explicit matrix is Hermitian.
items.title: matrix_isHermitian

items.label: mem_lowChart
items.statement: Membership in the low-eigenvector chart is the inequality `a < d`.
items.title: mem_lowChart

items.label: norm_highVector
items.statement: On the chart `a < d`, the explicit high eigenvector has unit norm.
items.title: norm_highVector

items.label: norm_lowVector
items.statement: On the chart `a < d`, the explicit low eigenvector has unit norm.
items.title: norm_lowVector

items.label: rootMultiplicity_high
items.statement: With positive spectral gap, the upper eigenvalue has algebraic multiplicity one.
items.title: rootMultiplicity_high

items.label: rootMultiplicity_low
items.statement: With positive spectral gap, the lower eigenvalue has algebraic multiplicity one.
items.title: rootMultiplicity_low

items.label: refl
items.statement: Every seminorm is equivalent to itself.
items.title: refl

items.label: symm
items.statement: Equivalence of seminorms is symmetric.
items.title: symm

items.label: trans
items.statement: Equivalence of seminorms is transitive.
items.title: trans

items.label: isContracting_iff
items.statement: Contraction of a seminorm expressed as a pointwise estimate.
items.title: isContracting_iff

items.label: isEquivalent_iff
items.statement:
Seminorm.isEquivalent_iff: equivalence of seminorms expressed by pointwise
two-sided bounds.
items.title: isEquivalent_iff

items.label: norm_sub_limit_isBigO
items.statement:
An eventual comparison for forward differences and a uniformly summable
comparison tail give the corresponding big-O bound for the distance to the
limit.
items.title: norm_sub_limit_isBigO

items.label: norm_sub_limit_le
items.statement:
A pointwise comparison for forward differences and a summable comparison
tail give a pointwise bound on the distance to the limit.
items.title: norm_sub_limit_le

items.label: norm_sub_limit_le_tsum
items.statement:
The distance from a convergent sequence to its limit is bounded by the
sum of the norms of its remaining forward differences.
items.title: norm_sub_limit_le_tsum

items.label: tsum_forwardDiff
items.statement:
The sum of the forward-difference tail of a convergent sequence is its
remaining displacement.
items.title: tsum_forwardDiff

items.label: indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement: The extension by zero from the complement of a set vanishes on that set.
items.title: indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: coe_of
items.statement: Coercing a graph built with `of` recovers the original bounded continuous function.
items.title: coe_of

items.label: coe_zero
items.statement: The underlying bounded continuous function of the zero graph is zero.
items.title: coe_zero

items.label: contractingWith_of_dist_apply_le_mul
items.statement:
A pointwise output estimate by the input sup distance upgrades a self-map to
`ContractingWith`.
items.title: contractingWith_of_dist_apply_le_mul

items.label: dist_apply_le
items.statement:
Evaluation at any point is nonexpanding for the sup distance on small Lipschitz
graphs.
items.title: dist_apply_le

items.label: dist_eq
items.statement: The inherited distance is the distance between the underlying bounded continuous functions.
items.title: dist_eq

items.label: dist_fixedPoint_fixedPoint_le_of_dist_apply_le
items.statement:
Pointwise closeness of two uniformly contracting graph transforms controls the distance
between their unique fixed-point graphs.
items.title: dist_fixedPoint_fixedPoint_le_of_dist_apply_le

items.label: dist_fixedPoint_le_of_dist_apply_le
items.statement: A pointwise defect bound controls the distance to the unique fixed-point graph.
items.title: dist_fixedPoint_le_of_dist_apply_le

items.label: dist_le_iff
items.statement:
A sup-distance bound on small Lipschitz graphs is equivalent to the corresponding
pointwise bounds.
items.title: dist_le_iff

items.label: isClosed_carrier
items.statement: The ambient carrier cut out by all three small-graph constraints is closed.
items.title: isClosed_carrier

items.label: isClosed_lipschitzWith
items.statement: The cone of bounded continuous graphs with Lipschitz constant at most `slope` is closed.
items.title: isClosed_lipschitzWith

items.label: isClosed_supNorm
items.statement: The constraint that the uniform norm be bounded by `radius` is closed.
items.title: isClosed_supNorm

items.label: isClosed_valueAtZero
items.statement: The constraint that a bounded continuous graph vanish at zero is closed.
items.title: isClosed_valueAtZero

items.label: lipschitzWith
items.statement: A small Lipschitz graph obeys its prescribed Lipschitz bound.
items.title: lipschitzWith

items.label: lipschitzWith_fixedPoint_of_dist_apply_le_mul
items.statement:
A uniformly contracting family whose outputs are pointwise Lipschitz in the parameter has
fixed-point graphs that are Lipschitz in that parameter, with the exact constant
`L / (1 - K)`.
items.title: lipschitzWith_fixedPoint_of_dist_apply_le_mul

items.label: norm_le
items.statement: The bounded-continuous-function norm of a small Lipschitz graph is at most its radius.
items.title: norm_le

items.label: spec
items.statement: The combined defining specification of a small Lipschitz graph.
items.title: spec

items.label: zero_apply
items.statement: A small Lipschitz graph vanishes at zero.
items.title: zero_apply

items.label: zero_spec
items.statement: The zero bounded continuous graph satisfies every nonnegative radius and slope bound.
items.title: zero_spec

items.label: centeredBump_eq_one_of_mem_closedBall
items.statement: The centered cutoff equals one on its inner closed ball.
items.title: centeredBump_eq_one_of_mem_closedBall

items.label: centeredBump_nonneg_le_one
items.statement: The centered cutoff takes values in the unit interval.
items.title: centeredBump_nonneg_le_one

items.label: contDiff_centeredBump
items.statement: The centered cutoff is infinitely differentiable.
items.title: contDiff_centeredBump

items.label: exists_norm_fderiv_centeredBump_le
items.statement: The first derivative of a finite-dimensional centered cutoff has a global norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_fderiv_centeredBump_le

items.label: exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_centeredBump_le
items.statement:
Every fixed iterated derivative of a finite-dimensional centered cutoff has a global
nonnegative norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_centeredBump_le

items.label: exists_norm_secondFDeriv_centeredBump_le
items.statement: The second derivative of a finite-dimensional centered cutoff has a global norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_secondFDeriv_centeredBump_le

items.label: hasCompactSupport_centeredBump
items.statement: In finite-dimensional spaces the centered cutoff has compact support.
items.title: hasCompactSupport_centeredBump

items.label: support_centeredBump
items.statement: The function support of the centered cutoff is its outer open ball.
items.title: support_centeredBump

items.label: tsupport_centeredBump
items.statement: The topological support of the centered cutoff is its outer closed ball.
items.title: tsupport_centeredBump

items.label: abs_dotProduct_sub_phase_quadraticForm_le
items.statement:
The quadratic form of either phase differs from the Euclidean sum of
squares by at most `2 * |ε|` times that sum.
items.title: abs_dotProduct_sub_phase_quadraticForm_le

items.label: abs_one_sub_phase_tau_le
items.statement: The absolute strong-Wolfe ratio of either phase is at most `2 / 3`.
items.title: abs_one_sub_phase_tau_le

items.label: abs_one_sub_phase_tau_mem
items.statement: The two absolute strong-Wolfe ratios are exactly `1 / 3` and `2 / 3`.
items.title: abs_one_sub_phase_tau_mem

items.label: first_matrix
items.statement: The first control has matrix `!![1, ε; ε, 1]`.
items.title: first_matrix

items.label: first_tau
items.statement: The first control has ratio `2 / 3`.
items.title: first_tau

items.label: matrix_isHermitian
items.statement: Every matrix in the two-phase family is Hermitian.
items.title: matrix_isHermitian

items.label: matrix_posDef
items.statement: Under the prescribed scale restriction, every control matrix is positive definite.
items.title: matrix_posDef

items.label: phaseQuotient_mem_Icc_of_curvature
items.statement:
If a phase curvature equals `tau * q`, then `q` is uniformly comparable
to the squared Euclidean norm of the coordinate vector.
items.title: phaseQuotient_mem_Icc_of_curvature

items.label: phase_one
items.statement: Phase one is the second control.
items.title: phase_one

items.label: phase_quadraticForm_bounds
items.statement:
The quadratic form of either two-phase control is uniformly comparable to
the Euclidean sum of squares on the prescribed scale interval.
items.title: phase_quadraticForm_bounds

items.label: phase_tau_mem
items.statement: Every two-phase line ratio is one of the two prescribed rational values.
items.title: phase_tau_mem

items.label: phase_zero
items.statement: Phase zero is the first control.
items.title: phase_zero

items.label: quotient_bounds_of_phase_curvature_eq_tau_mul
items.statement:
If the phase curvature is `tau * q`, then `q` is nonnegative and uniformly
comparable to the Euclidean sum of squares.
items.title: quotient_bounds_of_phase_curvature_eq_tau_mul

items.label: radius_def
items.statement: The radius is the square of the common control scale.
items.title: radius_def

items.label: second_matrix
items.statement: The second control has matrix `!![1, -2 * ε; -2 * ε, 1]`.
items.title: second_matrix

items.label: second_tau
items.statement: The second control has ratio `1 / 3`.
items.title: second_tau

items.label: spectrum_mem
items.statement:
Under the prescribed scale restriction, every Hermitian eigenvalue of every
control matrix belongs to `[1 / 2, 3 / 2]`.
items.title: spectrum_mem

items.label: tau_pos
items.statement: Every step ratio in the ordered two-phase family is positive.
items.title: tau_pos

items.label: abs_inner_div_le_scale
items.statement:
A cubic vector bound, a quadratic-scale step bound, and a fourth-order
positive denominator bound control the corresponding inner-product quotient
linearly in the scale.
items.title: abs_inner_div_le_scale

items.label: contDiffAt_dotProduct
items.statement: Pointwise smooth finite-vector families have a smooth pointwise dot product.
items.title: contDiffAt_dotProduct

items.label: contDiffAt_matrix_diagonal
items.statement: Pointwise smooth vector families give pointwise smooth diagonal matrix families.
items.title: contDiffAt_matrix_diagonal

items.label: contDiffAt_matrix_mulVec
items.statement: Pointwise smooth matrix and vector families have a smooth matrix-vector product.
items.title: contDiffAt_matrix_mulVec

items.label: contDiffAt_matrix_of
items.statement: Pointwise smooth doubly indexed families assemble into pointwise smooth matrices.
items.title: contDiffAt_matrix_of

items.label: contDiffAt_matrix_vecCons
items.statement: Pointwise smoothness is preserved by prepending a coordinate to a finite vector.
items.title: contDiffAt_matrix_vecCons

items.label: contDiffOn_finsum_outside
items.statement:
The pointwise finsum of smooth functions supported in shrinking, pairwise-disjoint closed
balls is smooth away from a closed set containing the cluster points of the centers.
items.title: contDiffOn_finsum_outside

items.label: contDiff_dotProduct
items.statement: Globally smooth finite-vector families have a smooth pointwise dot product.
items.title: contDiff_dotProduct

items.label: contDiff_matrix_diagonal
items.statement: Globally smooth vector families give globally smooth diagonal matrix families.
items.title: contDiff_matrix_diagonal

items.label: contDiff_matrix_mulVec
items.statement: Globally smooth matrix and vector families have a smooth matrix-vector product.
items.title: contDiff_matrix_mulVec

items.label: contDiff_matrix_of
items.statement: Globally smooth doubly indexed families assemble into globally smooth matrices.
items.title: contDiff_matrix_of

items.label: contDiff_matrix_vecCons
items.statement: Global smoothness is preserved by prepending a coordinate to a finite vector.
items.title: contDiff_matrix_vecCons

items.label: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_eqOn_zero_jets
items.statement:
A disjoint shrinking family with supportwise value, first-derivative, and second-derivative
decay yields a global C² zero extension together with its value and first two Fréchet jets
vanishing on the closed cluster set.
items.title: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_eqOn_zero_jets

items.label: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_of_decay
items.statement:
A pointwise finsum over shrinking pairwise-disjoint supports extends by zero across its
closed cluster set as a globally twice continuously differentiable function, provided its
value and first two derivatives have the required boundary decay.
items.title: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_of_decay

items.label: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_of_supportwise_decay
items.statement:
Supportwise quadratic, linear, and zeroth-order decay of the first three jets of
disjoint shrinking summands makes their zero extension twice continuously differentiable.
items.title: contDiff_two_indicator_compl_finsum_of_supportwise_decay

items.label: contDiff_two_slowCurveBumpCorrection
items.statement:
The global bump correction is twice continuously differentiable along a
source-presented invariant slow curve.
items.title: contDiff_two_slowCurveBumpCorrection

items.label: contDiff_two_slowCurveRealizedObjective
items.statement:
Proposition 5.12a (Global Hessian bounds) (1): the realized objective
is globally twice continuously differentiable.
items.title: contDiff_two_slowCurveRealizedObjective

items.label: eventually_atTop_of_even_odd
items.statement:
An eventual property of both the even and odd subsequences is eventual for the
whole sequence.
items.title: eventually_atTop_of_even_odd

items.label: existsCommonInitialScale
items.statement:
Lemma 6.7a (Master choice of one initial scale satisfying all smallness requirements):
a finite family of positive preliminary thresholds and the positive Hessian constant `K`
admit one positive scale below every threshold and below `(2 * K)⁻¹`.
items.title: existsCommonInitialScale

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_mul_apply
items.statement:
The second Fréchet derivative of a product of real-valued `C²` functions satisfies
the four-term Leibniz rule. Here the outer derivative is applied first to `v`, and the
resulting continuous linear map is then evaluated at `u`.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_mul_apply

items.label: hessianHolderOn_comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: linear pullback preserves a Hölder
Hessian bound on a set, with its explicit coordinate-dependent constant.
This estimate is upstream-worthy for the Hessian coordinate-change API.
items.title: hessianHolderOn_comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: hessianHolder_comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: a linear pullback preserves a
global Hölder Hessian estimate.
items.title: hessianHolder_comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: hessian_apply_inner
items.statement: Pairing the Hessian with two directions evaluates the second iterated Frechet derivative.
items.title: hessian_apply_inner

items.label: hessian_def
items.statement: The operator-valued Hessian is the derivative of the gradient.
items.title: hessian_def

items.label: hessian_isSelfAdjoint
items.statement: Twice continuous differentiability makes the Hessian self-adjoint.
items.title: hessian_isSelfAdjoint

items.label: inner_gradient_sub_ge_of_hessian_lower_bound
items.statement:
A positive global Hessian lower bound makes the gradient strongly monotone along
every displacement.
items.title: inner_gradient_sub_ge_of_hessian_lower_bound

items.label: inner_gradient_sub_pos_of_hessian_lower_bound
items.statement:
A positive Hessian lower bound gives strict gradient-secant curvature for distinct
points.
items.title: inner_gradient_sub_pos_of_hessian_lower_bound

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
An iterated Fréchet derivative vanishes at every point outside the topological support
of the original function.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_at_center
items.statement:
At an active center outside the cluster set, every available iterated derivative of a
pointwise finsum equals the corresponding derivative of the centered summand.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_at_center

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_of_mem_tsupport
items.statement:
Away from the cluster set, the iterated derivatives of a pointwise finsum agree with those
of the summand whose topological support contains the point.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_of_mem_tsupport

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_zero
items.statement:
Away from the cluster set, every iterated derivative through the smoothness order of a
pointwise finsum vanishes at a point outside all topological supports.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_finsum_eq_zero

items.label: locallyFinite_tsupport_outside
items.statement:
Topological supports contained in shrinking, pairwise-disjoint closed balls are locally
finite away from a closed set containing every `atTop` cluster point of their centers.
items.title: locallyFinite_tsupport_outside

items.label: mem_closure_range_iff_mem_or_mapClusterPt
items.statement:
A point lies in the closure of a sequence's range exactly when it is attained or is an
`atTop` cluster point of the sequence.
items.title: mem_closure_range_iff_mem_or_mapClusterPt

items.label: normSq_mem_Icc_of_norm_mem_Icc
items.statement: Squaring a nonnegative norm interval preserves its endpoint ordering.
items.title: normSq_mem_Icc_of_norm_mem_Icc

items.label: norm_fderiv_gradient_eq_norm_fderiv_fderiv
items.statement:
Passing from the derivative covector to its Riesz-representing gradient preserves the
operator norm of the second Fréchet derivative.
items.title: norm_fderiv_gradient_eq_norm_fderiv_fderiv

items.label: norm_fderiv_gradient_eq_norm_iteratedFDeriv_two
items.statement:
The Hessian operator norm also agrees with the norm of the order-two iterated
Fréchet derivative.
items.title: norm_fderiv_gradient_eq_norm_iteratedFDeriv_two

items.label: norm_firstOrderRemainder_le_of_holderDerivative
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: a Hölder derivative on a segment
gives a remainder of order `1 + β`. This upstream-worthy mean-value estimate
does not require the sharp integral constant.
items.title: norm_firstOrderRemainder_le_of_holderDerivative

items.label: norm_hessian_eq_norm_iteratedFDeriv_two
items.statement: The Hessian norm agrees with the norm of the second iterated Frechet derivative.
items.title: norm_hessian_eq_norm_iteratedFDeriv_two

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_affine_le
items.statement:
Precomposition by the affine map `x ↦ A x + b` multiplies the pointwise norm of
the `n`-th iterated Fréchet derivative by at most `‖A‖ ^ n`.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_affine_le

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_at_center_le
items.statement:
A uniform bound for the iterated derivatives of centered summands gives the same bound
for the corresponding derivative of the pointwise finsum at every active center.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_at_center_le

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_le_of_tsupport_bound
items.statement:
A uniform bound for one iterated derivative on each summand's topological support
gives the same bound for the pointwise finsum away from the cluster set.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_le_of_tsupport_bound

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_le_of_weighted_tsupport_bound
items.statement:
A nonnegative weight bounded by `W` turns a supportwise estimate
`‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (ψ k) z‖ ≤ C * w k` into the uniform `C * W` bound
needed by the disjoint-finsum derivative theorem.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_le_of_weighted_tsupport_bound

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_of_tsupport
items.statement:
A nonnegative bound for an iterated derivative on the topological support of the
original function is automatically a global bound.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_of_tsupport

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_one_comp_affine_le
items.statement:
Precomposition by the affine map `x ↦ A x + b` multiplies the pointwise norm of
the first iterated Fréchet derivative by at most `‖A‖`.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_one_comp_affine_le

items.label: norm_iteratedFDeriv_two_comp_affine_le
items.statement:
Precomposition by the affine map `x ↦ A x + b` multiplies the pointwise norm of
the second iterated Fréchet derivative by at most `‖A‖ ^ 2`.
items.title: norm_iteratedFDeriv_two_comp_affine_le

items.label: norm_secondFDeriv_eq_norm_iteratedFDeriv_two
items.statement:
The norm of the ordinary second Fréchet derivative agrees with the norm of the
order-two iterated Fréchet derivative.
items.title: norm_secondFDeriv_eq_norm_iteratedFDeriv_two

items.label: norm_secondFDeriv_indicator_compl_finsum_le_of_tsupport_bound
items.statement:
A supportwise Hessian bound for disjoint shrinking summands gives the same global
bound after their pointwise finsum is extended by zero across the closed cluster set.
items.title: norm_secondFDeriv_indicator_compl_finsum_le_of_tsupport_bound

items.label: norm_secondFDeriv_indicator_compl_finsum_le_of_weighted_tsupport_bound
items.statement:
A weighted supportwise second-derivative estimate gives the uniform Hessian bound
for the zero extension of a disjoint finsum, provided the value and first-derivative
decay hypotheses needed at the cluster set are available.
items.title: norm_secondFDeriv_indicator_compl_finsum_le_of_weighted_tsupport_bound

items.label: quadraticQuantity_mem_Icc_of_norm_mem_Icc
items.statement:
A norm interval and a quadratic comparison in that norm give a quadratic
interval at the underlying scale.
items.title: quadraticQuantity_mem_Icc_of_norm_mem_Icc

items.label: slowCurveBumpCorrectionHessianBound
items.statement:
Lemma 5.10 (Global Hessian bound for the bump correction): one positive
constant chosen before the final initial scale bounds the Hessian of the global
bump correction at every point by that constant times the initial scale.
items.title: slowCurveBumpCorrectionHessianBound

items.label: slowCurveBumpCorrection_eqOn_zero
items.statement: The source-presented global bump correction vanishes on its limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveBumpCorrection_eqOn_zero

items.label: slowCurveBumpCorrection_gradient_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The source-presented gradient of the global bump correction vanishes on
its limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveBumpCorrection_gradient_eqOn_zero

items.label: slowCurveBumpCorrection_hessian_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The source-presented Hessian of the global bump correction vanishes on its
limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveBumpCorrection_hessian_eqOn_zero

items.label: slowCurveBumpFDerivUniformBound
items.statement:
Lemma 5.5 (Uniform supportwise value, gradient, and Hessian bounds) (2):
uniformly over sufficiently small initial scales, the norm of the first Fréchet
derivative (the source gradient) of each endpoint bump on its support is bounded by a
constant times the cycle scale and the endpoint radius.
items.title: slowCurveBumpFDerivUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveBumpSecondFDerivUniformBound
items.statement:
Lemma 5.5 (Uniform supportwise value, gradient, and Hessian bounds) (3):
uniformly over sufficiently small initial scales, the norm of the second Fréchet
derivative (the source Hessian) of each endpoint bump on its support is bounded by a
constant times the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveBumpSecondFDerivUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveBumpValueUniformBound
items.statement:
Lemma 5.5 (Uniform supportwise value, gradient, and Hessian bounds) (1):
uniformly over sufficiently small initial scales, the value of each endpoint bump on
its support is bounded by a constant times the cycle scale and the square of the
endpoint radius.
items.title: slowCurveBumpValueUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveInterpolationClosedBallDisjointLimitCircle
items.statement:
Lemma 5.1 (Isolation radii and pairwise-disjoint interpolation balls) (3):
uniformly over sufficiently small initial scales, every closed interpolation ball is
disjoint from the limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveInterpolationClosedBallDisjointLimitCircle

items.label: slowCurveInterpolationRadiusUniformBounds
items.statement:
Lemma 5.1 (Isolation radii and pairwise-disjoint interpolation balls) (1):
uniformly over sufficiently small initial scales, every interpolation radius is bounded
above and below by positive multiples of the squared scale of its cycle.
items.title: slowCurveInterpolationRadiusUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurvePairwiseDisjointInterpolationClosedBalls
items.statement:
Lemma 5.1 (Isolation radii and pairwise-disjoint interpolation balls) (2):
uniformly over sufficiently small initial scales, the closed interpolation balls are
pairwise disjoint.
items.title: slowCurvePairwiseDisjointInterpolationClosedBalls

items.label: slowCurveRealizedObjectiveHessianBounds
items.statement:
Proposition 5.12a (Global Hessian bounds) (2): whenever
`K * ε₀ ≤ 1 / 2`, the Hessian of the realized objective lies globally between
`(1 / 2)I` and `(3 / 2)I`.
items.title: slowCurveRealizedObjectiveHessianBounds

items.label: squaredNorm_div_mem_Icc_of_norm_mem_Icc
items.statement:
Separate positive norm and decrease intervals give a uniform interval for
their squared-norm-to-decrease ratio.
items.title: squaredNorm_div_mem_Icc_of_norm_mem_Icc

items.label: tendsto_norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_div_infDist_pow
items.statement:
A supportwise scaled decay estimate for disjoint shrinking summands gives the
same decay for their pointwise finsum along the complement of the cluster set.
items.title: tendsto_norm_iteratedFDeriv_finsum_div_infDist_pow

items.label: tendsto_of_tendsto_even_odd
items.statement:
If the even and odd subsequences of a sequence converge to the same point,
the whole sequence converges to that point.
items.title: tendsto_of_tendsto_even_odd

items.label: slowCurveFrameAngleExpansion
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.8 (Specialized frame-angle expansion): on an invariant
slow curve with the fixed cubic and quartic shape jets, the actual curve's
frame-angle increment is
`-3 * ε ^ 2 - (196 / 5) * ε ^ 5 + (28 / 5) * ε ^ 6 + O(ε ^ 7)`.
This transports the polynomial calculation on `DFP.TwoLeg.slowGraphJetPath`
to explicit invariant slow-curve functions.
items.title: slowCurveFrameAngleExpansion

items.label: slowCurveRealizedObjective_strongConvexOn
items.statement:
Corollary 5.12b (Global strong and uniform convexity): the realized objective is
globally `(1 / 2)`-strongly convex and therefore uniformly convex with quadratic modulus
`(fun r ↦ (1 / 2 : ℝ) / 2 * r ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveRealizedObjective_strongConvexOn

items.label: orthogonalSumObjectiveHessianBounds
items.statement:
Corollary 6.7 (Extension to every dimension $n\ge2$) (2): adjoining the
quadratic complement `‖w‖ ^ 2 / 2` preserves the global Hessian bounds
`(1 / 2)I ≼ ∇²f ≼ (3 / 2)I`.
items.title: orthogonalSumObjectiveHessianBounds

items.label: orthogonalSumGradientNormTendsto_iff
items.statement:
Corollary 6.7 (Extension to every dimension $n\ge2$) (5): zero-component
embedding preserves the limiting gradient norm, hence also its positive limit.
items.title: orthogonalSumGradientNormTendsto_iff

items.label: extendedMap_base
items.statement: The analytically extended complete map fixes the factored base point.
items.title: extendedMap_base

items.label: slowCurveFirstEndpointAngleIncrement
items.statement:
Lemma 3.24 (Leading within-cycle endpoint-gradient angle increments) (1):
on an invariant slow curve with the fixed shape jets, the real lift of the
first endpoint-gradient angle increment is `-2 * ε ^ 2 + o(ε ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveFirstEndpointAngleIncrement

items.label: slowCurveSecondEndpointAngleIncrement
items.statement:
Lemma 3.24 (Leading within-cycle endpoint-gradient angle increments) (2):
on an invariant slow curve with the fixed shape jets, the real lift of the
second endpoint-gradient angle increment is `-ε ^ 2 + o(ε ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveSecondEndpointAngleIncrement

items.label: slowCurveInitialLowVector
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c1: the initial slow-curve state has the standard basis
as its physical low vector.
items.title: slowCurveInitialLowVector

items.label: endpointPolarLiftFrameBase
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c1: the initial endpoint lift is the physical correction
when the initial low vector is the standard basis.
items.title: endpointPolarLiftFrameBase

items.label: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotientAt
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c1: at one even endpoint, the frame representation
identifies the lifted polar quotient with the physical low-vector angle.
items.title: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotientAt

items.label: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotient
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c1: the frame representation supplies the initial and
all even-index quotient identities simultaneously.
items.title: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotient

items.label: standardBasis_oangle_rotation
items.statement:
The oriented angle from the standard basis to its planar rotation is the
rotation parameter itself.
items.title: standardBasis_oangle_rotation

items.label: slowCurveInitialGradientAngle_tendsto_zero
items.statement:
The Lemma 4.8c1 slow-graph gradient angle tends to the principal branch at the
base point, uniformly after restricting the scale to a small metric ball.
items.title: slowCurveInitialGradientAngle_tendsto_zero

items.label: lowVector_gradientAngle_toReal_eq
items.statement:
The Lemma 4.8c1 low-vector to even-gradient angle is the coordinate slope
angle in the current oriented frame.
items.title: lowVector_gradientAngle_toReal_eq

items.label: radialPerturbationAngleBounds
items.statement:
A small radial perturbation has a uniformly small oriented-angle error when
the unperturbed gradient has a positive norm lower bound.
items.title: radialPerturbationAngleBounds

items.label: oangle_toReal_add_small
items.statement:
The Lemma 4.8c1 sum of two principal oriented-angle representatives remains
principal and is bounded by the sum of their absolute values.
items.title: oangle_toReal_add_small

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleLiftCompatible
items.statement:
Lemma 4.8c1 (Compatible real lifts of the physical endpoint polar angles):
below one common slow-curve threshold, consecutive lifted endpoint angles are
the unique small signed representatives of their quotient-valued gaps, and the
even lifts differ from the physical frame lift by the endpoint-to-frame correction.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleLiftCompatible

items.label: polarVectorRemainderOfRadialRemainder
items.statement:
Scalar little-o remainders remain little-o after multiplication by an
eventually unit vector-valued direction.
items.title: polarVectorRemainderOfRadialRemainder

items.label: boundaryModel_sub_lowVector
items.statement:
The quadratic boundary model differs from the low frame vector by its
second transported frame column.
items.title: boundaryModel_sub_lowVector

items.label: boundaryFrameColumnNorms
items.statement: The first and second columns of a special-orthogonal frame have unit norm.
items.title: boundaryFrameColumnNorms

items.label: endpointSubCenterNonzero
items.statement:
Uniform gradient and center-tail bounds exclude endpoint coincidence with a
limiting center on sufficiently small slow-curve orbits.
items.title: endpointSubCenterNonzero

items.label: slowCurveInitialLowVector
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): the initial
slow-curve low vector is the first standard basis vector.
items.title: slowCurveInitialLowVector

items.label: endpointPolarLiftFrameBase
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): the initial
lift/frame difference is the physical initial correction angle.
items.title: endpointPolarLiftFrameBase

items.label: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotientAt
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): an even
lift/frame quotient equals the oriented angle from the low vector to the endpoint.
items.title: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotientAt

items.label: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotient
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): the initial
and all even endpoint quotient identities form one reusable lift interface.
items.title: endpointPolarLiftFrameQuotient

items.label: lowVectorGradientAngle_toReal
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): the angle
from a valid state's low vector to its gradient is its normalized coordinate angle.
items.title: lowVectorGradientAngle_toReal

items.label: oangleToReal_add_small
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): two
successive small oriented angles compose without leaving the principal branch.
items.title: oangleToReal_add_small

items.label: slowCurveNormalizedGradientAngleTendsto
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): the
normalized slow-curve gradient angle tends to zero with the scale.
items.title: slowCurveNormalizedGradientAngleTendsto

items.label: ofSlowCurveScaleAndShape
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): a slow-graph
iterate gives the scale bound and shape coordinate of the corresponding orbit state.
items.title: ofSlowCurveScaleAndShape

items.label: lowVectorGradientAngleSmallOfShape
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): a valid
state on the slow graph inherits the normalized coordinate-angle bound.
items.title: lowVectorGradientAngleSmallOfShape

items.label: slowCurveLowGradientAngleSmall
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): on a
small slow-curve orbit, every low-vector-to-gradient angle lies in a fixed
principal subinterval.
items.title: slowCurveLowGradientAngleSmall

items.label: evenPhysicalCorrectionSmallOfLiftDifference
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): a small
low-to-gradient angle and a small lifted gradient-to-endpoint correction give
a small physical low-to-endpoint angle.
items.title: evenPhysicalCorrectionSmallOfLiftDifference

items.label: slowCurveEvenPolarPhysicalCorrectionBound
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): boundary
expansion controls the even physical endpoint correction by a quadratic scale.
items.title: slowCurveEvenPolarPhysicalCorrectionBound

items.label: slowCurveEvenPolarPhysicalCorrectionSmall
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): below one
uniform scale, every even physical low-vector correction lies in the principal
eighth-turn interval.
items.title: slowCurveEvenPolarPhysicalCorrectionSmall

items.label: slowCurveEvenPolarPhysicalCorrectionControl
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation): one
threshold supplies both global principal-branch control and the eventual
quadratic physical-correction bound.
items.title: slowCurveEvenPolarPhysicalCorrectionControl

items.label: allIndexSquareBoundOfEventually
items.statement:
An eventual quadratic bound on a positive antitone sequence extends to all
indices when the bounded quantity has a positive global bound.
items.title: allIndexSquareBoundOfEventually

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarRepresentation
items.statement:
Lemma 4.8c (Two-phase endpoint polar representation) (1): for both endpoint
phases of every sufficiently small slow-curve orbit, the endpoint displacement
has the canonical polar direction and current amplitude up to `o(ε_j ^ 2)`,
while its lifted polar angle differs from the cycle frame by `O(ε_j ^ 2)`.
The current amplitude converges to the prescribed positive limit `Glim`.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarRepresentation

items.label: slowCurveEndpointClusterPt_mem_limitCircle
items.statement:
Lemma 4.9a (All endpoint cluster points lie on $\Gamma$ and $\mathcal E$ is closed) (1):
every `atTop` cluster point of the endpoint sequence of a sufficiently small
slow-curve orbit belongs to its limiting circle `Γ`.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointClusterPt_mem_limitCircle

items.label: isClosed_slowCurveClosedSetCandidate
items.statement:
Lemma 4.9a (All endpoint cluster points lie on $\Gamma$ and $\mathcal E$ is closed) (2):
the union `𝓔` of the limiting circle and the endpoint range of a sufficiently
small slow-curve orbit is closed.
items.title: isClosed_slowCurveClosedSetCandidate

items.label: slowCurveInterpolationRadiusTendstoZero
items.statement:
Lemma 5.1a (Shrinking support radii and support accumulation only on $\Gamma$) (1):
uniformly over sufficiently small slow-curve orbits, the interpolation radii tend to
zero.
items.title: slowCurveInterpolationRadiusTendstoZero

items.label: slowCurveAffineCutoffBumpSupportSubsetInterpolationClosedBall
items.statement:
Every affine-cutoff support lies in the closed interpolation ball centered at the
corresponding endpoint, uniformly over sufficiently small slow-curve orbits. This is
conclusion (3) of Lemma 5.1a (Shrinking support radii and support accumulation only on
$\Gamma$).
items.title: slowCurveAffineCutoffBumpSupportSubsetInterpolationClosedBall

items.label: slowCurveInterpolationBallsEventuallyNearLimitCircle
items.statement:
Every positive closed thickening of the limiting circle eventually contains every
interpolation ball, uniformly over sufficiently small slow-curve orbits. This is
conclusion (4) of Lemma 5.1a (Shrinking support radii and support accumulation only on
$\Gamma$).
items.title: slowCurveInterpolationBallsEventuallyNearLimitCircle

items.label: endpointBump_tsum_eq_zero
items.statement:
Lemma 5.3a (Pointwise summability and unique active bump) (4): when every
endpoint bump vanishes at `z`, their pointwise tsum is zero.
items.title: endpointBump_tsum_eq_zero

items.label: endpointBump_fderiv
items.statement:
Lemma 5.4 (First and second derivative formulas for each bump) (1):
the first Fréchet derivative of an endpoint correction bump.
items.title: endpointBump_fderiv

items.label: endpointBump_secondFDeriv_apply
items.statement:
Lemma 5.4 (First and second derivative formulas for each bump) (2):
the second Fréchet derivative of an endpoint correction bump, evaluated on two directions.
items.title: endpointBump_secondFDeriv_apply

items.label: slowCurveBumpSupportDistanceBounds
items.statement:
Lemma 5.6 (Support distance is comparable to the cycle scale) (1): eventually,
every point in the support of the `k`th endpoint bump has distance from the limiting
circle bounded above and below by positive multiples of the scale of cycle `k / 2`.
items.title: slowCurveBumpSupportDistanceBounds

items.label: slowCurveInterpolationRadiusIsBigO
items.statement:
The quadratic-radius assertion of Lemma 5.6 (Support distance is comparable to the
cycle scale): the interpolation radius is eventually bounded by a constant multiple of
the squared scale of its cycle.
items.title: slowCurveInterpolationRadiusIsBigO

items.label: slowCurveBumpValueDistSqDecay
items.statement:
Lemma 5.7 (Vanishing second-order jets at the limiting circle) (4): the endpoint
bump value divided by squared distance to the limiting circle tends uniformly to zero
along support points approaching that circle.
items.title: slowCurveBumpValueDistSqDecay

items.label: slowCurveBumpFDerivDistDecay
items.statement:
Lemma 5.7 (Vanishing second-order jets at the limiting circle) (5): the norm of
the first Fréchet derivative divided by distance to the limiting circle tends uniformly
to zero along support points approaching that circle.
items.title: slowCurveBumpFDerivDistDecay

items.label: slowCurveBumpSecondFDerivDecay
items.statement:
Lemma 5.7 (Vanishing second-order jets at the limiting circle) (6): the norm of
the second Fréchet derivative tends uniformly to zero along support points approaching
the limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveBumpSecondFDerivDecay

items.label: fderiv_eq
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.26 (Derivative formulas and scale bounds for affine cutoff bumps) (1):
the first Fréchet derivative of the affine cutoff bump.
items.title: fderiv_eq

items.label: secondFDeriv_apply
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.26 (Derivative formulas and scale bounds for affine cutoff bumps) (2):
the second Fréchet derivative of the affine cutoff bump, evaluated on two directions.
items.title: secondFDeriv_apply

items.label: norm_le
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.26 (Derivative formulas and scale bounds for affine cutoff bumps) (3):
the value bound on the support at positive scale.
items.title: norm_le

items.label: norm_fderiv_le
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.26 (Derivative formulas and scale bounds for affine cutoff bumps) (4):
the first-derivative bound on the support at positive scale.
items.title: norm_fderiv_le

items.label: norm_secondFDeriv_le
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.26 (Derivative formulas and scale bounds for affine cutoff bumps) (5):
the second-derivative bound on the support at positive scale.
items.title: norm_secondFDeriv_le

items.label: le_sub_sum_range_of_succ_add_le
items.statement:
A one-step decrease inequality bounds the later value by the initial value minus the
partial sum of the nonnegative increments.
items.title: le_sub_sum_range_of_succ_add_le

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_succ_add_le_of_not_summable
items.statement:
A real sequence that decreases by nonnegative increments whose series is not summable
tends to `atBot`.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_succ_add_le_of_not_summable

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_succ_add_le_of_not_summable
items.statement:
A real sequence that eventually decreases by nonnegative increments with a
nonsummable series tends to `atBot`.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_succ_add_le_of_not_summable

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_le_decrement_of_not_summable
items.statement:
If the eventual decrement of a real sequence dominates a positive multiple of a
nonnegative nonsummable sequence, then the original sequence tends to `atBot`.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_le_decrement_of_not_summable

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_abs_forwardDiff_add_le_of_not_summable
items.statement:
An eventual absolute error bound around a negative leading forward difference forces
divergence to `atBot` when the retained positive part is nonsummable.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_abs_forwardDiff_add_le_of_not_summable

items.label: not_summable_of_nonneg_add_isLittleO
items.statement:
A nonnegative, nonsummable sequence stays nonsummable after an asymptotically smaller
perturbation whenever the perturbed sequence is eventually nonnegative.
items.title: not_summable_of_nonneg_add_isLittleO

items.label: not_summable_of_eventually_le_mul
items.statement:
A nonnegative sequence remains nonsummable when another sequence eventually
dominates it by a fixed positive factor.
items.title: not_summable_of_eventually_le_mul

items.label: not_summable_of_eventually_norm_mul_le
items.statement:
A fixed positive lower bound on the terms of a sequence in a complete normed additive
group transfers nonsummability to a real control sequence, without requiring the control
sequence to be pointwise nonnegative.
items.title: not_summable_of_eventually_norm_mul_le

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_abs_forwardDiff_add_le_of_square_vanishing
items.statement:
A fourth-order absolute remainder around the decrement `3 * ε n ^ 2` forces a real
sequence to tend to `atBot` when `ε n` tends to zero and its square is nonsummable.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_abs_forwardDiff_add_le_of_square_vanishing

items.label: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_abs_forwardDiff_add_le_of_vanishing_factor
items.statement:
If the error in a forward-difference estimate is bounded by `C * v n * w n`, where
`w` tends to zero, then a nonsummable nonnegative `v` still forces
the sequence to tend to `atBot`.
items.title: tendsto_atBot_of_eventually_abs_forwardDiff_add_le_of_vanishing_factor

items.label: continuousLinearMap_apply
items.statement:
Applying a continuous linear map transports a uniform remainder bound and scales
its coefficient by the operator norm.
items.title: continuousLinearMap_apply

items.label: fst
items.statement: Projecting to the first factor preserves a uniform remainder coefficient.
items.title: fst

items.label: snd
items.statement: Projecting to the second factor preserves a uniform remainder coefficient.
items.title: snd

items.label: inv_cube_smul_comp_square_isLittleO_one
items.statement:
A uniform quadratic remainder stays `o(1)` after restriction to the parabolic
diagonal `r = ε²` and normalization by `ε³`.
items.title: inv_cube_smul_comp_square_isLittleO_one

items.label: matrixMul
items.statement:
Rectangular matrix multiplication preserves uniform remainder estimates for the scoped
Euclidean `L2Operator` norm.
items.title: matrixMul

items.label: zero
items.statement: The zero remainder has the identically zero uniform remainder modulus.
items.title: zero

items.label: add
items.statement: The sum of two uniform remainders has modulus equal to the sum of their moduli.
items.title: add

items.label: sub
items.statement: The difference of two uniform remainders has modulus equal to the sum of their moduli.
items.title: sub

items.label: finsetSum
items.statement:
A finite sum of uniform remainders has modulus equal to the pointwise sum of the
individual moduli.
items.title: finsetSum

items.label: prod
items.statement:
Two uniform remainder moduli combine into a product-valued modulus by taking their
pointwise maximum.
items.title: prod

items.label: prod
items.statement:
Uniform remainder estimates for two components combine into the product-valued estimate
with the larger of the two coefficients.
items.title: prod

items.label: pi
items.statement:
A finite coordinate family with one common scalar remainder coefficient has the same
coefficient after assembling the coordinates into a dependent function space.
items.title: pi

items.label: pi_of_dominating_coefficient
items.statement:
A finite coordinate family with individually bounded coefficients can be assembled under
any nonnegative coefficient that dominates all coordinate bounds.
items.title: pi_of_dominating_coefficient

items.label: pi_of_finset_sup
items.statement:
A nonempty finite coordinate family inherits a uniform remainder bound with the exact
finite supremum of its nonnegative coordinate coefficients.
items.title: pi_of_finset_sup

items.label: comp_tendsto
items.statement:
A filter-tending reparameterization preserves a uniform remainder estimate when the
transformed real-power gauge has its own uniform estimate.
items.title: comp_tendsto

items.label: weightedPath
items.statement:
A mixed estimate with gauge `|b| ^ p * |r| ^ q` restricts along
`b = ε`, `r = ε ^ 2` to a uniform remainder of order `p + 2 * q`.
items.title: weightedPath

items.label: weightedPathCubic
items.statement:
A mixed cubic estimate in `r` has uniform order six along
`b = ε`, `r = ε ^ 2`.
items.title: weightedPathCubic

items.label: weightedPathLinearCubic
items.statement:
A mixed estimate with gauge `|b| * |r| ^ 3` has uniform order seven along
`b = ε`, `r = ε ^ 2`.
items.title: weightedPathLinearCubic

items.label: finsetSum
items.statement:
A finite sum of uniform remainders of one order has coefficient equal to the
sum of the individual coefficients.
items.title: finsetSum

items.label: analyticAt_recoveryFactors
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.5: analytic spectral and gradient factor pairs give an
analytic recovery package whenever the two quotient denominators are nonzero.
items.title: analyticAt_recoveryFactors

items.label: isBigO_of_threefold_vanishing
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16 (finite-order graph-jet contraction): vanishing zeroth,
first, and second scalar derivatives force a cubic asymptotic bound for a `C^3` map.
items.title: isBigO_of_threefold_vanishing

items.label: hasHessianBounds_indicator_compl_finsum_add_halfNormSq_of_decay
items.statement:
A twice differentiable zero extension of a disjoint shrinking finsum with a supportwise
Hessian bound gives two-sided global Hessian bounds after adding a quadratic base.
items.title: hasHessianBounds_indicator_compl_finsum_add_halfNormSq_of_decay

items.label: strongConvexOn_indicator_compl_finsum_add_halfNormSq_of_decay
items.statement:
A twice differentiable zero extension of a disjoint shrinking finsum is strongly convex
after adding a quadratic base whenever the supportwise Hessian is bounded by `η < 1`.
items.title: strongConvexOn_indicator_compl_finsum_add_halfNormSq_of_decay

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_three_eq_zero_of_eventually_secondJet_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.15: a locally zero evaluation of a `C³` second jet has
zero derivative in every parameter direction, hence zero third mixed jet.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_three_eq_zero_of_eventually_secondJet_zero

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_three_eq_zero_of_eventually_affine_secondJet_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Lemma 4.15: the same vanishing conclusion holds after translating
   the parameter slice by a fixed base point.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_three_eq_zero_of_eventually_affine_secondJet_zero

items.label: IsUniformOn.eventually_cubic_bound_of_coeff_zero

items.label: exists_cubic_bound_of_contDiffAt_of_iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero

items.label: eventually_cubic_bound_of_contDiffAt_of_iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero

items.label: coeff_postcompContinuousLinearMap

the original remainder.

items.label: weighted_transverse_isBigO
items.statement:
If two parameter paths differ by `O(a)` and the derivative of every fixed-index
slice is uniformly `O(b)` along the segment joining them, then their images differ

transport.
items.title: weighted_transverse_isBigO

items.label: weighted_transverse_pow_isBigO
items.statement:

path perturbation and an `O(ε^k)` slice derivative produce an
`O(ε^(m+k))` image perturbation.
items.title: weighted_transverse_pow_isBigO

Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the transported increment estimate at a
source pair exposes the second projection needed by the graph-transform proof.

items.label: TransportedIncrementRecurrenceData.iterate_at_pair
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: recurrence iteration at `(u, t)` keeps
the terminal state and the geometric forcing factor in source notation.
items.title: TransportedIncrementRecurrenceData.iterate_at_pair

items.label: FiniteTransportedIncrementBudgetCertificate.terminal_error_le_at_pair

Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a finite transported-increment budget
certificate exposes its terminal estimate at the source pair `(u, t)`.
items.title: FiniteTransportedIncrementBudgetCertificate.terminal_error_le_at_pair

items.label: FiniteTransportedIncrementBudgetCertificate.source_budget_interface
items.statement:
