forcing budget are the explicit terminal data consumed by the finite estimate.
items.title: FiniteTransportedIncrementBudgetCertificate.source_budget_interface

items.label: transportedIncrementError_le_of_source_fields
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: explicit source recurrence, terminal, and forcing
fields assemble through the existing finite certificate and bound the error at
the source pair `(u, t)`.
items.title: transportedIncrementError_le_of_source_fields

items.label: TransportedIncrementRecurrenceData.iterate

Infrastructure I.16a: iterating a transported-increment recurrence exposes
the terminal error and the geometric forcing budget at the original increment.
items.title: TransportedIncrementRecurrenceData.iterate

items.label: FiniteTransportedIncrementBudgetCertificate.error_le_budget
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the finite transported-increment certificate bounds
the initial error by its declared terminal-plus-forcing budget.
items.title: FiniteTransportedIncrementBudgetCertificate.error_le_budget

items.label: centerProjection_dist_apply_le_of_center_fiber
items.statement:
The center coordinate maps of two small graphs differ by the center-fiber bound
when their graph values are compared at the same parameter.
items.title: centerProjection_dist_apply_le_of_center_fiber

items.label: map_dist_apply_le_of_inverse_dist
items.statement:
The stable output of the graph transform satisfies the quantitative distance estimate
once the two inverse center parameters have a uniform distance bound.
items.title: map_dist_apply_le_of_inverse_dist

items.label: contractingWith_of_center_fiber
items.statement:
The graph transform is a strict contraction when the center-fiber estimate controls
the inverse center parameters.
items.title: contractingWith_of_center_fiber

items.label: GraphTransformContractionData.transform_apply
items.statement:
Expose the concrete formula for the packaged graph-transform map so downstream modules do
not need to unfold an opaque definition across an import boundary.
items.title: GraphTransformContractionData.transform_apply

items.label: GraphTransformContractionData.transform_contracting
items.statement: The packaged transform is contracting with the rate supplied by the data.
items.title: GraphTransformContractionData.transform_contracting

items.label: GraphTransformContractionData.exists_fixedGraph
items.statement: A complete quantitative data package produces a fixed graph of the cutoff transform.
items.title: GraphTransformContractionData.exists_fixedGraph

items.label: GraphTransformContractionData.fixedGraph_invariant
items.statement:
The fixed graph supplied by the contraction package is forward invariant after the
center-coordinate inverse is cancelled.
items.title: GraphTransformContractionData.fixedGraph_invariant

items.label: exists_invariantGraph_of_explicit_contraction
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a (Finite-smooth invariant graph under an explicit stable contraction):
quantitative graph-transform data together with a finite-smoothness witness yields the invariant
graph, its zero value, and the zero stable tangent required by the source statement.
items.title: exists_invariantGraph_of_explicit_contraction

items.label: transform_fixedPoint_contDiff_of_bunching
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a fixed point of the explicit graph-transform map is
finite-smooth when the transform satisfies the bunching inequality at every order.
items.title: transform_fixedPoint_contDiff_of_bunching

items.label: exists_finiteSmooth_fixedGraph_of_bunching
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a (finite-smooth invariant graph under an explicit stable contraction):
the explicit graph-transform map has a finite-smooth fixed graph under the same bunching
certificate.
items.title: exists_finiteSmooth_fixedGraph_of_bunching

items.label: fixedGraph_invariant_of_explicit_map
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: an explicit fixed graph of the inverse-center transform
obeys the forward-invariance equation before the center inverse is cancelled.
items.title: fixedGraph_invariant_of_explicit_map

items.label: invariantGraph_of_bunched_cutoff_germ
items.statement:
A quantitative cutoff certificate and its bunching inequalities transfer a finite-smooth
  invariant graph to any original map with the same germ at the fixed point.

  The certificate is intentionally an explicit input: local differentiability of an original
  map alone does not provide the global support, radius, inverse-center, or Lipschitz bounds
  required by the graph transform.
items.title: invariantGraph_of_bunched_cutoff_germ

items.label: invariantGraph_of_finiteSmoothCertificate
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a (paper-facing finite-smooth invariant graph): a quantitative cutoff
certificate and a certified original-map germ produce a finite-smooth invariant graph through
the fixed point with zero stable tangent.  The certificate remains an explicit input; this
theorem does not claim that the bare local hypotheses construct it automatically.
items.title: invariantGraph_of_finiteSmoothCertificate

items.label: secantCertificateOneSectionValue_curryLeft
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the curry-left evaluation of the represented section
is the continuous linear map determined by its secant limit.
items.title: secantCertificateOneSectionValue_curryLeft

items.label: continuous_secantCertificateOneSectionValue
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: continuity of the represented limiting section follows
from bounded-section continuity and the canonical scalar-source multilinear equivalence.
items.title: continuous_secantCertificateOneSectionValue

items.label: secantCertificateOneSectionValue_hasFDerivAt
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the represented secant section has the bundled
predecessor derivative required by the order-one holonomic interface.
items.title: secantCertificateOneSectionValue_hasFDerivAt

items.label: MetricCanonicalOrderwiseCertificate.toHolonomicCertificate
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: canonical orderwise operator data directly produces the holonomic
fixed-graph certificate, while retaining the source predecessor equations in the result.
items.title: MetricCanonicalOrderwiseCertificate.toHolonomicCertificate

items.label: MetricCanonicalOrderwiseCertificate.contDiff
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: canonical orderwise contraction and predecessor data, together with
the explicit bunching inequalities, yield finite smoothness of the metric fixed graph.
items.title: MetricCanonicalOrderwiseCertificate.contDiff

items.label: MetricTopSectionOperatorCertificate.fixedSection_unique
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the fixed section recorded in an operator certificate is
the unique fixed point supplied by its strict contraction.
items.title: MetricTopSectionOperatorCertificate.fixedSection_unique

items.label: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_operatorCertificates
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: orderwise section-operator certificates assemble into the
holonomic certificate consumed by the finite-smooth metric bootstrap.  The fixed sections are
obtained canonically from the existing bounded-section contraction theorem.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_operatorCertificates

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_operatorCertificates
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a complete family of section-operator certificates directly yields
the finite smoothness of the metric fixed graph.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_operatorCertificates

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_holonomicFixedTopSectionCertificates
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a family of holonomic graph-jet fixed-section certificates gives the
metric finite-smoothness conclusion through the shared contraction and successor bootstrap.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_holonomicFixedTopSectionCertificates

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_canonicalTopSectionOperators
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: contraction data and predecessor derivative equations for the canonical
fixed sections directly yield the finite-smooth metric graph.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_canonicalTopSectionOperators

items.title: MetricFiniteSmoothCertificate.toHolonomicCertificate

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_finiteSmoothCertificate

items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_finiteSmoothCertificate

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_and_topSections_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
The order-by-order induction also identifies every certified top section with the next
iterated derivative of the fixed graph.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_and_topSections_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_holonomicFixedTopSectionCertificates
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a family of holonomic graph-jet fixed-section

interface; the operator and predecessor obligations remain in the inputs.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_holonomicFixedTopSectionCertificates

items.label: continuous_iteratedFDeriv_one_of_contDiff
items.statement:

`C^1` graph is a continuous section.
items.title: continuous_iteratedFDeriv_one_of_contDiff

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_one_hasFDerivAt_ftaylor_zero
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the first iterated derivative of a globally

items.title: iteratedFDeriv_one_hasFDerivAt_ftaylor_zero

items.label: MetricOrderwiseCertificateAssembly.toHolonomicCertificate
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: an orderwise assembly projects to the holonomic
fixed-graph certificate independently of the bunching inequalities.
items.title: MetricOrderwiseCertificateAssembly.toHolonomicCertificate

items.label: MetricOrderwiseCertificateAssembly.contDiff
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a complete orderwise contraction-and-holonomicity
assembly yields the finite smoothness of the metric fixed graph.
items.title: MetricOrderwiseCertificateAssembly.contDiff

items.label: MetricOrderwiseCertificateAssembly.contDiff_and_topSections_eq_iteratedFDeriv

sections with the iterated derivatives of the fixed graph.
items.title: MetricOrderwiseCertificateAssembly.contDiff_and_topSections_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: scalarTopSectionValue_curryLeft
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: currying the canonical scalar section
recovers the scalar-multiplication map on the embedded derivative value.
items.title: scalarTopSectionValue_curryLeft

items.label: scalarTopSectionValue_curryLeft_eq_comp
items.statement:

composition of the multilinear embedding with the one-dimensional derivative.
items.title: scalarTopSectionValue_curryLeft_eq_comp

items.label: ScalarTopJetDerivativeData.hasFDerivAt_section
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a scalar predecessor derivative gives the
bundled holonomic derivative of the corresponding multilinear Taylor section.
items.title: ScalarTopJetDerivativeData.hasFDerivAt_section

items.label: continuous_topSectionValue_of_continuous
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: continuity of a scalar top-jet value
field transports through the canonical multilinear section embedding.
items.title: continuous_topSectionValue_of_continuous

items.label: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.factor_lt_one
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: the source bunching inequality makes the
metric factor of one candidate operator a strict NNReal contraction factor.
items.title: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.factor_lt_one

items.label: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.toHolonomicCertificate
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the source-facing top-section package exposes the
holonomic fixed-graph certificate independently of the bunching conclusion.
items.title: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.toHolonomicCertificate

items.label: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.contDiff
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the complete source-facing top-section package gives
finite smoothness of the metric fixed graph.  Bare bunching alone is not enough.
items.title: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.contDiff

items.label: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.contDiff_and_fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the source-facing assembly simultaneously gives
finite smoothness and identifies every supplied fixed top section with the
corresponding iterated derivative of the metric fixed graph.
items.title: MetricSourceTopSectionAssembly.contDiff_and_fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: metricFixedGraph_topSectionWitness_of_core
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: a scalar top-jet derivative supplied by the metric core is packaged as
the multilinear holonomic top-section witness at one positive order.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_topSectionWitness_of_core

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_and_topSection_of_core
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: an explicit metric top-section core supplies both finite smoothness and
the holonomic witness at every order in the declared range.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_and_topSection_of_core

items.label: metricFixedGraph_topSection_of_core
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the core projection exposes the orderwise top-section field needed by
downstream metric holonomic certificates without reconstructing the finite-smooth induction.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_topSection_of_core

items.label: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_fixedGraphJetContexts
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: an orderwise family of fixed graph jet contexts
projects to the existential metric holonomic certificate at every declared order.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_fixedGraphJetContexts

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_fixedGraphJetContexts
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the fixed graph jet-context family directly yields finite
smoothness after its explicit predecessor derivative and contraction data have been supplied.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_fixedGraphJetContexts

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_topSectionData
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the source-facing top-section family directly yields
the `ContDiff` conclusion after all operator and holonomicity certificates are supplied.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_topSectionData

items.label: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_topSectionData
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the same source-facing top-section family also exposes
the orderwise holonomic certificate needed by fixed-jet realization.  This is a
projection bridge; all operator estimates and predecessor derivative equations
remain explicit in the inputs.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_topSectionData

items.label: metricTopSectionBunchingFactor_coe
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: coercing the NNReal top-section factor gives the real
bunching expression used by `MetricFiniteSmooth`.
items.title: metricTopSectionBunchingFactor_coe

items.label: metricTopSectionBunchingFactor_lt_one_of_bunching
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the original real bunching inequality implies strictness of the
nonnegative factor used by the bounded-section contraction certificate.
items.title: metricTopSectionBunchingFactor_lt_one_of_bunching

items.label: metricTopSectionBunchingFactor_lt_one_of_real

corresponding strict inequality for the nonnegative factor used by contraction certificates.
items.title: metricTopSectionBunchingFactor_lt_one_of_real

items.label: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_contraction_and_data

Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: contraction-and-holonomic data assemble directly into the
metric fixed-graph certificate used by finite-smooth regularity arguments.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_contraction_and_data

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_contraction_and_data
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the preceding contraction-and-data package directly yields finite
smoothness of the metric fixed graph.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_contraction_and_data

items.label: invariantGraph_of_cutoff_germ
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: a cutoff-model invariant graph transfers to an
original map that has the same germ at the fixed point.
items.title: invariantGraph_of_cutoff_germ

items.label: centerStableLinearize_hasFDerivAt_of_zeroDerivative
items.statement:

items.label: invariantGraph_of_zeroDerivative_cutoff_germ
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure I.16a: combines the zero-derivative remainder bridge with
the cutoff-germ transfer, so an original map can consume the quantitative contraction data
without separately constructing the derivative certificate.
items.title: invariantGraph_of_zeroDerivative_cutoff_germ

items.label: polarDistance_ge_max
items.statement:
In a positive annulus, the distance between two polar points dominates both their radial
separation and their principal angular separation.
items.title: polarDistance_ge_max

items.label: strongConvexOnOfHessianLowerBound
items.statement:
A twice continuously differentiable function on the Euclidean plane with a global
positive lower bound on its Hessian quadratic form is strongly convex on the whole plane.
items.title: strongConvexOnOfHessianLowerBound

items.label: symm_pushforward_pushforward
items.statement:
Pushing an endomorphism forward and then back along an equivalence returns the original
endomorphism.
items.title: symm_pushforward_pushforward

items.label: pushforward_symm_pushforward
items.statement:
Pushing an endomorphism back and then forward along an equivalence returns the original
endomorphism.
items.title: pushforward_symm_pushforward

items.label: symm_pullback_pullback
items.statement:
Pulling an endomorphism back and then forward along an equivalence returns the original
endomorphism.
items.title: symm_pullback_pullback

items.label: pullback_symm_pullback
items.statement:
Pulling an endomorphism forward and then back along an equivalence returns the original
endomorphism.
items.title: pullback_symm_pullback

items.label: isPositive_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A nonnegative Loewner lower bound makes a continuous self-endomorphism positive.
items.title: isPositive_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: antilipschitzWith_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A strict Loewner lower bound gives a quantitative inverse-distance estimate for the operator.
items.title: antilipschitzWith_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: isUnit_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A strict Loewner lower bound makes a continuous self-endomorphism invertible.
items.title: isUnit_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: ker_eq_bot_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A strict Loewner lower bound forces the operator kernel to be trivial.
items.title: ker_eq_bot_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: range_eq_top_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A strict Loewner lower bound forces the operator range to be all of the space.
items.title: range_eq_top_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: exists_sqrt_factorization_of_lowerBound_of_cfc
items.statement:
A real continuous functional calculus turns a strict Loewner lower bound into an invertible
self-adjoint square-root factor whose pushforward of the identity is the original operator.
items.title: exists_sqrt_factorization_of_lowerBound_of_cfc

items.label: exists_sqrtEquiv_of_lowerBound_of_cfc
items.statement:
A CFC square-root factorization can be upgraded from an invertible operator to a
continuous linear equivalence with the same self-adjoint pushforward identity.
items.title: exists_sqrtEquiv_of_lowerBound_of_cfc

items.label: exists_sqrtEquiv_of_lowerBound_of_finiteDimensional
items.statement:
A uniformly positive self-adjoint operator on a finite-dimensional real inner-product
space admits an invertible self-adjoint square-root factor.
items.title: exists_sqrtEquiv_of_lowerBound_of_finiteDimensional

items.label: exists_sqrtEquiv_normalizing_of_lowerBound_of_finiteDimensional
items.statement:
The inverse square-root coordinates normalize a uniformly positive operator to the
identity.
items.title: exists_sqrtEquiv_normalizing_of_lowerBound_of_finiteDimensional

items.label: tail_rpow_isEquivalent_self_via_power_scale
items.statement:
The power-scale tail asymptotic can be rewritten in terms of the original sequence rather
than its model power, so the coefficient becomes `C ^ p * (p / (q - p))`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isEquivalent_self_via_power_scale

items.label: norm_lowVector
items.statement: On the explicit spectral chart, the gradient-oriented low eigenvector has unit norm.
items.title: norm_lowVector

items.label: lowVector_hasEigenvector
items.statement:
On the explicit spectral chart, changing the sign preserves the low-eigenvector
equation and nonvanishing condition.
items.title: lowVector_hasEigenvector

items.label: inner_lowVector_pos
items.statement:
If the updated gradient is not orthogonal to the original low eigenvector, the
chosen low eigenvector has strictly positive inner product with it.
items.title: inner_lowVector_pos

items.label: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup
items.statement: On the explicit spectral chart, the gradient-oriented frame is special orthogonal.
items.title: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.label: frame_diagonalizes
items.statement:
In the gradient-oriented frame, the symmetric matrix is diagonal with its low
eigenvalue first and high eigenvalue second.
items.title: frame_diagonalizes

items.label: fromBlocks_zero_zero_dotProduct
items.statement:
Helper for the block-congruence bridge: the quadratic form of a zero-cross-block
matrix is the sum of the two diagonal block quadratic forms.
items.title: fromBlocks_zero_zero_dotProduct

items.label: fromBlocks_zero_zero_posSemidef_iff
items.statement:
For the block-congruence bridge, a block diagonal matrix is positive
semidefinite exactly when both diagonal blocks are positive semidefinite.
items.title: fromBlocks_zero_zero_posSemidef_iff

items.label: fromBlocks_zero_zero_posDef_iff
items.statement:
For the block-congruence bridge, a block diagonal matrix is positive
definite exactly when both diagonal blocks are positive definite.
items.title: fromBlocks_zero_zero_posDef_iff

items.label: w_apply
items.statement: The coordinate formula for the secant image.
items.title: w_apply

items.label: control_isHermitian
items.statement: The control matrix is Hermitian over the real coordinate space.
items.title: control_isHermitian

items.label: nextGradient_eq
items.statement: A planar abstract step with these coordinate equations has the displayed next gradient.
items.title: nextGradient_eq

items.label: nextInverseHessian_eq
items.statement: A planar abstract step with these coordinate equations has the displayed next inverse Hessian.
items.title: nextInverseHessian_eq

items.label: components_iff
items.statement: A DFP orbit is equivalent to its four defining component conditions.
items.title: components_iff

items.label: extendMatrix_eq_fromBlocks
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: the canonical extension is the
corresponding identity-block matrix from `Matrix.fromBlocks`.
items.title: extendMatrix_eq_fromBlocks

items.label: posSemidef_congruence_left
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: congruence by a rectangular matrix
preserves positive semidefiniteness.
items.title: posSemidef_congruence_left

items.label: posDef_congruence_left
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: an injective rectangular
congruence preserves positive definiteness.
items.title: posDef_congruence_left

items.label: posSemidef_congruence_iff
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: an invertible left congruence
reflects and preserves positive semidefiniteness.
items.title: posSemidef_congruence_iff

items.label: posDef_congruence_iff
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: an invertible left congruence
reflects and preserves positive definiteness.
items.title: posDef_congruence_iff

items.label: zero_conjTranspose_matrix
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: the zero rectangular block has
zero conjugate transpose.
items.title: zero_conjTranspose_matrix

items.label: sumElim_components_eq
items.statement:
Helper for OrthogonalSum PosDef adapters: a finitely-supported vector on
an orthogonal sum is recovered from its two `Finsupp` components.
items.title: sumElim_components_eq

items.label: extendMatrix_posSemidef_iff
items.statement:
Positive semidefiniteness of an identity-block extension is equivalent to
positive semidefiniteness of its original block.
items.title: extendMatrix_posSemidef_iff

items.label: slowGraphAmplitudeRemainder
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the normalized amplitude equals
`1 - (13 / 2) * ε ^ 4 + (116 / 5) * ε ^ 6 - (976 / 5) * ε ^ 7` up to
`O(ε ^ 8)`.
items.title: slowGraphAmplitudeRemainder

items.label: amplitudeRemainderOfSlowGraphJets
items.statement:
Fifth-order perturbations of the polynomial slow graph preserve the normalized
amplitude ratio's expansion through order seven.
items.title: amplitudeRemainderOfSlowGraphJets

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeDrift
items.statement:
On an invariant graph of the two-leg state map with the prescribed slow-graph
jets, the normalized amplitude ratio equals `1 - (13 / 2) * ε ^ 4` up to
`O(ε ^ 6)`.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeDrift

items.label: slowGraphAmplitudeJet
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the normalized amplitude has
order-seven jet
`1 - (13 / 2) * ε ^ 4 + (116 / 5) * ε ^ 6 - (976 / 5) * ε ^ 7`.
items.title: slowGraphAmplitudeJet

items.label: secondLegAmplitude_eq_gradientFactor
items.statement: The named amplitude function is definitionally the public low gradient factor.
items.title: secondLegAmplitude_eq_gradientFactor

items.label: secondLegAmplitude_analyticAt
items.statement: The second-leg amplitude is real analytic at the canceled base point `(0, 2, 1)`.
items.title: secondLegAmplitude_analyticAt

items.label: secondLegAmplitude_base
items.statement: The second-leg amplitude has normalized base value one.
items.title: secondLegAmplitude_base

items.label: eventually_secondLegAmplitude_ne_zero
items.statement: The low gradient factor is nonzero on some neighborhood of the canceled base point.
items.title: eventually_secondLegAmplitude_ne_zero

items.label: observableMap_amplitude_eq_secondLegAmplitude_eventually
items.statement: Along a path converging to `(0, 2, 1)`, the observable amplitude is the named low factor.
items.title: observableMap_amplitude_eq_secondLegAmplitude_eventually

items.label: slowGraphAmplitudeP_apply
items.statement: The shape coordinate of the slow graph is the cubic-quartic polynomial shown by its path.
items.title: slowGraphAmplitudeP_apply

items.label: slowGraphAmplitudeH_apply
items.statement: The high coordinate of the slow graph is the cubic polynomial shown by its path.
items.title: slowGraphAmplitudeH_apply

items.label: secondLegAmplitude_coordinateEquality
items.statement: The two divided differences reconstruct the amplitude change along a fifth-order path.
items.title: secondLegAmplitude_coordinateEquality

items.label: secondLegAmplitudeCoordinateCoefficients_isBigO
items.statement: The two divided differences are bounded at the base point for fifth-order graph paths.
items.title: secondLegAmplitudeCoordinateCoefficients_isBigO

items.label: secondLegAmplitude_cubicCoordinateFactorization
items.statement:
The concrete cubic factorization and its bounded coefficient estimates hold for fifth-order
perturbations of the polynomial slow graph.
items.title: secondLegAmplitude_cubicCoordinateFactorization

items.label: mixedIndependentRadiusCoefficientGerms
items.statement:
The bounded-control independent-radius cancellation supplies the three local germs on
    the strip `|b| < 1 / 4` for Appendix Lemma A.5 (Mixed-variable expansion of radius,
    shape, and scale). -/
-- TODO: transport the completed independent-radius normal form to `map` on a punctured
-- neighborhood, then assemble its first-order recovered-factor jet into these germs.
-- Route correction: the residual, spectral, recovery, and `ContDiffAt` interfaces now
-- compile in `RecoveryAdapter`; the remaining blocker is the oriented-frame sign bridge
-- and its denominator-free first-order jet, not regularity of the normal form itself.
lemma mixedIndependentRadiusCancellation :
    IndependentRadiusTruncatedGerm
        (fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).1)
          {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)} 3
        (fun n θ ↦ (![0, 1,
          θ.1 * (6 * θ.2.2 + 5 * θ.2.1 - 300) / 18] : Fin 3 → ℝ) n) ∧
      IndependentRadiusTruncatedGerm
        (fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).2.1)
          {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)} 2
        (fun n θ ↦ (![2,
          θ.1 * (6 * θ.2.2 - θ.2.1 + 348) / 9] : Fin 2 → ℝ) n) ∧
      IndependentRadiusTruncatedGerm
        (fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).2.2)
          {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)} 2
        (fun n θ ↦ (![1, 8 * θ.1] : Fin 2 → ℝ) n) := by
  -- First construct the three normal-form germs; their regularity and zero-radius
  -- coefficients are independent of the public removable branch.
  have hnormal := independentRadiusNormalForm_truncatedGerms
  have htransport_radius :
      IndependentRadiusTruncatedGerm
        (fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).1)
          {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)} 3
        (fun n θ ↦ (![0, 1,
          θ.1 * (6 * θ.2.2 + 5 * θ.2.1 - 300) / 18] : Fin 3 → ℝ) n) := by
    refine independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_eventuallyEq
      (f := fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).1)
      (g := fun θ r ↦ (independentRadiusNormalForm θ r).1)
      (K := {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)})
      (m := 3)
      (coeff := fun n θ ↦ (![0, 1,
        θ.1 * (6 * θ.2.2 + 5 * θ.2.1 - 300) / 18] : Fin 3 → ℝ) n)
      ?_ ?_ hnormal.1
    · intro θ hθ
      have hEq := independentRadiusNormalForm_eventuallyEq_map θ hθ
      have hEq' := hEq.symm.fun_comp (fun y : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.1)
      filter_upwards [hEq'] with z hz
      exact hz
    · intro θ hθ
      have hEq := independentRadiusNormalForm_eventuallyEq_map θ hθ
      have hpath : Filter.Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ (θ, r)) (nhds 0) (nhds (θ, 0)) :=
        continuousAt_const.prodMk continuousAt_id
      have hEq' := hEq.symm.comp_tendsto hpath
      have hEq'' := hEq'.fun_comp (fun y : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.1)
      filter_upwards [hEq''] with r hr
      exact hr
  have htransport_shape :
      IndependentRadiusTruncatedGerm
        (fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).2.1)
          {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)} 2
        (fun n θ ↦ (![2,
          θ.1 * (6 * θ.2.2 - θ.2.1 + 348) / 9] : Fin 2 → ℝ) n) := by
    refine independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_eventuallyEq
      (f := fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).2.1)
      (g := fun θ r ↦ (independentRadiusNormalForm θ r).2.1)
      (K := {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)})
      (m := 2)
      (coeff := fun n θ ↦ (![2,
        θ.1 * (6 * θ.2.2 - θ.2.1 + 348) / 9] : Fin 2 → ℝ) n)
      ?_ ?_ hnormal.2.1
    · intro θ hθ
      have hEq := independentRadiusNormalForm_eventuallyEq_map θ hθ
      have hEq' := hEq.symm.fun_comp (fun y : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.2.1)
      filter_upwards [hEq'] with z hz
      exact hz
    · intro θ hθ
      have hEq := independentRadiusNormalForm_eventuallyEq_map θ hθ
      have hpath : Filter.Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ (θ, r)) (nhds 0) (nhds (θ, 0)) :=
        continuousAt_const.prodMk continuousAt_id
      have hEq' := hEq.symm.comp_tendsto hpath
      have hEq'' := hEq'.fun_comp (fun y : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.2.1)
      filter_upwards [hEq''] with r hr
      exact hr
  have htransport_scale :
      IndependentRadiusTruncatedGerm
        (fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).2.2)
          {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)} 2
        (fun n θ ↦ (![1, 8 * θ.1] : Fin 2 → ℝ) n) := by
    refine independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_eventuallyEq
      (f := fun θ r ↦ (map θ.1 (input θ r)).2.2)
      (g := fun θ r ↦ (independentRadiusNormalForm θ r).2.2)
      (K := {θ : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ | |θ.1| < (1 / 4 : ℝ)})
      (m := 2)
      (coeff := fun n θ ↦ (![1, 8 * θ.1] : Fin 2 → ℝ) n)
      ?_ ?_ hnormal.2.2
    · intro θ hθ
      have hEq := independentRadiusNormalForm_eventuallyEq_map θ hθ
      have hEq' := hEq.symm.fun_comp (fun y : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.2.2)
      filter_upwards [hEq'] with z hz
      exact hz
    · intro θ hθ
      have hEq := independentRadiusNormalForm_eventuallyEq_map θ hθ
      have hpath : Filter.Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ (θ, r)) (nhds 0) (nhds (θ, 0)) :=
        continuousAt_const.prodMk continuousAt_id
      have hEq' := hEq.symm.comp_tendsto hpath
      have hEq'' := hEq'.fun_comp (fun y : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ y.2.2)
      filter_upwards [hEq''] with r hr
      exact hr
  exact ⟨htransport_radius, htransport_shape, htransport_scale⟩

items.label: shapeQuadraticGerm_of_componentGerms

Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: four component quadratic germs determine the
    recovered shape germ through order two.
items.title: shapeQuadraticGerm_of_componentGerms

items.label: independentRadiusNormalFormQuadraticGerm
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.6: the independent-radius normal form has the explicit
    radius, shape, and high-scale quadratic germs.
items.title: independentRadiusNormalFormQuadraticGerm

items.label: independentRadiusCoefficientGerm_of_quadraticGerms
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.6: `C³` quadratic germs determine an independent-radius coefficient
    germ with the factorial-normalized coefficients `[a₀, a₁, a₂]`.
items.title: independentRadiusCoefficientGerm_of_quadraticGerms

items.label: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_quadraticGerms
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: the same quadratic certificates give the truncated
    three-term germ whose compact-uniform remainder has order three.
items.title: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_quadraticGerms

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveryFactorQuadraticGerm
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.6: the recovered radius factor has the explicit quadratic
germ obtained from the four second-leg factor germs.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveryFactorQuadraticGerm

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveredRadiusQuadraticGerm
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.6: multiplying the recovered radius factor by the
independent radius yields the quadratic germ of the recovered radius path.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveredRadiusQuadraticGerm

items.label: independentSecondFactorQuadraticGerms_of_residualGerms
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: second-leg residual and gradient quadratic germs determine
the four normalized spectral/gradient factor germs through order two.
items.title: independentSecondFactorQuadraticGerms_of_residualGerms

items.label: independentRadiusSecondFactorQuadraticGerms
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.6: the second-leg factor paths on the independent-radius
path carry the explicit quadratic coefficients used by the recovery map.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondFactorQuadraticGerms

items.label: scalarFamily_eventuallyEq_of_uncurry_radius
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: an uncurried eventual equality specializes to
    an eventual equality on every fixed-parameter radius path.
items.title: scalarFamily_eventuallyEq_of_uncurry_radius

items.label: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_truncatedGerm_generic
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: the normalized second-gradient low coordinate
    carries its exact three-term coefficient germ on an arbitrary parameter set.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_truncatedGerm_generic

items.label: truncatedGerm_of_uncurryEq_secondGradientLow
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.6: any scalar family with a certified uncurried equality to
    the normalized second-gradient low coordinate inherits its exact amplitude
    coefficient germ.
items.title: truncatedGerm_of_uncurryEq_secondGradientLow

items.label: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_scale_quadraticGerm
items.statement:
Infrastructure I.16a: the independent-radius second-gradient low coordinate has a flat
signed-scale quadratic germ after the source substitution `r = ε ^ 2`.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_scale_quadraticGerm

items.label: independentRadiusFirstFactorJets

The first normalized spectral and gradient factors have
    their first-radius jets at the canonical zero-radius base point.
items.title: independentRadiusFirstFactorJets

items.statement:
The normalized second-leg residual triple has its explicit
    first derivative at zero.

The normalized second-leg spectral pair has derivative
    `(b (2 J + P - 12), 8 b)` at zero radius.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondSpectralJet

items.statement:
The normalized second-leg gradient pair has derivative
`(0, 4 b (3 J + P + 12) / 9)` at zero radius.

The normalized second-leg spectral and gradient pairs have their corrected component
jets at the zero-radius base point.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondComponentJetCertificate

items.label: orientedRecoveryTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_frame
items.statement:
An oriented planar frame with the prescribed low/high
    eigenvalue and gradient coordinates produces the normalized recovery triple, independently
    of the global sign chosen by the orientation test.
items.title: orientedRecoveryTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_frame

items.label: euclideanPlane_frame_neg_of_vector
items.statement:
Negating a planar vector negates both columns of its
    canonical orthonormal frame.
items.title: euclideanPlane_frame_neg_of_vector

items.label: orientedEigenframe_frame_negate_gradient_of_inner_ne_zero
items.statement:
Away from the orthogonality boundary, negating the gradient
    flips the oriented low-eigenvector frame by one global sign.
items.title: orientedEigenframe_frame_negate_gradient_of_inner_ne_zero

items.label: independentRawRecoveredTriple_negate_gradient
items.statement:
When the output gradient is not orthogonal to the low
    eigenvector, simultaneous sign changes in the input gradient leave raw recovery unchanged.
items.title: independentRawRecoveredTriple_negate_gradient

items.label: independentRawRecoveredTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_secondStep
items.statement:
After a concrete second raw step has been identified,
    its frame-level recovery data determine the normalized independent-radius triple.
items.title: independentRawRecoveredTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_secondStep

items.label: hasDerivAt_fst_of_prod
items.statement:
A derivative of a product-valued path transports to
    its first coordinate through the canonical one-dimensional derivative map.
items.title: hasDerivAt_fst_of_prod

items.label: hasDerivAt_snd_of_prod
items.statement:
A derivative of a product-valued path transports to
    its second coordinate through the canonical one-dimensional derivative map.
items.title: hasDerivAt_snd_of_prod

    the displayed second-radius derivative through the normalized low-gradient path.

items.statement:

items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: a pointwise chart factorization transfers the
    component quadratic germ to the normalized second-gradient low coordinate.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm_of_chartFactorization

items.label: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm_of_componentCertificate
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: component quadratic germs and a pointwise chart
factorization determine the normalized second-gradient low germ.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm_of_componentCertificate

items.label: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm_of_explicitComponentCertificates
items.statement:
Helper for Appendix Lemma A.6: the canonical second-leg component coefficients
specialize the chart certificate to the displayed low-gradient coefficient.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm_of_explicitComponentCertificates

items.label: independentRadiusFirstFactorQuadraticGerms

factors have explicit quadratic germs along the independent-radius path.
items.title: independentRadiusFirstFactorQuadraticGerms

normal form with the first-leg factor germs.

items.label: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm
items.statement:

items.title: independentRadiusSecondGradientLow_quadraticGerm

normalized shape and scale remainders.
items.title: normalized_transverseIncrement_sub_eq_remainders

A fixed coefficient pair lies in the mixed parameter set for all sufficiently
small signed controls.
items.title: eventually_mem_parameterSet

items.statement:
Uniform quadratic shape and scale expansions imply the normalized transverse
little-o estimate along `b = ε`, `r = ε²`.

items.label: independentRawStep_negate_gradient

One DFP raw step is equivariant under negating its
incoming gradient; its updated matrix is unchanged and its updated gradient is negated.

items.statement:
Simultaneous negation of the two gradient coordinates
does not change the recovered radius quotient.
items.title: recoveryRadius_neg_neg

items.label: recoveryShape_neg_neg
items.statement:
Simultaneous negation of the two gradient coordinates
does not change the recovered shape quotient.
items.title: recoveryShape_neg_neg

items.statement:
A recovered triple is unchanged when both oriented
gradient coordinates are negated.
items.title: recoveryTriple_neg_neg

items.label: independentRawStep_first_eq
items.statement:
The first independent-radius raw step is the
    normalized first-step metric and gradient once its secant-step side conditions
    are supplied.
items.title: independentRawStep_first_eq

items.label: independentRawStep_second_eq
items.statement:
The second independent-radius raw step is the
    normalized second-step metric and gradient for a diagonal first-leg state.
items.title: independentRawStep_second_eq

items.label: independentRadiusNormalForm_analyticAt_of_recoveryFactors
items.statement:
An analytic recovered-factor map gives an analytic
normal-form map after multiplying the radius coordinate into its first factor.
items.title: independentRadiusNormalForm_analyticAt_of_recoveryFactors

items.label: independentRadiusNormalForm_contDiffAt_of_analyticRecovery
items.statement:
The analytic recovery interface yields finite smoothness
of the normal form at every order.
items.title: independentRadiusNormalForm_contDiffAt_of_analyticRecovery

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_analyticAt_of_secondFactors
items.statement:
The parent second-factor analytic declarations
assemble into an analytic recovery package without unfolding the raw DFP map.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_analyticAt_of_secondFactors

items.label: independentRadiusNormalForm_contDiffAt_of_secondFactors
items.statement:
Appendix Lemma A.5: the independent-radius normal form is finite-smooth after
the second-factor analytic declarations have been established.
items.title: independentRadiusNormalForm_contDiffAt_of_secondFactors

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_eq_analyticRecovery
items.statement:
The concrete independent-radius recovery triple is
    represented pointwise by the analytic quotient adapter.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_eq_analyticRecovery

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_corrected
items.statement:
Corrected component jets at the canonical base give
    the recovered first-radius derivative, with the squared shape denominator accounted
    for explicitly.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_corrected

items.statement:
Component derivative data at `(S 0, G 0) = ((2,1),(1,2))`
    determine the first derivative of the recovered radius, shape, and high-scale factors.  The
    squared denominator in the shape quotient contributes the coefficient `4 * g₁`.
items.title: recoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_correctedComponentJets
items.statement:
Corrected second-factor component jets determine the
    recovery derivative with radius coefficient `b * (6 * J + 5 * P - 276) / 18` and
    shape coefficient `b * (6 * J - P + 300) / 9`.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_correctedComponentJets

items.label: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets
items.statement:
First-radius jets of the second spectral and gradient
factor pairs transport to the derivative of the recovered factor triple.
items.title: independentRadiusRecoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets

items.label: independentRadiusNormalForm_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets
items.statement:
The same component jets give the first-radius jet of
the full independent-radius normal form, with unit derivative in its first coordinate.
items.title: independentRadiusNormalForm_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets

items.label: independentRadiusNormalForm_eq_map_of_raw_transport
items.statement:
Once the independent normal form is identified with
the raw two-leg evaluator, the public-map equality follows from the nonzero-radius raw
map bridge.
items.title: independentRadiusNormalForm_eq_map_of_raw_transport

items.label: mem_parameterSet
items.statement:
Membership in the mixed parameter set separates into the control interval and
the coefficient ball.
items.title: mem_parameterSet

items.label: input_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the mixed canonical input.
items.title: input_apply

items.label: map_zero
items.statement: The removable mixed map fixes the canonical base state for every control scale.
items.title: map_zero

items.label: map_fixedScale
items.statement:
Away from zero signed scale and near the canonical base state, specializing the
independent radius to `ε ^ 2` agrees with the square of the signed-scale coordinate
of `DFP.TwoLeg.stateMap`.
items.title: map_fixedScale

items.label: mem_parameterSet_iff
items.statement: Membership in the mixed parameter set is componentwise membership in its two factors.
items.title: mem_parameterSet_iff

items.label: input_eq
items.statement: The canonical mixed input evaluates to its three explicit coordinates.
items.title: input_eq

items.label: map_base
items.statement: The removable mixed map sends zero radius to the canonical base state.
items.title: map_base

items.label: observableMap_projectionData_eq_fields
items.statement: The projection tuple is exactly the corresponding fields of `observableMap`.
items.title: observableMap_projectionData_eq_fields

items.label: observableMap_fixedScale
items.statement:
Away from zero signed scale and near the canonical base state, specializing
the independent radius to the squared scale recovers the fixed-scale complete
observable evaluator.
items.title: observableMap_fixedScale

items.label: firstLegGradientNormDrop
items.statement:
Along any real coordinate path with the polynomial slow-graph shape jet, the normalized
first-leg decrease of the gradient norm is asymptotic to `2 * ε ^ 3` from the right.
items.title: firstLegGradientNormDrop

items.label: secondLegGradientNormRise
items.statement:
Along any real coordinate path with the polynomial slow-graph shape and high-eigenvalue
jets, the normalized second-leg increase of the gradient norm is asymptotic to `2 * ε ^ 3`
from the right.
items.title: secondLegGradientNormRise

items.label: eventuallyStrictGradientNormValley
items.statement:
Along any real coordinate path with the polynomial slow-graph coordinate jets, every
sufficiently small positive point has a strict gradient-norm valley, also after scaling all
three norms by any positive amplitude.
items.title: eventuallyStrictGradientNormValley

items.label: isBigO_norm_sub_of_sq_norm_sub
items.statement:
A lower bound on the sum of two norms turns a squared-norm remainder into a norm
remainder with the reciprocal lower-bound constant.
items.title: isBigO_norm_sub_of_sq_norm_sub

items.label: FiniteTaylorJet.IsUniformOn.postcompContinuousLinearMap
items.statement:
Continuous-linear postcomposition transports a uniform finite-jet family, including
its coefficient bounds and every-positive-coefficient Peano remainders.
items.title: FiniteTaylorJet.IsUniformOn.postcompContinuousLinearMap

items.label: coordinates_apply

branch-selection margins.

items.statement: Positivity of every branch-selection margin supplies all canonical branch conditions.
items.title: branchConditions_of_branchFactors_pos

items.statement: Each branch-selection margin is continuous at the common zero-scale base state.
items.title: branchFactors_continuousAt

items.label: branchFactors_base
items.statement:

zero-scale base state.
items.title: branchFactors_base

items.label: domainFactors_state
items.statement: The first thirteen common-domain factors are the factored-state margins.

items.label: domainFactors_branch
items.statement: The final five common-domain factors are the canonical branch-selection margins.
items.title: domainFactors_branch

items.label: domainFactors_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the ordered vector of eighteen factored-state and branch margins.
items.title: domainFactors_apply

items.label: contDiffAt_coordinatesAlongGraphJetPath
items.statement:
The complete observable coordinate family along the graph path is jointly
`C^9` at every point of the zero-scale coefficient fiber.
items.title: contDiffAt_coordinatesAlongGraphJetPath

items.label: branchFactorsCommonDomain
items.statement:
On a bounded closed coefficient ball, the five branch-selection margins have
one positive lower bound throughout one common zero-scale neighborhood.
items.title: branchFactorsCommonDomain
